# Business Constraints Specification
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-BC-001 |
| **Document Title** | Business Constraints — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Senior Business Analyst |
| **Source Documents** | BRD-IMS-001 (Section 18), Business Constraints Discovery Artifact |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business and operational constraints only — not technical architecture, infrastructure, or implementation design |

### Purpose

This document identifies the **38 business constraints** that bound how the Inventory Management System initiative may be delivered and operated. Constraints are fixed business conditions — not optional preferences. Each constraint is expressed in operational terms: what the organization can and cannot do while running inventory management as a business capability.

### Constraint Categories

| Prefix | Category | Count |
|--------|----------|-------|
| BC | Budget | 6 |
| TC | Time | 6 |
| LC | Legal | 5 |
| OC | Operational | 8 |
| ORC | Organizational | 7 |
| TEC | Technology — Business Level | 6 |

### Severity Classification

| Severity | Constraints |
|----------|-------------|
| **Blocking** | BC-01, TC-02, OC-01, ORC-07 |
| **High** | BC-02, BC-05, TC-01, TC-03, TC-04, ORC-01, ORC-03, ORC-05, TEC-01, TEC-04 |
| **Medium** | BC-03, BC-04, BC-06, TC-05, TC-06, LC-01, LC-02, LC-03, OC-02, OC-04, OC-07, OC-08, ORC-02, ORC-04, ORC-06, TEC-02, TEC-05, TEC-06 |
| **Low** | LC-04, LC-05, OC-03, OC-05, OC-06 |

---

## 1. Budget Constraints

### BC-01: Fixed Total Initiative Budget

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | BC-01 |
| **Description** | The IMS initiative must be delivered within a fixed total budget approved by executive leadership, covering software, services, training, change management, and first-year operational support. No additional funding is guaranteed if overruns occur. |
| **Business Justification** | Inventory improvement must demonstrate return within approved capital and operating investment limits. Executive leadership has committed a defined envelope tied to business case ROI — not an open-ended transformation program. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | All processes (BP-01 – BP-32); particularly BP-29 (Performance Reporting), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness), and Phase 2/3 processes deferred by scope prioritization |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Scope reduction or project pause; P1 objectives (BO-01, BO-03, BO-19) at risk; Phase 2/3 capabilities (replenishment automation, financial alignment, network rebalancing) indefinitely deferred; stakeholder trust in program governance erodes |

---

### BC-02: No Additional Warehouse Headcount Budget

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | BC-02 |
| **Description** | The business case does not include budget for additional warehouse or inventory control headcount in the first 12 months. Efficiency must come from improved processes and system support, not new hires. |
| **Business Justification** | The initiative is funded as a productivity and control investment, not a staffing expansion. Leadership expects existing teams to operate more effectively with better visibility and standardized workflows. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-09 (Put-Away), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-21 (Low-Stock Alert Review), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Unfunded headcount creates budget overrun (BC-01 conflict); existing staff overwhelmed during rollout; adoption fails (BO-21); manual parallel tools persist (BO-22); accuracy and movement recording objectives (BO-02, BO-03) not sustained |

---

### BC-03: Capital Expenditure vs. Operating Expenditure Limits

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | BC-03 |
| **Description** | Finance has defined separate caps for capital expenditure (licenses, implementation) and operating expenditure (subscriptions, support, training). Spending cannot be reclassified between categories without CFO approval. |
| **Business Justification** | Corporate financial policy requires predictable classification of investment versus recurring cost for balance-sheet and budget planning. IMS spending must fit established fiscal governance. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-22 (Replenishment Planning), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation) — indirect; primarily affects procurement timing of delivery activities |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Delivery delayed to next fiscal period; training or go-live support deferred; misaligned spend blocks vendor payment; project timeline slips against TC-02 and TC-05 milestones |

---

### BC-04: Training and Change Management Budget Ceiling

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | BC-04 |
| **Description** | A fixed budget is allocated for training, communications, and change management. This budget cannot be reallocated from development or licensing budgets. |
| **Business Justification** | Change investment is necessary but bounded. Leadership requires demonstrable efficiency in rollout — scalable training models rather than unlimited per-location bespoke programs. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | All operational processes at rollout; especially BP-07, BP-11, BP-14, BP-18, BP-24 where floor adoption is critical |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Incomplete role training; location managers reject standardized processes (BO-03); user adoption below 90% (BO-21); parallel spreadsheets and paper logs continue (BO-22); rework and support costs increase without budget to absorb them |

---

### BC-05: No Budget for External System Replacement

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | BC-05 |
| **Description** | The IMS budget does not fund replacement of finance, sales, HR, or ERP systems. IMS must operate within the current enterprise application landscape. |
| **Business Justification** | IMS addresses inventory control as a targeted capability gap — not a full enterprise platform replacement. Finance, sales, and HR systems remain authoritative in their domains. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-16 (Order Availability), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Scope creep into ERP/CRM territory; stakeholder resistance from system owners; delivery failure on inventory-specific objectives; duplicated master data across systems; BO-18 and BO-20 remain unachievable without agreed interim reconciliation |

---

### BC-06: Ongoing Operational Cost Limit

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | BC-06 |
| **Description** | Annual recurring cost for licenses, support, and maintenance after go-live must remain within a CFO-approved operating budget threshold, typically capped relative to current inventory carrying cost. |
| **Business Justification** | Sustainable inventory management must not impose recurring cost that exceeds the economic value of improved control. Ongoing spend must be defensible against working-capital and carrying-cost benefits. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-02 (Location Setup) — future location onboarding; BP-29 (Performance Reporting) — executive visibility scope |
| **Consequences if Violated** | New locations cannot be onboarded without separate approval; feature tiers or user counts restricted; network-wide rollout (TC-03) stalls; long-term scalability of BO-01 and BO-14 constrained |

---

## 2. Time Constraints

### TC-01: 18-Month Business Vision Horizon

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TC-01 |
| **Description** | All SMART business objectives and phased outcomes must be achievable within 18 months of project initiation, aligned with the short-term business vision. |
| **Business Justification** | Leadership committed to measurable inventory improvement within a defined planning horizon. Beyond 18 months, priorities may shift and funding is not assured. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | All processes; Phase 3 processes especially BP-26 (Network Rebalancing), BP-29 (KPI Reporting), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Objectives BO-09, BO-10, BO-18, BO-20, BO-23, BO-24 measured as failed despite incomplete delivery; steering committee loses confidence; initiative descoped or restarted |

---

### TC-02: MVP Delivery Within 6 Months

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TC-02 |
| **Description** | Minimum Viable Product must be live at the first primary location within 6 months of project kickoff to meet Phase 1 vision and P1 SMART objectives. |
| **Business Justification** | Early credible control is the strategic intent of Phase 1. Delayed go-live prolongs stockouts, inaccurate records, and fulfillment failures that the initiative was created to resolve. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-01 – BP-18, BP-24 – BP-25, BP-29 (core reports), BP-32 (audit trail) — MVP process set |
| **Consequences if Violated** | P1 objectives missed: trusted view (BO-01), movement recording (BO-03), audit trail (BO-19), sales self-service (BO-16), adoption (BO-21), manual tool retirement (BO-22); executive sponsorship weakens; business continues absorbing current-state losses |

---

### TC-03: Sequential Location Rollout Window

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TC-03 |
| **Description** | Primary locations must be onboarded sequentially over approximately 6 months following first go-live, with a minimum 4-week gap between deployments — not simultaneous network-wide cutover. |
| **Business Justification** | Support capacity, change absorption, and lessons-learned application require controlled rollout. Simultaneous deployment would overwhelm operations and SMEs (ORC-01). |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-02 (Location Setup), BP-10 (Status Monitoring), BP-24 – BP-26 (Network Balance), BP-29 (Reporting) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Inconsistent processes across locations persist (BO-03); network visibility incomplete until ~month 12 (BO-01); cross-location imbalance correction delayed (BO-14); hypercare support fails; accuracy and adoption vary by site |

---

### TC-04: Peak Season Blackout Periods

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TC-04 |
| **Description** | Go-live, major upgrades, and intensive training cannot occur during defined peak business periods (e.g., holiday season, fiscal year-end, major promotional events) at each location. |
| **Business Justification** | Peak periods generate disproportionate revenue and customer commitments. Operational disruption during peak directly damages fill rate, on-time delivery, and brand reputation. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-16 – BP-19 (Order Fulfillment), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-31 (Promotional Readiness), BP-07 (Receiving) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Fill rate and on-time delivery drop (BO-05, BO-15); stock-related cancellations increase (BO-08); customer complaints and revenue at risk; rollout calendar slips 3–6 months; staff cannot complete training before peak |

---

### TC-05: SMART Objective Measurement Deadlines

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TC-05 |
| **Description** | Business objectives have fixed measurement milestones at months 3, 6, 9, 12, and 18 post-initiation. Enabling capabilities must be live before their measurement window opens. |
| **Business Justification** | Accountability to the business case requires time-bound outcomes. Objectives without aligned delivery dates cannot be governed or rewarded. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | Process-to-objective mapping: BP-10/16 (BO-01, BO-16); BP-11/13 (BO-02); BP-07/18/25 (BO-03); BP-18/19 (BO-05, BO-08); BP-21/22 (BO-07, BO-13); BP-30 (BO-18, BO-20) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | False "red" KPI status when capability not yet delivered; premature descoping of objectives; steering committee makes decisions on misleading data; team morale and sponsor confidence decline |

---

### TC-06: Baseline Measurement Lead Time

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TC-06 |
| **Description** | Pre-implementation baseline data for SMART objectives must be collected 30–60 days before first go-live, consuming part of the overall project timeline. |
| **Business Justification** | Improvement claims require credible before-and-after comparison. Without baseline, ROI and objective achievement cannot be substantiated to leadership or auditors. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-29 (Performance Reporting), BP-11/12/13 (Accuracy), BP-18/19 (Fulfillment), BP-15 (Shrinkage) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | BO-04, BO-06, BO-07, BO-09, BO-11 targets unprovable; steering committee cannot validate success; external audit challenges benefit claims; late baseline compresses build and test window (conflicts with TC-02) |

---

## 3. Legal Constraints

### LC-01: Data Protection and Privacy Regulations

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | LC-01 |
| **Description** | The business must comply with applicable data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, local privacy regulations) for personal data in user accounts, audit logs, and customer-linked order and return records. |
| **Business Justification** | Legal obligation to protect employee and customer personal data. Non-compliance exposes the organization to regulatory penalties, legal action, and reputational harm. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-16 – BP-19 (customer-linked fulfillment), BP-27 – BP-28 (Returns), BP-32 (Audit & Control Review) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Regulatory fines and enforcement actions; required data deletion or access restrictions disrupt audit trail (BO-19); customer data breaches damage trust; legal hold on system use pending remediation |

---

### LC-02: Financial Record Retention Requirements

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | LC-02 |
| **Description** | Inventory transaction records, adjustment logs, valuation substantiation, and audit evidence must be retained for the minimum period required by tax and corporate law — typically 5–7 years. |
| **Business Justification** | Statutory and audit requirements mandate preservation of financial and inventory substantiation records. Early destruction invalidates audit defense and tax compliance. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-14 (Adjustments & Write-Offs), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-32 (Audit & Control Review), BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-25 (Transfer Execution) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Audit findings and qualified opinions; inability to defend inventory valuations in tax review; regulatory penalties; BO-19 (audit trail) and BO-18 (valuation alignment) fail at external audit |

---

### LC-03: Employment and Labor Law

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | LC-03 |
| **Description** | Changes to work procedures, performance measurement, and mandatory transaction recording introduced by IMS must comply with employment contracts, collective bargaining agreements, and labor regulations. |
| **Business Justification** | Workforce practices are legally governed. Unilateral imposition of new performance or recording requirements without proper consultation creates labor relations and legal risk. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-07, BP-09, BP-11, BP-18 (floor work procedures); BP-32 (accountability policies) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Union grievances or work stoppages at affected locations; rollback of mandatory recording policies (BO-03, BO-22 fail); go-live delay at unionized sites; HR and legal remediation costs |

---

### LC-04: Supplier and Commercial Contract Terms

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | LC-04 |
| **Description** | Purchase order formats, delivery documentation, and receipt dispute processes must remain compatible with existing supplier contracts. Suppliers cannot be required to adopt new processes without contract amendment. |
| **Business Justification** | Supplier relationships are contractually bound. Receiving and procurement workflows must work with current commercial terms — the IMS initiative does not renegotiate the supplier base. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-08 (Receipt Discrepancy Resolution) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Supplier refusal to deliver or document shipments; receipt disputes unresolvable; inbound supply disruption; emergency procurement increases (BO-12); BR-006 and BR-007 controls weakened |

---

### LC-05: Consumer Protection and Trade Regulations

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | LC-05 |
| **Description** | Customer-facing availability and delivery commitments based on IMS data must comply with consumer protection laws on accurate product representation, cancellation rights, and delivery obligations. |
| **Business Justification** | B2B and B2C customers have legal protections against misleading availability and unfair commercial practices. ATP-based commitments must be defensible. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-16 (Order Availability Confirmation), BP-19 (Partial Fulfillment & Backorder), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Customer complaints to regulators; chargebacks and compensation claims; contractual penalties with B2B customers; reputational damage; BO-08 (cancellations) and BO-15 (on-time delivery) worsen |

---

## 4. Operational Constraints

### OC-01: No Operational Shutdown for Go-Live

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-01 |
| **Description** | Warehouses and stores must continue receiving, fulfilling, and shipping orders during and after go-live. No full operational shutdown is permitted for system transition. |
| **Business Justification** | Customer commitments and revenue depend on continuous fulfillment. A shutdown-based cutover is commercially unacceptable for a distribution and retail operator. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-07 (Receiving), BP-17 – BP-18 (Reservation & Fulfillment), BP-24 – BP-25 (Transfers), BP-10 (Status Monitoring) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Lost sales and customer cancellations; carrier and supplier penalties; emergency manual fulfillment at higher cost; opening balance errors from rushed cutover (BO-02); rollback required with extended dual-system operation |

---

### OC-02: Daily Fulfillment Service Levels Must Be Maintained

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-02 |
| **Description** | Agreed customer fulfillment service levels (fill rate, dispatch timeliness) must not materially degrade during implementation and rollout. |
| **Business Justification** | Customer contracts and brand promise depend on reliable fulfillment. The IMS program must improve control without becoming a cause of service failure. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-16 – BP-20 (Order Fulfillment), BP-17 (Reservation), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | BO-05 (fill rate), BO-06 (cycle time), BO-15 (on-time delivery) regress; NPS on fulfillment drops (KPI-27); B2B penalties; steering committee halts rollout; revert to manual processes |

---

### OC-03: Physical Warehouse Layout and Storage Are Fixed

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-03 |
| **Description** | Warehouse layouts, racking, and storage zones will not be restructured as part of the IMS initiative. Physical infrastructure remains as-is. |
| **Business Justification** | Facility investment is outside IMS funding and timeline. Accuracy and efficiency gains must come from process discipline and visibility, not capital warehouse redesign. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-09 (Put-Away), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-11 (Cycle Counting) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Unfunded facility projects distract from IMS; bin-level optimization deferred; pick path inefficiency persists; accuracy improvements slower than planned (BO-02) if layout is root cause |

---

### OC-04: Existing Product Portfolio and SKU Count

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-04 |
| **Description** | IMS must accommodate the current active product catalog and projected SKU growth over 18 months without requiring product range reduction. |
| **Business Justification** | Commercial strategy continues to expand assortment and channels. Inventory control must scale with the business — not force assortment rationalization as a prerequisite. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-01 (Product Master), BP-03 (Stock Policy), BP-04 (ABC Classification), BP-10 (Status Monitoring) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Forced SKU reduction damages sales; catalog cutover errors; threshold and alert programs unmanageable; BO-07 (priority stockouts) on excluded products; data migration failure at go-live |

---

### OC-05: Current Supplier and Carrier Relationships

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-05 |
| **Description** | Inbound and outbound logistics continue through existing approved suppliers and carriers. The IMS project does not include supplier renegotiation or carrier replacement. |
| **Business Justification** | Supply chain partnerships are long-term commercial relationships. Receiving and shipping workflows must align with current partner capabilities and lead times. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-05 – BP-09 (Inbound), BP-18 (Shipment Handoff), BP-23 (Inbound Supply Tracking) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Unplanned partner changes disrupt supply; receiving documentation mismatch; inbound delays invalidate replenishment thresholds (BO-13); carrier tracking gaps persist |

---

### OC-06: Returns Volume Within Manual Handling Capacity

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-06 |
| **Description** | Customer returns volume is expected to remain processable through basic return workflows without a dedicated returns operation for the first 12 months. If volume exceeds ~5% of outbound, scope review is required. |
| **Business Justification** | Returns handling capacity is sized for current business volume. Full reverse-logistics maturity is Phase 2 — not day-one operational capacity. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-27 (Customer Return Intake), BP-28 (Return-to-Stock or Disposal) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Returns backlog; incorrect restock or write-off; customer refund delays; warehouse floor congestion; BO-11 (shrinkage) worsens from mishandled returns; scope exception and unfunded work required |

---

### OC-07: Cycle Counting Without Operational Disruption

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-07 |
| **Description** | Physical inventory verification required for accuracy objectives must be performed without shutting down receiving, picking, or shipping at any location. |
| **Business Justification** | Continuous operations are non-negotiable (OC-01, OC-02). Accuracy programs must use rolling cycle counts — not full shutdowns — except scheduled full counts planned outside peak. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-12 (Full Physical Count), BP-13 (Variance Investigation) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Forced shutdown conflicts with OC-01; accuracy targets delayed (BO-02); count variances increase from concurrent movements; local managers refuse count program (ORC-05); audit substantiation weak |

---

### OC-08: Multi-Location Network with Existing Transfer Practices

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | OC-08 |
| **Description** | Inter-location transfers follow existing approval practices and freight arrangements. The project does not introduce new logistics infrastructure or transfer service level agreements. |
| **Business Justification** | Network redistribution depends on current freight capacity and approval culture. IMS standardizes recording — not physical logistics network redesign. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-24 (Transfer Request), BP-25 (Transfer Execution), BP-26 (Network Rebalancing) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Unfunded logistics investment expected; transfer SLAs assumed but not met; BO-14 (imbalance reduction) delayed; emergency transfers continue outside system; source locations stockout from uncontrolled transfers (BR-012 risk) |

---

## 5. Organizational Constraints

### ORC-01: No Dedicated Full-Time Project Team

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | ORC-01 |
| **Description** | The project relies on part-time contribution from business SMEs (~20% allocation). No dedicated full-time business operations lead is assigned exclusively to the initiative. |
| **Business Justification** | Operational leaders must continue running daily business. The organization cannot spare full-time inventory SMEs without compromising fulfillment and replenishment. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | All processes requiring SME definition: BP-01, BP-03, BP-07, BP-11, BP-14, BP-21, BP-32 |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Slow decisions delay TC-02; UAT incomplete; policies undefined at go-live; floor users adopt workarounds; requirements errors discovered post-go-live; accuracy and adoption objectives fail |

---

### ORC-02: Single Product Owner Authority

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | ORC-02 |
| **Description** | Product prioritization is centralized under one Product Owner with steering committee oversight. Department heads cannot unilaterally add scope for their function. |
| **Business Justification** | Twenty-nine stakeholder groups create conflicting demands. Central prioritization protects MVP delivery and budget (BC-01) against local optimization. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | Scope affects all processes; escalations common for BP-05, BP-31, BP-26, BP-30 when deferred |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Scope creep breaches BC-01; MVP date missed (TC-02); fragmented product with inconsistent workflows (BO-03); steering committee loses governance confidence |

---

### ORC-03: Change Resistance in Warehouse Culture

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | ORC-03 |
| **Description** | Warehouse teams rely on informal practices — spreadsheets, paper logs, tribal knowledge — and history shows resistance to mandated system use without management enforcement. |
| **Business Justification** | Cultural inertia is a known organizational reality, not a failure of intent. Adoption requires enforcement policy, not only training and tooling. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-07, BP-09, BP-11, BP-14, BP-18, BP-25 — all floor-recording processes |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Dual systems persist (BO-22 fails); movement recording below 98% (BO-03); accuracy stays at ~78% (BO-02); audit trail incomplete (BO-19); pilot failure poisons network rollout (TC-03) |

---

### ORC-04: Limited Internal IT Business Support Capacity

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | ORC-04 |
| **Description** | Internal technology support has limited capacity for business process design support, bulk user provisioning, and post-go-live business hypercare. Primary IT focus remains existing enterprise systems. |
| **Business Justification** | IT resources are committed to maintaining current finance, sales, and infrastructure systems. IMS operational support must be business-led at go-live. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-32 (user access and audit); rollout of all transactional processes |
| **Consequences if Violated** | User provisioning delays location go-live; access errors block floor operations; post-go-live issues unresolved; business hypercare unfunded; adoption stalls (BO-21) |

---

### ORC-05: Decentralized Location Management Structure

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | ORC-05 |
| **Description** | Each warehouse and store is managed locally with operational autonomy. Central mandates require regional or executive endorsement for enforcement. |
| **Business Justification** | The operating model delegates day-to-day accountability to site managers. Network standardization is a cultural and governance challenge — not automatic with system deployment. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-02 (Location Setup), BP-03 (Stock Policy), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-24 (Transfers), BP-29 (Location Performance) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Location-to-location process variation continues (BO-03); network KPIs not comparable; some sites never adopt; BO-14 (imbalance) uncorrected; executive dashboard misleading (BO-01) |

---

### ORC-06: Finance and Operations Reporting Alignment Gap

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | ORC-06 |
| **Description** | Finance and operations use different data sources and reconciliation practices for inventory. No established single reconciliation process exists between operational and financial records. |
| **Business Justification** | Historical organizational silos separated operational stock records from general ledger inventory. IMS alone cannot create alignment — cross-department process must be designed. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-14 (Adjustments & Write-Offs), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation), BP-29 (Reporting) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | BO-18 (valuation variance ≤2%) unachievable; month-end close remains 7+ days (BO-20); finance distrusts operational data; manual reconciliation continues (BO-04 fails); audit findings on inventory substantiation |

---

### ORC-07: No Formal Inventory Management Function Today

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | ORC-07 |
| **Description** | The business lacks a mature, centralized inventory management function with defined policies, KPIs, and single-point accountability. Control is distributed across warehouse, purchasing, and finance. |
| **Business Justification** | Growth outpaced governance design. The initiative assumes creation of Inventory Controller accountability — a structural gap that must be closed for sustained control. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-01, BP-03, BP-04, BP-11, BP-13, BP-15, BP-21, BP-32 — all governance-heavy processes |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Policies unwritten and unenforced; no owner for accuracy program (BO-02); replenishment remains reactive (BO-13); shrinkage unanalyzed (BO-11); project delivers software without organizational capability; chronic inaccuracy persists |

---

## 6. Technology Constraints — Business Level

*Expressed as business operating boundaries, not technical implementation limits.*

### TEC-01: Must Coexist With Existing Enterprise Systems

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TEC-01 |
| **Description** | IMS operates alongside existing finance, sales, and HR systems without replacing them. Users continue working across multiple systems daily. |
| **Business Justification** | Enterprise systems remain authoritative in their domains per BC-05. IMS is the inventory system of record — not the enterprise platform of record. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-05 (PO with finance), BP-16 (orders from sales systems), BP-30 (valuation to finance), BP-27 (returns with CS systems) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Stakeholder conflict and duplicate data entry; users revert to legacy tools; BO-16 limited to IMS-native workflows; finance alignment delayed (BO-18); initiative perceived as failed ERP attempt |

---

### TEC-02: No Budget for Dedicated Warehouse Hardware

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TEC-02 |
| **Description** | The business will not purchase dedicated warehouse hardware (rugged scanners, handhelds, label printers) as part of IMS. Users access the system via existing company computers and devices. |
| **Business Justification** | Hardware investment is a separate capital decision. IMS rollout must be achievable with assets already deployed at sites. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-07 (Receiving), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Unbudgeted capex request (BC-03 conflict); floor process slower than planned (BO-06); barcode benefits limited; users skip scanning steps; receipt and pick errors persist (BO-02, BO-05) |

---

### TEC-03: Standard Web Browser Access Required

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TEC-03 |
| **Description** | All users must access IMS through a standard web browser on company-approved devices without installing specialized desktop applications. |
| **Business Justification** | Corporate IT standardizes on browser-based applications for supportability and security. Proprietary client software is not approved for this initiative. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | All user-facing processes; floor operations at BP-07, BP-11, BP-18 most affected |
| **Consequences if Violated** | IT blocks deployment; locations without reliable connectivity cannot operate (floor downtime); adoption limited to office roles; warehouse recording compliance drops (BO-03) |

---

### TEC-04: No Real-Time External Channel Integration in MVP

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TEC-04 |
| **Description** | Sales channels (e-commerce, B2B portal, marketplaces) will not receive automated real-time inventory feeds from IMS in the first 12 months. Channel availability updates follow existing manual processes. |
| **Business Justification** | Channel integration requires separate business case and partner agreements. MVP focuses on internal operational truth before external synchronization. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-10 (Status Monitoring), BP-16 (Availability Confirmation) — external channel context |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Unplanned integration work breaches BC-01 and TC-02; channel overselling continues (BO-08); marketplace penalties; BO-16 applies only to internal sales — external channels remain inaccurate |

---

### TEC-05: Manual Data Exchange With Finance System

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TEC-05 |
| **Description** | Inventory valuation and movement data transfer to finance through scheduled export or manual reconciliation in the first 12 months — not automated general ledger posting. |
| **Business Justification** | Finance system integration is out of IMS scope (BC-05). Interim operating model must close books using agreed manual reconciliation until Phase 3 automation. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-14 (Adjustments & Write-Offs), BP-30 (Financial Reconciliation) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Finance team unprepared for new data volume; month-end delays continue (BO-20); valuation variance stays at ~8% (BO-18); duplicate or lost adjustments; audit trail gaps if exports not archived (LC-02) |

---

### TEC-06: User Access Limited to Company Network and Approved Devices

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Constraint ID** | TEC-06 |
| **Description** | Access to inventory data — stock levels, valuation, movement history — is restricted to company-managed devices and approved network access per corporate security policy. |
| **Business Justification** | Inventory data is commercially and financially sensitive. Corporate security policy prohibits unmanaged device access to operational and valuation information. |
| **Affected Business Processes** | BP-10 (Visibility), BP-16 (Sales Availability), BP-29/30 (Management & Finance Reporting) |
| **Consequences if Violated** | Security policy breach; data leakage of stock positions or valuation; remote sales and regional managers cannot access ATP without VPN; workaround spreadsheets reappear (BO-22); regulatory exposure (LC-01) |

---

## Constraint Interaction Summary

Constraints frequently compound. The following interactions have amplified operational impact:

| Interaction | Constraints | Operational Consequence if Ignored |
|-------------|-------------|-----------------------------------|
| Budget + Time | BC-01 + TC-02 | MVP scope inflation causes missed go-live and unfunded overrun |
| Budget + Organization | BC-02 + ORC-01 | Same staff run daily ops and project — burnout and adoption failure |
| Operational + Time | OC-01 + TC-04 | Narrow rollout windows; missed blackout = delayed network benefits 6+ months |
| Organization + Technology | ORC-03 + TEC-01 | Resistant users juggle IMS plus legacy systems without integration |
| Legal + Operations | LC-02 + TEC-05 | Manual finance exports must still meet 5–7 year retention |
| Operational + Organization | OC-07 + ORC-05 | Rolling counts need local manager cooperation at every decentralized site |
| Governance gap + Time | ORC-07 + TC-02 | Go-live without Inventory Controller — policies undefined, accuracy fails |

# Business Exception Scenarios Specification
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-EX-001 |
| **Document Title** | Business Exception Scenarios — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Senior Business Analyst |
| **Source Documents** | BRD-IMS-001, Business Events Catalog (BE-01–BE-59), Business Workflows (WF-01–WF-32), Common Inventory Management Scenarios, Business Rules (BR-001–BR-032) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business exception behavior only — not technical error handling, system faults, or implementation recovery |

### Purpose

This document identifies **exception scenarios** — situations that deviate from the standard happy-path inventory process and require defined business judgment, escalation, and response. Exceptions are normal operational events, not system failures. Each scenario describes what the business should do when the exception occurs.

### How to Read Each Exception

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Exception ID** | Unique identifier (EX-001, EX-002, …) |
| **Business Scenario** | What is happening from a business perspective |
| **Trigger** | Event or condition that causes the exception |
| **Expected Business Response** | What the organization should do — policies and actions |
| **Responsible Actor** | Primary role accountable for resolution |
| **Business Impact** | Consequences if not handled correctly |

### Related Business Event Reference

Where applicable, exceptions map to the Business Events Catalog (BE-xx) and Business Processes (BP-xx).

---

## Domain 1: Master Data & Governance Exceptions

### EX-001 — Duplicate Product Identity Detected

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-001 |
| **Business Scenario** | A new product submission matches or closely resembles an existing SKU, barcode, or product name, risking parallel product identities for the same physical item. |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller or stakeholder attempts to create or update a product record (BE-02, BE-01). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Halt new record creation; compare existing and proposed records side by side; merge or correct the existing record rather than create a duplicate; document justification if a genuinely new SKU is confirmed. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Fragmented stock records; inaccurate ATP; duplicate purchasing; reconciliation effort; unreliable network visibility |

---

### EX-002 — Discontinued Product With Open Activity

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-002 |
| **Business Scenario** | A product marked for discontinuation still has open purchase orders, active reservations, or remaining on-hand stock requiring disposition. |
| **Trigger** | Product discontinuation requested (BE-03). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Block new replenishment per BR-027; warn stakeholders of dependent open POs and reservations; define runout timeline for remaining stock; cancel or amend open POs; fulfill or release existing reservations per policy; plan clearance or write-off for residual quantity. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller (with Purchasing Manager and Operations Director) |
| **Business Impact** | Obsolete inventory accumulation; customer orders for withdrawn products; trapped working capital; conflicting assortment decisions |

---

### EX-003 — Location Closure With Remaining Stock

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-003 |
| **Business Scenario** | A warehouse or store approved for closure still holds on-hand inventory that must be dispositioned before deactivation. |
| **Trigger** | Inventory location change approved for closure (BE-04). |
| **Expected Business Response** | List all remaining stock; execute disposition plan (transfer out, sell-through, write-off); block new inbound and fulfillment except authorized disposition; obtain Operations Director sign-off before location deactivation. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Stranded inventory; orphaned records; financial misstatement; lost asset value |

---

### EX-004 — Opening Balance Dispute at Go-Live

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-004 |
| **Business Scenario** | Physical opening count results for a new or cutover location are challenged by local management or finance before location activation. |
| **Trigger** | Opening stock balance submitted for approval (BP-02, BP-12). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Suspend location activation; conduct recount or independent verification for disputed SKUs; resolve catalog gaps for unknown products; require authorized approver sign-off on final baseline before operational transactions begin. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Go-live with embedded errors; chronic inaccuracy from day one; distrust in system data; cascading fulfillment failures |

---

## Domain 2: Inbound & Procurement Exceptions

### EX-005 — Supplier Short-Shipment

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-005 |
| **Business Scenario** | Supplier delivers fewer units than ordered on a purchase order, especially for a product already low or committed to customer orders. |
| **Trigger** | Receipt verification finds quantity below PO expected quantity (BE-15). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Record only verified received quantity; document short-shipment discrepancy; exclude disputed quantity from sellable stock; escalate with supplier for balance; recalculate ATP and customer commitments; hold payment pending three-way match resolution per BR-008. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk (document) → Purchasing Manager (supplier resolution) |
| **Business Impact** | Phantom inventory if PO quantity accepted silently; stockouts on committed orders; supplier accountability lost; payment for undelivered goods |

---

### EX-006 — Damaged Goods at Receiving

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-006 |
| **Business Scenario** | Inbound shipment arrives with visible damage — crushed cartons, broken units, or temperature excursion — making some or all units unsellable. |
| **Trigger** | Receiving clerk inspects packaging and product condition (BE-14, BE-15). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Segregate damaged goods; accept only sellable units into inventory; photograph and document damage; initiate supplier or carrier claim; quarantine damaged quantity; exclude damaged stock from ATP per BR-013. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk → Warehouse Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Defective goods sold to customers; returns and brand damage; unrecoverable supplier claims without dock evidence; inflated on-hand balances |

---

### EX-007 — Wrong Item Received Against Purchase Order

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-007 |
| **Business Scenario** | Physical product delivered does not match the purchase order line — different SKU, variant, or entirely wrong merchandise. |
| **Trigger** | Product identity verification fails during goods receipt (BE-15). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Reject mismatched product from inventory acceptance; document wrong-item discrepancy; notify purchasing and supplier; accept only correct items if partial shipment; do not record wrong SKU as on-hand. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk → Buyer |
| **Business Impact** | Inventory records show stock that cannot be fulfilled; customer orders fail at pick; supplier dispute without documentation; payment for wrong goods |

---

### EX-008 — Receipt Without Valid Purchase Order

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-008 |
| **Business Scenario** | Supplier truck arrives with no matching open purchase order, or emergency delivery requires receipt outside standard procurement. |
| **Trigger** | Receiving initiated without PO reference (BE-14). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Hold shipment until purchasing confirms valid PO or grants authorized ad-hoc exception with documented approver and reason per BR-007; record exception for audit; do not accept standard supplier receipt without authorization. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk → Purchasing Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Unauthorized spending; maverick buying; three-way match failure; audit control weakness |

---

### EX-009 — Over-Shipment Beyond Tolerance

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-009 |
| **Business Scenario** | Supplier delivers more units than ordered beyond the business-defined receipt tolerance. |
| **Trigger** | Received quantity exceeds PO open quantity plus tolerance (BE-15). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Flag over-receipt; require Warehouse Manager or Purchasing Manager approval before acceptance; document decision to accept excess, return excess, or create supplemental PO; adjust payment only for accepted quantity. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk → Warehouse Manager / Purchasing Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Unplanned inventory investment; payment for unapproved goods; storage capacity strain; supplier assumes over-shipment is always accepted |

---

### EX-010 — Inbound Delivery Delayed Past Customer Promise

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-010 |
| **Business Scenario** | Purchase order or transfer shipment is delayed past the date already communicated to customers waiting on backorders or scheduled deliveries. |
| **Trigger** | Supplier or carrier reports delay; expected delivery date passes without receipt (BE-39). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Update expected arrival internally; proactively notify affected customers of revised dates; escalate with supplier; evaluate network transfer or alternate supply for critical commitments; reassess backorder queue priorities. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Buyer → Customer Service Representative |
| **Business Impact** | Silent delay destroys customer trust; backorder cancellations; contract penalties; emergency procurement at premium cost |

---

### EX-011 — Supplier Lead Time Extension

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-011 |
| **Business Scenario** | Supplier communicates longer lead times due to capacity, material, or logistics disruption, invalidating current reorder points and safety stock. |
| **Trigger** | Demand or supply condition changed (BE-06); supplier notification during inbound tracking (BE-39). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Recalculate reorder levels and safety stock for affected products; place orders earlier; inform sales of longer delivery windows; evaluate alternate suppliers for critical SKUs; document policy revision effective date. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller → Purchasing Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Preventable stockouts despite alerts; false confidence in replenishment timing; working capital shock if reactive safety stock increase |

---

## Domain 3: Inventory Control & Accuracy Exceptions

### EX-012 — Material Cycle Count Variance

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-012 |
| **Business Scenario** | Cycle count finds physical quantity differs from recorded balance beyond defined tolerance. |
| **Trigger** | Count variance identified after blind count submission (BE-24). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Order recount if needed; investigate root cause before adjustment per BR-022; document investigation notes; route to independent approver per BR-019; apply adjustment with mandatory reason code per BR-020. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Recurring variances if root cause ignored; accuracy metrics meaningless; audit findings; undetected shrinkage or process failure |

---

### EX-013 — Phantom Inventory (Record Shows Stock, Shelf Empty)

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-013 |
| **Business Scenario** | System shows positive available quantity but product cannot be found physically — empty pick location, bare shelf, or customer cannot locate item. |
| **Trigger** | Pick exception reported (BE-33); customer or sales inquiry; verification count flagged (BE-21). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Conduct physical search including overflow and mislabeled locations; if not found, adjust inventory with shrinkage or count correction reason code immediately; correct ATP to prevent further overselling; investigate root cause (theft, misplacement, unrecorded movement). |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Continued overselling; pick failures; customer embarrassment; lost sales despite "in stock" status; eroded data trust |

---

### EX-014 — Unexplained Shrinkage Trend at Location

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-014 |
| **Business Scenario** | A location shows rising shrinkage, write-offs, or negative adjustments exceeding its historical norm and network average without a single large incident. |
| **Trigger** | Significant loss or adjustment event; monthly shrinkage review (BE-26, BE-27). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Analyze trends by SKU, reason code, and shift; conduct process and security review; increase count frequency for affected categories; assign corrective action owner; escalate to Internal Auditor if suspected fraud. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller → Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Escalating unexplained loss; margin erosion; audit material weakness; chronic accuracy failure at location |

---

### EX-015 — Quality Hold on Received Lot

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-015 |
| **Business Scenario** | Inbound lot fails inspection, receives supplier quality alert, or is flagged for investigation before release to sellable stock. |
| **Trigger** | Quality concern at receipt or post-receipt inspection. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Move lot to quarantine; exclude from ATP immediately per BR-013; investigate with supplier; disposition as release, return, rework, or write-off with documented authorization; reassess customer orders depending on quarantined lot. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Shipping defective or non-compliant product; regulatory exposure; customer safety risk; recall scope expansion |

---

### EX-016 — Full Physical Count Material Variance

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-016 |
| **Business Scenario** | Full wall-to-wall count produces location-wide variance exceeding acceptable threshold for financial substantiation. |
| **Trigger** | Full physical count completed (BE-22, BE-23). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Investigate significant line items; escalate to Operations Director and Finance; apply approved adjustments with full documentation; identify systemic causes; agree corrected baseline with finance before close. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller → Operations Director / Finance Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Financial misstatement; audit qualification; delayed month-end close; loss of inventory baseline credibility |

---

## Domain 4: Order Fulfillment Exceptions

### EX-017 — Customer Order Exceeds Available-to-Promise

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-017 |
| **Business Scenario** | Customer order or sales quote requests quantity greater than current ATP at the fulfillment location, including cumulative effect of multiple orders against limited stock. |
| **Trigger** | Customer order or quote received (BE-28); large or strategic order submitted (BE-29). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Confirm only fulfillable quantity against ATP per BR-001; offer partial shipment, backorder with customer acknowledgment per BR-028, alternate location, or revised delivery date; do not confirm full order without documented plan; reserve only accepted quantity per BR-002. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Sales Representative / Customer Service Representative |
| **Business Impact** | Overselling; order cancellations; pick failures; customer complaints; expedited shipping costs; damaged sales credibility |

---

### EX-018 — Pick Failure — Stock Not Found at Location

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-018 |
| **Business Scenario** | Picker cannot locate reserved quantity at the designated storage location despite positive system record. |
| **Trigger** | Pick exception reported during fulfillment (BE-33). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Conduct immediate physical search; if unfound, trigger phantom inventory response (EX-013); re-pick if found elsewhere; initiate partial fulfillment or order line cancellation if unrecoverable; do not ship without verified pick per BR-003. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Picker / Packer → Warehouse Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Shipment delay; wrong inventory record persists; customer promise missed; cascading pick queue disruption |

---

### EX-019 — Damaged Item Discovered During Pick

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-019 |
| **Business Scenario** | Product retrieved for order is damaged, expired, or otherwise unsellable at the pick point. |
| **Trigger** | Picker reports condition exception during pick verification (BE-33). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Quarantine damaged unit; process stock adjustment or write-off with reason code; attempt re-pick from alternate stock if available; substitute only with authorized approval; notify customer service if order affected. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Picker / Packer → Warehouse Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Wrong or damaged goods shipped if ignored; customer return; brand damage; compounding record inaccuracy |

---

### EX-020 — Concurrent Demand for Last Available Units

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-020 |
| **Business Scenario** | Multiple customers, channels, or locations simultaneously require the last available units of a product — total demand exceeds remaining ATP. |
| **Trigger** | Multiple simultaneous availability confirmations or reservations against depleting ATP (BE-28, BE-30). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Apply documented allocation priority rules (contract obligation, customer tier, order date, channel priority); hard-reserve allocated quantity; communicate honestly with deprioritized parties; record allocation decision and rationale; do not award stock ad hoc under pressure. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller / Sales Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Arbitrary fulfillment; B2B contract breach; channel conflict; customer disputes; revenue loss on strategic accounts |

---

### EX-021 — Customer Order Cancelled After Reservation

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-021 |
| **Business Scenario** | Customer cancels order or reduces quantity after stock was reserved but before shipment. |
| **Trigger** | Customer order cancelled (BE-35). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Release reservation to restore ATP; return picked but unshipped goods to stock if applicable; record cancellation reason; notify operations if material quantity restored; update fulfillment status for customer service. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Customer Service Representative → Warehouse Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Stock artificially locked to dead orders; false stockouts; reduced sellable availability; fulfillment queue clutter |

---

### EX-022 — Partial Fulfillment Required

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-022 |
| **Business Scenario** | Full order quantity cannot be fulfilled at reservation or pick time, but customer policy allows partial delivery. |
| **Trigger** | Insufficient stock at fulfillment (BE-34). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Identify fulfillable vs. unfulfillable quantity; obtain customer acknowledgment before partial ship per BR-028; ship available portion; place remainder on backorder with ETA or cancellation option; alert purchasing for replenishment. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Customer Service Representative → Warehouse Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Complete order hold loses partial revenue; silent partial ship without acknowledgment causes disputes; backorder queue unmanaged |

---

### EX-023 — Authorized Product Substitution Required

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-023 |
| **Business Scenario** | Primary ordered SKU is unavailable at pick, but an approved alternate product could satisfy the customer need. |
| **Trigger** | Pick exception or availability shortfall with defined substitute relationship (BE-33). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Present only pre-approved substitute options; obtain customer acceptance and authorized approval; reserve and ship substitute SKU; record substitution on order with original and fulfilled product reference; adjust inventory for actual product shipped. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Manager → Sales Manager / Customer Service Representative |
| **Business Impact** | Unauthorized substitute causes margin loss, warranty issues, or customer rejection; order remains unfulfilled if substitution declined without plan |

---

## Domain 5: Replenishment Exceptions

### EX-024 — False Positive Low-Stock Alert

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-024 |
| **Business Scenario** | Low-stock alert fires but investigation shows adequate stock, inbound supply en route, or data timing issue — no genuine replenishment need. |
| **Trigger** | Low-stock alert issued (BE-36); purchasing daily review. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Validate against ATP, open POs, and in-transit transfers; dismiss alert with documented reason; review threshold configuration if recurring false positives; do not place duplicate purchase order. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Buyer / Purchasing Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Duplicate procurement; excess inventory; alert fatigue; ignored genuine alerts later |

---

### EX-025 — Emergency Stockout on Priority SKU

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-025 |
| **Business Scenario** | Class A or priority product reaches zero ATP with active customer demand or open commitments. |
| **Trigger** | Emergency stockout declared (BE-10); stock threshold breached at zero (BE-19). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Escalate urgently to purchasing and operations leadership; check network for transfer before new purchase per BR-011; initiate expedited PO or emergency transfer; communicate realistic re-availability to sales and customer service; document root cause for post-incident review. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Purchasing Manager → Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Lost sales; customer cancellations; premium freight costs; revenue at risk on priority products; reputational damage |

---

### EX-026 — Safety Stock Override Requested

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-026 |
| **Business Scenario** | Reservation, transfer, or fulfillment request would consume safety stock below policy buffer without a replenishment plan. |
| **Trigger** | Reservation or transfer evaluation against safety stock (BE-30, BE-41). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Block routine consumption of safety stock per BR-010; require authorized exception with approver, documented reason, and replenishment plan; record exception for governance review; deny if no recovery plan exists. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Operations Director / Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Next demand or supply shock causes immediate stockout; safety investment wasted; chronic crisis replenishment |

---

## Domain 6: Network Balance & Transfer Exceptions

### EX-027 — Local Stockout With Network Excess Elsewhere

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-027 |
| **Business Scenario** | One location is out of stock on a product while other network locations hold available excess quantity. |
| **Trigger** | Network imbalance identified (BE-42); low-stock at one site with surplus elsewhere. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Verify network ATP; initiate inter-location transfer request before new purchase per BR-011; approve transfer if source can spare stock per BR-012; communicate revised availability to sales. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Regional / Store Manager → Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Duplicate purchasing; excess at one site while another stockouts; trapped capital; lost local sales |

---

### EX-028 — Transfer Would Breach Source Minimum

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-028 |
| **Business Scenario** | Approved or requested transfer quantity would deplete the source location below its minimum threshold or safety stock. |
| **Trigger** | Inter-location transfer requested or approved (BE-41, BE-43). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Reduce transfer to maximum spareable quantity per BR-012; reject or modify request with documented reason; suggest alternate source location if available; do not approve transfer that creates source stockout. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Operations Director / Warehouse Manager (source) |
| **Business Impact** | Cascading stockouts across network; emergency replenishment at source; net worsening of network availability |

---

### EX-029 — In-Transit Transfer Receipt Variance

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-029 |
| **Business Scenario** | Destination receives fewer units than dispatched, or goods arrive damaged in transit between locations. |
| **Trigger** | Transfer shipment received with variance (BE-46). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Document receipt variance; investigate loss or damage in transit; adjust source and destination records accordingly; process write-off or claim if applicable; close transfer only when quantities reconciled. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk (destination) → Warehouse Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Stock lost between locations; both sites show incorrect balances; accountability gap; unresolved in-transit aging |

---

### EX-030 — Emergency Transfer Request

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-030 |
| **Business Scenario** | Location urgently needs stock — key customer order, promotional event, or unexpected spike — faster than supplier replenishment allows. |
| **Trigger** | Inter-location transfer requested with urgency flag (BE-41). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Verify source ATP and minimum threshold; obtain expedited approval; execute pick and ship with documented freight authorization; track in-transit until receipt confirmed; review why standard replenishment failed. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Regional / Store Manager → Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Customer promise missed if transfer delayed; premium freight unbudgeted; source location risk if minimum not protected |

---

## Domain 7: Returns Exceptions

### EX-031 — Return Received Without Authorization

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-031 |
| **Business Scenario** | Warehouse receives returned goods without a valid return authorization linked to an original order. |
| **Trigger** | Returned goods arrive at dock (BE-48) without matching authorization. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Hold goods; contact customer service to validate or issue retroactive authorization per policy; refuse acceptance if policy violation or fraud suspected; do not add to sellable stock without valid linkage per BR-025. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk → Customer Service Representative |
| **Business Impact** | Returns cannot match orders; fraudulent returns accepted; refund without receipt; inventory records incorrect |

---

### EX-032 — Returned Product Fails Inspection

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-032 |
| **Business Scenario** | Returned item is used, damaged, or defective and does not meet resale quality standards. |
| **Trigger** | Return inspection completed with fail outcome (BE-49). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Write off or liquidate non-resalable quantity with reason code per BR-026; do not restock to sellable inventory; process customer refund or credit per original resolution agreement; capture return reason for trend analysis. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Manager → Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Damaged goods resold as new; repeat returns; customer complaints; inflated sellable ATP |

---

### EX-033 — Return Quantity or Product Mismatch

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-033 |
| **Business Scenario** | Physical return does not match authorization — wrong product, partial quantity, or excess units. |
| **Trigger** | Return receipt verification against authorization (BE-48). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Document mismatch; contact customer; hold mismatched items; accept only authorized product and quantity; adjust refund or credit proportionally per policy. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Receiving Clerk → Customer Service Representative |
| **Business Impact** | Over-refund; inventory credited for wrong items; unresolved return status; customer dispute |

---

## Domain 8: Commercial & Promotional Exceptions

### EX-034 — Promotional Demand Exceeds Forecast

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-034 |
| **Business Scenario** | Marketing promotion drives demand above planned levels and promotional stock depletes faster than campaign duration. |
| **Trigger** | Marketing campaign scheduled with accelerating sell-through (BE-55); stock threshold breached on promoted SKUs. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Ring-fence remaining promotional stock per BR-029; allocate to promoted channels; expedite replenishment or network transfer if feasible; inform marketing to adjust campaign intensity; communicate "while supplies last" if stock will not last. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Marketing Manager → Purchasing Manager / Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Campaign stockout during peak visibility; promotional ROI lost; customer disappointment at worst moment; channel conflict |

---

### EX-035 — Campaign Stock Gap Before Launch

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-035 |
| **Business Scenario** | Pre-launch readiness review finds current plus inbound stock insufficient for campaign targets within lead time. |
| **Trigger** | Marketing campaign scheduled or new product launch date set (BE-55, BE-56). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Quantify gap by SKU and location; escalate go/no-go decision to commercial and operations leadership; expedite purchasing if recoverable; delay or reduce campaign scope if not; document risk acceptance if proceeding. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Marketing Manager → Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Public launch without stock; brand embarrassment; wasted marketing spend; BO-24 promotional readiness failure |

---

### EX-036 — Channel Conflict Over Shared Inventory

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-036 |
| **Business Scenario** | Online, retail, wholesale, or marketplace channels compete for the same limited ATP — conflicting allocation requests for last units. |
| **Trigger** | Concurrent orders from multiple channels against shared pool (BE-28). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Apply leadership-defined channel priority rules; hard-allocate per EX-020; update channel-facing availability manually until integration available; escalate recurring conflicts to commercial leadership for policy review. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller / Sales Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Double-selling across channels; store associates vs. e-commerce conflict; wholesale contract breach; inconsistent customer experience |

---

## Domain 9: Financial, Governance & Compliance Exceptions

### EX-037 — Operations and Finance Inventory Mismatch at Month-End

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-037 |
| **Business Scenario** | Operational inventory quantities or valuation do not reconcile with general ledger balance at month-end close. |
| **Trigger** | Month-end financial close initiated (BE-53). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Categorize variances (timing, quantity, valuation); investigate unexplained gaps; correct operational records or agree financial adjustment; complete reconciliation within close calendar; escalate material gaps to CFO. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Finance Manager → Inventory Controller |
| **Business Impact** | Financial misstatement; audit findings; delayed close; BO-18 and BO-20 objectives fail; operations-finance distrust persists |

---

### EX-038 — Adjustment or Write-Off Exceeds Approval Threshold

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-038 |
| **Business Scenario** | Proposed inventory adjustment or write-off exceeds the approver's financial or quantity authority. |
| **Trigger** | Stock correction required (BE-25); significant write-off recorded (BE-54). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Route to independent higher-authority approver per BR-021; require documented evidence for write-offs per BR-023; block application until approved; notify finance for material write-offs. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Manager (initiator) → Operations Director / CFO |
| **Business Impact** | Unauthorized large adjustments; fraud opportunity; financial misstatement; audit material weakness |

---

### EX-039 — Segregation of Duties Violation Attempted

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-039 |
| **Business Scenario** | Same person attempts to perform and approve a conflicting action — count and approve own variance, receive and approve own PO variance, or self-approve material adjustment. |
| **Trigger** | Control incident or policy breach identified (BE-59). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Block self-approval; route to independent approver per BR-019; log policy breach or authorized exception; review role assignment for systemic conflicts; inform Internal Auditor if material or recurring. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Warehouse Manager / Inventory Controller → Operations Director |
| **Business Impact** | Fraud and error undetected; SOX or audit failure; invalid accuracy and adjustment records |

---

### EX-040 — Product Recall Requiring Lot Quarantine

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-040 |
| **Business Scenario** | Quality defect, contamination, or regulatory notice requires recall of specific lot or batch — stock may be in warehouse, in transit, or already shipped. |
| **Trigger** | Supplier quality alert; regulatory notice; internal quality failure discovery. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Identify all affected lot quantity through traceability records; quarantine immediately and exclude from ATP per BR-013; trace shipped units to customers; notify regulatory authorities within mandated timelines; disposition quarantined stock after investigation. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller → Quality / Regulatory (with Operations Director) |
| **Business Impact** | Consumer harm; regulatory penalties; full product-line recall if lot data missing; legal liability; brand catastrophe |

---

### EX-041 — Control Policy Breach With Authorized Exception

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-041 |
| **Business Scenario** | Business situation requires deviation from standard policy — ad-hoc receipt without PO, safety stock override, or emergency approval outside normal authority — with legitimate operational justification. |
| **Trigger** | Control incident identified with exception path (BE-59). |
| **Expected Business Response** | Document approver, policy reference, business reason, and replenishment or recovery plan; apply exception only within granted authority; log for governance review; do not normalize exception into standard practice. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Operations Director / Purchasing Manager |
| **Business Impact** | If undocumented: audit finding and control erosion; if denied when needed: operational paralysis during genuine emergency |

---

## Domain 10: Demand Shock & Lifecycle Exceptions

### EX-042 — Flash Demand Spike From External Event

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-042 |
| **Business Scenario** | Unplanned external event — viral trend, competitor stockout redirect, weather — causes sudden demand depleting stock in hours or days. |
| **Trigger** | Rapid ATP depletion; multiple urgent availability inquiries; stock threshold breached on unaffected forecast SKUs. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Apply allocation rules immediately; assess fastest replenishment path; communicate realistic availability internally and externally; avoid overcommitment; conduct post-event review for safety stock and supplier capacity. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Operations Director → Inventory Controller / Purchasing Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Overselling during spike; reputational damage outlasting revenue gain; unfilled strategic customer orders; supplier also caught short |

---

### EX-043 — End-of-Season or Obsolete Stock Requiring Write-Off

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | EX-043 |
| **Business Scenario** | Seasonal, discontinued, or slow-moving product has no remaining commercial value and must be removed from active inventory. |
| **Trigger** | Scheduled aging review; product discontinued with residual stock (BE-03); overstock report review. |
| **Expected Business Response** | Segregate physically; execute planned exit (markdown, outlet, donation, destroy); process authorized write-off with evidence per BR-023; update financial records; do not delay write-off inflating reported inventory. |
| **Responsible Actor** | Inventory Controller → Finance Manager |
| **Business Impact** | Trapped working capital; inflated operational and financial inventory; recurring carrying cost; misleading availability if stock remains "active" |

## Exception Response Pattern Summary

| Pattern | Exception IDs | Core Business Discipline |
|---------|---------------|--------------------------|
| **Verify before recording** | EX-005 – EX-009, EX-031 – EX-033 | Document at point of occurrence; never accept silent variance |
| **Investigate before adjusting** | EX-012, EX-013, EX-014, EX-016 | Root cause before number correction |
| **Check network first** | EX-025, EX-027, EX-030 | Transfer before purchase |
| **ATP-only commitment** | EX-017, EX-020, EX-022, EX-036 | Promise only fulfillable quantity |
| **Independent approval** | EX-038, EX-039 | Segregation of duties on material actions |
| **Proactive communication** | EX-010, EX-017, EX-022, EX-025 | Customer and internal honesty on delays |
| **Quarantine and exclude** | EX-006, EX-015, EX-040 | Non-sellable stock never in ATP |
| **Governed exception only** | EX-008, EX-026, EX-041 | Documented override — not normalized bypass |

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-DT-001 |
| **Document Title** | Business Process Decision Tables — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Senior Business Analyst |
| **Source Documents** | BRD-IMS-001 (Section 10), Business Workflows (WF-01–WF-32), Business Exception Scenarios (EX-001–EX-043) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business decision logic only — not system rules, validation logic, or technical branching |

### Purpose

This document identifies **32 business processes** that contain **multiple decision paths** and expresses key branching logic as **decision tables**. Each table maps business **conditions** to **actions** and **outcomes** so stakeholders can see how the organization should respond when situations differ.

### How to Read Decision Tables

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Rule** | Rule identifier within the process (R1, R2, …). Rules are evaluated in priority order unless noted. |
| **Conditions** | Business facts that must be true for the rule to apply. "—" means any value. |
| **Actions** | What responsible actors should do when conditions are met. |
| **Outcome** | Resulting process state or next workflow triggered. |

**Notation:** Y = Yes / True · N = No / False · — = Don't care / Not applicable
