## Domain 1: Master Data & Governance

### BP-01: Product Master Data Management (DT-01)

**Decision context:** Product create, update, or discontinuation request received.

| Rule | Request complete & valid | Duplicate SKU exists | Dept approval | Requested status | Actions | Outcome |
|------|--------------------------|----------------------|---------------|------------------|---------|---------|
| R1 | N | — | — | — | Return to requester for missing information | Request pending — not in catalog |
| R2 | Y | Y | — | — | Compare records; merge or correct existing SKU; do not create duplicate | Single product identity maintained |
| R3 | Y | N | N | — | Revise definition; resubmit for purchasing and operations review | Request pending approval |
| R4 | Y | N | Y | Active | Finalize record; publish to all locations; enable receive, replenish, fulfill | Product active in network |
| R5 | Y | N | Y | Inactive | Set inactive; block new replenishment; allow fulfill existing stock per policy | Product inactive |
| R6 | Y | N | Y | Discontinued | Set discontinued; block new orders; flag remaining stock for clearance or write-off plan | Product discontinued — runout planning |

---

### BP-02: Location & Warehouse Setup (DT-02)

**Decision context:** Leadership approves a location change (open, close, or reorganize).

## Cross-Process Decision Flow Summary

High-frequency decision chains across processes:

```text
Goods Receipt (BP-07)
  ├─ Clean → Put-Away (BP-09) → Available
  └─ Variance → Discrepancy (BP-08) → Resolved receipt

Order Intake (BP-16)
  ├─ Full ATP → Reserve (BP-17) → Pick/Ship (BP-18)
  ├─ Partial ATP → Partial/Backorder (BP-19)
  └─ No ATP → Replenish (BP-21) or Transfer (BP-24)

Low Stock (BP-21)
  ├─ False alert → Dismiss
  ├─ Open PO → Track (BP-23)
  ├─ Network stock → Transfer (BP-24)
  └─ No network stock → Requisition (BP-22) → PO (BP-05)

Count Variance (BP-11/12)
  └─ Material variance → Investigate (BP-13)
        ├─ Approved → Adjust (BP-14)
        └─ Rejected → Continue investigation
```

# Business Rule Dependency Analysis
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-BRDEP-001 |
| **Document Title** | Business Rule Dependencies — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Senior Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-BR-001, BRD-IMS-001 (Section 13), Business Workflows (WF-01–WF-32), SRS-DT-001 |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business rule relationships only — not system implementation, validation rules, or technical constraints |

### Purpose

This document analyzes **dependencies among the 32 business rules** (BR-001–BR-032). For each dependency it identifies the **parent rule**, **dependent rule**, **dependency type**, and **business impact**. It also catalogs **conflicting** and **overlapping** rules that require explicit policy resolution.

### Dependency Type Definitions

| Type | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Prerequisite** | The parent rule must be satisfied or in force before the dependent rule can be applied meaningfully. |
| **Sequential** | The parent rule governs an earlier step in the same business process; the dependent rule applies only after the parent step completes. |
| **Compositional** | The dependent rule builds on or is calculated from conditions established by the parent rule. |
| **Constraint** | The parent rule limits, bounds, or restricts how the dependent rule may be executed. |
| **Exception** | The parent rule defines an authorized exception path to the dependent rule under defined conditions. |
| **Reinforcement** | Rules apply to the same control objective from different angles; both must hold simultaneously. |

### Conflict / Overlap Classification

| Classification | Meaning |
|----------------|---------|
| **Scope Overlap** | Two rules govern the same business object or decision point with partially duplicate intent. |
| **Operational Tension** | Both rules are valid but compete for the same resource, timing, or stock pool. |
| **Priority Ambiguity** | Precedence between rules is not explicit; actors may apply them in conflicting order. |
| **Mutual Exclusion** | Rules require mutually exclusive actions in the same context without a defined selector. |

## 1. Dependency Catalog

Dependencies are grouped by business domain. Rule pairs already noted in SRS-BR-001 as interdependent combinations are included and extended.

### 1.1 Availability, Commitment & Fulfillment

| ID | Parent Rule | Dependent Rule | Dependency Type | Business Impact |
|----|-------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| DEP-001 | **BR-005** Put-Away Before Availability | **BR-001** ATP-Only Customer Commitment | Compositional | ATP cannot include received-but-not-put-away stock. Violating BR-005 inflates ATP and causes BR-001 overselling — customers confirmed against stock pickers cannot locate. |
| DEP-002 | **BR-013** Quarantine Exclusion | **BR-001** ATP-Only Customer Commitment | Compositional | Quarantined, hold, and recall stock must be excluded from ATP. If BR-013 is ignored, BR-001 permits commitment to non-sellable inventory — regulatory, quality, and customer risk. |
| DEP-003 | **BR-030** Bonded Inventory Clearance | **BR-001** ATP-Only Customer Commitment | Compositional | Bonded stock is non-sellable until customs release. Same ATP exclusion logic as BR-013; failure blocks legal domestic sale while appearing available. |
| DEP-004 | **BR-001** ATP-Only Customer Commitment | **BR-002** Reservation at Order Confirmation | Compositional | BR-001 defines what quantity is promiseable; BR-002 locks that quantity at confirmation. Without BR-001's ATP definition, reservations lack a consistent baseline and double-allocation risk returns. |
| DEP-005 | **BR-002** Reservation at Order Confirmation | **BR-001** ATP-Only Customer Commitment | Compositional | Each reservation reduces ATP. BR-002 is the mechanism that keeps BR-001 accurate as orders confirm — circular but mutually defining: ATP = on-hand minus reservations and non-sellable holds. |
| DEP-006 | **BR-001** ATP-Only Customer Commitment | **BR-028** Backorder Customer Acknowledgment | Sequential | When ATP is insufficient at confirmation, BR-028 governs the customer agreement path before backorder is recorded. BR-001 prevents silent over-commitment; BR-028 governs explicit under-commitment. |
| DEP-007 | **BR-002** Reservation at Order Confirmation | **BR-003** Verified Pick Before Shipment | Sequential | Stock must be reserved before pick execution. BR-003 deducts inventory only after verified pick; BR-002 ensures the picked quantity was already committed to the correct order. |
| DEP-008 | **BR-002** Reservation at Order Confirmation | **BR-028** Backorder Customer Acknowledgment | Sequential | Partial reservation (available portion) pairs with BR-028 for the unreserved remainder. Without sequencing, partial ship may occur without customer agreement on the backorder portion. |
| DEP-009 | **BR-010** Safety Stock Protection | **BR-002** Reservation at Order Confirmation | Constraint | Reservations must not consume safety stock without authorized exception and replenishment plan. Violation depletes buffer protecting against demand/supply uncertainty — next disruption causes stockout despite apparent policy compliance. |
| DEP-010 | **BR-029** Promotional Stock Ring-Fencing | **BR-001** ATP-Only Customer Commitment | Constraint | Promotional allocation reduces ATP available to non-promotional demand. BR-029 further restricts which orders may consume ring-fenced stock beyond ATP arithmetic alone. |
| DEP-011 | **BR-029** Promotional Stock Ring-Fencing | **BR-002** Reservation at Order Confirmation | Constraint | Non-promotional orders must not reserve ring-fenced promotional stock without commercial leadership approval. Prevents campaign stock erosion through standard reservation. |
| DEP-012 | **BR-014** FEFO Rotation | **BR-003** Verified Pick Before Shipment | Constraint | Pick verification must confirm correct lot/batch per FEFO priority. Wrong lot picked violates rotation even if quantity matches — expiry write-off and compliance risk. |
| DEP-013 | **BR-015** FIFO Rotation | **BR-003** Verified Pick Before Shipment | Constraint | Same as DEP-012 for non-perishable goods — oldest receipt date must be picked first. |
| DEP-014 | **BR-017** Lot/Batch Capture | **BR-003** Verified Pick Before Shipment | Prerequisite | Traceable products require lot attribution at pick. BR-003 verification is incomplete without lot capture — recall scope cannot be determined. |
| DEP-015 | **BR-017** Lot/Batch Capture | **BR-014** FEFO Rotation | Reinforcement | FEFO requires expiry-aware lot identity; BR-017 provides the data FEFO depends on for shelf-life products. |

### 1.2 Inbound, Receiving & Procurement

| ID | Parent Rule | Dependent Rule | Dependency Type | Business Impact |
|----|-------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| DEP-016 | **BR-007** PO Required for Supplier Receipt | **BR-004** Verify Before Inventory Acceptance | Prerequisite | Verification is performed against an authorized PO (or approved ad-hoc exception). Without BR-007, verification lacks a reference baseline — unauthorized receipts enter inventory. |
| DEP-017 | **BR-004** Verify Before Inventory Acceptance | **BR-005** Put-Away Before Availability | Sequential | Only verified quantities proceed to put-away. Put-away without verification propagates unconfirmed stock into the availability chain (DEP-001 risk). |
| DEP-018 | **BR-004** Verify Before Inventory Acceptance | **BR-006** Document Receipt Discrepancies | Sequential | Discrepancies are identified during verification and must be documented before acceptance. BR-006 preserves evidence BR-004 discovers — undocumented acceptance waives supplier claims. |
| DEP-019 | **BR-006** Document Receipt Discrepancies | **BR-008** Three-Way Match Before Payment | Prerequisite | Documented receipt quantities are the "received" leg of three-way match. Missing discrepancy documentation causes payment for goods not received or failure to withhold payment for shorts. |
| DEP-020 | **BR-007** PO Required for Supplier Receipt | **BR-008** Three-Way Match Before Payment | Prerequisite | PO is the "ordered" leg of three-way match. Receiving without PO (BR-007 violation) makes BR-008 impossible — payment control breakdown. |
| DEP-021 | **BR-004** Verify Before Inventory Acceptance | **BR-008** Three-Way Match Before Payment | Prerequisite | Verified receipt is the "received" leg. Unverified acceptance corrupts the match and financial records simultaneously. |
| DEP-022 | **BR-016** Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt | **BR-004** Verify Before Inventory Acceptance | Constraint | MRSL check is part of condition verification for shelf-life products. Failed MRSL triggers reject/disposition before acceptance — prevents BR-014 FEFO from managing already-expired inbound stock. |
| DEP-023 | **BR-016** Minimum Remaining Shelf Life at Receipt | **BR-014** FEFO Rotation | Reinforcement | MRSL at receipt ensures sufficient selling window; FEFO during fulfillment minimizes remaining expiry at customer delivery. Jointly protect shelf-life economics. |
| DEP-024 | **BR-017** Lot/Batch Capture | **BR-004** Verify Before Inventory Acceptance | Constraint | Traceable products require lot capture at receipt as part of verification completeness. |
| DEP-025 | **BR-017** Lot/Batch Capture | **BR-005** Put-Away Before Availability | Sequential | Lot identity must be assigned before or during put-away so subsequent movements maintain traceability. |
| DEP-026 | **BR-030** Bonded Inventory Clearance | **BR-005** Put-Away Before Availability | Constraint | Bonded goods may be physically stored but must not enter sellable availability (DEP-003) until customs clearance — put-away to sellable location prohibited until cleared. |
| DEP-027 | **BR-031** Consignment Ownership at Consumption | **BR-004** Verify Before Inventory Acceptance | Constraint | Consignment receipt is physical verification without ownership transfer. Misclassifying as owned at receipt overstates assets and breaks BR-031 valuation treatment. |
| DEP-028 | **BR-031** Consignment Ownership at Consumption | **BR-008** Three-Way Match Before Payment | Exception | Consignment may not trigger standard PO-to-payment flow until consumption event per supplier agreement — BR-008 applies at ownership transfer, not physical receipt. |

### 1.3 Replenishment & Network Balance

| ID | Parent Rule | Dependent Rule | Dependency Type | Business Impact |
|----|-------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| DEP-029 | **BR-009** Reorder at Reorder Level | **BR-021** Low-Stock Alert Review (via BP-21) | Sequential | Reorder level breach triggers replenishment review. BR-009 mandates same-business-day action; delay guarantees stockout during lead time. |
| DEP-030 | **BR-011** Network Check Before Purchase | **BR-009** Reorder at Reorder Level | Constraint | Before executing replenishment (BR-009), network transfer must be evaluated. Skipping BR-011 causes unnecessary PO spend and worsens network imbalance while BR-009 appears satisfied. |
| DEP-031 | **BR-011** Network Check Before Purchase | **BR-012** Protect Source Location Minimum | Reinforcement | Network check (BR-011) often resolves shortage via transfer; BR-012 ensures the transfer path does not create a new shortage at source. Both required for effective network balance. |
| DEP-032 | **BR-012** Protect Source Location Minimum | **BR-011** Network Check Before Purchase | Constraint | Transfer feasibility assessment must respect source minimum. BR-011 "network has stock" is insufficient if BR-012 blocks the transferable quantity. |
| DEP-033 | **BR-010** Safety Stock Protection | **BR-012** Protect Source Location Minimum | Reinforcement | Both protect minimum stock buffers — BR-010 at policy level, BR-012 at transfer execution. Source minimum typically includes safety stock component. |
| DEP-034 | **BR-027** No Reorder of Discontinued Products | **BR-009** Reorder at Reorder Level | Constraint | BR-009 replenishment action is prohibited for discontinued SKUs. Alert may still fire but response must be runout/clearance, not reorder. |
| DEP-035 | **BR-027** No Reorder of Discontinued Products | **BR-011** Network Check Before Purchase | Constraint | Network transfer may still move discontinued stock for clearance; new procurement is blocked. Prevents obsolete inventory creation. |
| DEP-036 | **BR-032** Class A Priority Monitoring | **BR-009** Reorder at Reorder Level | Constraint | Class A SKUs receive heightened monitoring and faster escalation when approaching reorder level. BR-032 intensifies BR-009 response without changing the threshold logic. |
| DEP-037 | **BR-032** Class A Priority Monitoring | **BR-011** Network Check Before Purchase | Reinforcement | Priority SKUs require expedited network evaluation before external purchase — reduces stockout duration on high-impact items. |

### 1.4 Inventory Control & Governance

| ID | Parent Rule | Dependent Rule | Dependency Type | Business Impact |
|----|-------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| DEP-038 | **BR-018** Blind Cycle Counting | **BR-022** Investigate Before Adjusting | Sequential | Blind count produces unbiased variance detection that triggers investigation. Showing system quantity before count (BR-018 violation) undermines variance integrity and root cause analysis. |
| DEP-039 | **BR-022** Investigate Before Adjusting | **BR-020** Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes | Sequential | Investigation findings must be captured as reason code at adjustment. BR-020 without BR-022 produces codes without verified root cause — analytically weak. |
| DEP-040 | **BR-022** Investigate Before Adjusting | **BR-021** Independent Approval for Material Adjustments | Sequential | Investigation completes before approval decision. Approving without investigation (BR-022 violation) repeats same variance on next count. |
| DEP-041 | **BR-018** Blind Cycle Counting | **BR-019** Independent Count Approval | Reinforcement | Blind count (BR-018) detects variance; independent approval (BR-019) prevents counter from self-approving biased or erroneous counts. Joint fraud/error control. |
| DEP-042 | **BR-019** Independent Count Approval | **BR-021** Independent Approval for Material Adjustments | Reinforcement | BR-019 applies to count variances; BR-021 applies to material adjustments generally. Same segregation principle — overlapping scope (see OV-003). |
| DEP-043 | **BR-020** Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes | **BR-023** Documented Write-Off Authorization | Compositional | Write-off is a subset of adjustment requiring reason code (BR-020) plus additional evidence and authorization (BR-023). |
| DEP-044 | **BR-021** Independent Approval for Material Adjustments | **BR-023** Documented Write-Off Authorization | Reinforcement | Material write-offs require both threshold-based independent approval (BR-021) and documented evidence (BR-023). |
| DEP-045 | **BR-024** Physical Inventory Freeze | **BR-018** Blind Cycle Counting | Constraint | Full count freeze suspends movements that would change quantities during count. Cycle counts during operations (BR-018) continue under BP-11 without full freeze. |
| DEP-046 | **BR-024** Physical Inventory Freeze | **BR-003** Verified Pick Before Shipment | Operational Tension | Freeze suspends shipping until count complete. Conflicts with open order fulfillment — requires freeze scheduling and customer communication (see CF-001). |
| DEP-047 | **BR-024** Physical Inventory Freeze | **BR-005** Put-Away Before Availability | Operational Tension | Freeze suspends receiving/put-away at counted location. Inbound goods queue — delays BR-005 and downstream BR-001 ATP increase. |
| DEP-048 | **BR-013** Quarantine Exclusion | **BR-020** Mandatory Adjustment Reason Codes | Sequential | Quarantine disposition (damage, recall) typically results in adjustment with mandatory reason code — links quality hold to governance trail. |
| DEP-049 | **BR-032** Class A Priority Monitoring | **BR-018** Blind Cycle Counting | Constraint | Class A products receive highest count frequency per BR-032. More frequent BR-018 application on priority SKUs. |

## 3. Rule Dependency Chains

Critical end-to-end chains where breaking any link undermines the chain:

### Chain A — Sellable Availability (Inbound to Customer)

```text
BR-007 (PO) → BR-004 (Verify) → BR-006 (Document variance)
     → BR-005 (Put-away) → BR-013/BR-030 (Exclude non-sellable)
     → BR-001 (ATP) → BR-002 (Reserve) → BR-003 (Pick/Ship)
```

**Business impact of chain failure:** Any break causes phantom availability, overselling, or shipment of non-compliant stock.

### Chain B — Replenishment Without Waste

```text
BR-009 (Reorder trigger) → BR-011 (Network check) → BR-012 (Source minimum)
     → [Transfer] or [BR-007 PO path]
```

**Business impact:** Skipping network check wastes capital; ignoring source minimum relocates shortage.

### Chain C — Count Integrity

```text
BR-018 (Blind count) → BR-022 (Investigate) → BR-020 (Reason code)
     → BR-019/BR-021 (Independent approval)
```

**Business impact:** Skipping investigation or approval perpetuates errors and fraud exposure.

### Chain D — Financial Control

```text
BR-007 (PO) → BR-004 (Verify) → BR-006 (Document) → BR-008 (Three-way match)
```

**Business impact:** Payment for unordered, unreceived, or mispriced goods; audit failure.

## 4. Conflicting Rules

Rules that create genuine tension requiring explicit policy, timing, or precedence resolution.

---

### CF-001 — BR-024 Physical Inventory Freeze vs. BR-002 / BR-003 Fulfillment

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Rules in Conflict** | BR-024 (suspend shipping during full count) vs. BR-002 (honor reservations) vs. BR-003 (ship verified picks) |
| **Conflict Type** | Operational Tension |
| **Nature** | Full count freeze stops outbound movements; confirmed orders with reservations expect fulfillment. |
| **Business Impact** | Customer delivery delays; reservation hold times extend; potential BR-028 backorder triggers if freeze is prolonged. |
| **Recommended Resolution** | Schedule freeze during low-activity window; pre-communicate delays; complete freeze before peak; regional freeze rotation so network can fulfill from alternate locations (BR-011). |

---

### CF-002 — BR-024 Physical Inventory Freeze vs. BR-005 / BR-004 Inbound

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Rules in Conflict** | BR-024 vs. BR-004 / BR-005 |
| **Conflict Type** | Operational Tension |
| **Nature** | Freeze suspends receiving and put-away; supplier deliveries may arrive on schedule regardless. |
| **Business Impact** | Dock congestion; delayed ATP increase; supplier detention charges; inbound backlog after freeze lifts. |
| **Recommended Resolution** | Coordinate inbound schedule with count calendar; stage received goods without put-away to quarantine/staging if policy allows; or reschedule supplier deliveries. |

---

### CF-003 — BR-009 Same-Day Replenishment vs. BR-011 Network Evaluation Time

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Rules in Conflict** | BR-009 (act same business day at reorder level) vs. BR-011 (evaluate network before purchase) |
| **Conflict Type** | Priority Ambiguity |
| **Nature** | Thorough network transfer evaluation may delay PO placement beyond same day; rushing BR-011 risks missing transferable stock. |
| **Business Impact** | Either stockout (BR-009 delayed) or unnecessary PO (BR-011 skipped). |
| **Recommended Resolution** | Define SLA: network check within same business day for Class A (BR-032); standard SKUs may place PO same day while transfer evaluation runs in parallel for next cycle. |

---

### CF-004 — BR-006 Document Before Acceptance vs. Partial Receipt Urgency

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Rules in Conflict** | BR-006 (document all discrepancies before acceptance) vs. operational need to accept good units immediately |
| **Conflict Type** | Priority Ambiguity |
| **Nature** | Damaged/wrong items mixed with good stock — strict interpretation blocks all acceptance until full documentation; operations want good portion in inventory. |
| **Business Impact** | Dock hold delays BR-005/BR-001; or premature full acceptance waives claims (BR-006 violation). |
| **Recommended Resolution** | Accept verified good quantity with documented discrepancy on remainder — partial acceptance path in BP-08/DT-08; never accept undocumented variance. |

---

### CF-005 — BR-029 Promotional Ring-Fence vs. BR-001 / BR-002 General Fulfillment

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Rules in Conflict** | BR-029 (promo stock reserved for campaign) vs. BR-001/BR-002 (ATP and reservation for any confirmed order) |
| **Conflict Type** | Operational Tension |
| **Nature** | ATP may show stock available that BR-029 reserves for promotional channel only. |
| **Business Impact** | Campaign stock consumed by routine orders; promoted channel stockout; or routine orders rejected despite apparent ATP. |
| **Recommended Resolution** | Treat ring-fenced quantity as separate ATP pool or hard reservation at campaign setup; BR-029 overrides general BR-001 for ring-fenced portion. |

---

### CF-006 — BR-010 Safety Stock Exception vs. BR-002 Reservation for Urgent Orders

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Rules in Conflict** | BR-010 (no safety stock consumption without exception) vs. BR-002 (reserve at confirmation for urgent/priority orders) |
| **Conflict Type** | Priority Ambiguity |
| **Nature** | Urgent order confirmation may require stock below safety threshold; BR-010 blocks unless exception documented. |
| **Business Impact** | Order confirmation fails despite physical stock; or safety buffer eroded without replenishment plan. |
| **Recommended Resolution** | Explicit safety-stock exception workflow with approver, replenishment plan, and time limit; priority orders do not auto-bypass BR-010. |

---

### CF-007 — BR-007 PO Required vs. Emergency Ad-Hoc Receipt

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Rules in Conflict** | BR-007 (PO required) vs. emergency receiving without pre-issued PO |
| **Conflict Type** | Exception Gap |
| **Nature** | BR-007 allows "explicitly approved ad-hoc receipt exception" but BR-008 three-way match assumes standard PO flow. |
| **Business Impact** | Emergency stock received but payment blocked; or unauthorized receipt bypasses financial controls. |
| **Recommended Resolution** | Define ad-hoc exception approver, retroactive PO process, and BR-008 alternate match rules for emergency receipts. |

## 5. Overlapping Rules

Rules with partially duplicate scope that are complementary when coordinated, or redundant/confusing when not.

---

### OV-001 — BR-013 Quarantine Exclusion vs. BR-030 Bonded Inventory Clearance

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Scope Overlap |
| **Shared Scope** | Stock excluded from sellable ATP |
| **Distinction** | BR-013: quality hold, investigation, recall. BR-030: customs/regulatory hold. |
| **Business Impact** | If treated as one status, customs-cleared bonded stock may remain blocked; or quality-hold stock may be released incorrectly. |
| **Recommendation** | Maintain separate hold reasons; both exclude from ATP (DEP-002, DEP-003); disposition paths differ. |

---

### OV-002 — BR-014 FEFO vs. BR-015 FIFO

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Mutual Exclusion (by product attribute) |
| **Shared Scope** | Pick and ship rotation priority |
| **Distinction** | BR-014 applies to shelf-life products; BR-015 to non-perishable standard goods. |
| **Business Impact** | Applying wrong rule ships suboptimal lot — expiry write-off (BR-014) or aged stock accumulation (BR-015). |
| **Recommendation** | Product master must classify rotation rule per SKU; never apply both simultaneously to same product. |

---

### OV-003 — BR-019 Independent Count Approval vs. BR-021 Independent Approval for Material Adjustments

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Scope Overlap |
| **Shared Scope** | Segregation of duties for inventory adjustments |
| **Distinction** | BR-019: count-specific (counter ≠ approver). BR-021: value/quantity threshold for any adjustment. |
| **Business Impact** | Low-value count variance may satisfy BR-019 but not BR-021 threshold — approver rules differ. Material non-count adjustment triggers BR-021 only. |
| **Recommendation** | Apply both where applicable; BR-021 is superset for materiality; BR-019 always applies to count-originated adjustments regardless of value. |

---

### OV-004 — BR-020 Mandatory Reason Codes vs. BR-022 Investigate Before Adjusting

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Scope Overlap |
| **Shared Scope** | Adjustment governance |
| **Distinction** | BR-022: process requirement (investigate first). BR-020: data requirement (reason code). |
| **Business Impact** | Reason code without investigation produces categorized but unexplained adjustments; investigation without code loses analytical value. |
| **Recommendation** | Enforce sequence: investigate (BR-022) → reason code reflects finding (BR-020) → approve (BR-019/BR-021). |

---

### OV-005 — BR-009 Reorder at Reorder Level vs. BR-032 Class A Priority Monitoring

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Scope Overlap |
| **Shared Scope** | Low-stock response intensity |
| **Distinction** | BR-009: universal threshold trigger. BR-032: heightened frequency and escalation for Class A. |
| **Business Impact** | Class A stockout if treated with same response speed as Class C; or over-procurement if Class A rules applied to all SKUs. |
| **Recommendation** | BR-009 sets the trigger; BR-032 modulates response priority and monitoring cadence by classification. |

---

### OV-006 — BR-001 ATP-Only Commitment vs. BR-029 Promotional Ring-Fencing

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Scope Overlap |
| **Shared Scope** | What quantity may be promised to customers |
| **Distinction** | BR-001: general ATP arithmetic. BR-029: commercial allocation restriction on subset of ATP. |
| **Business Impact** | See CF-005 — double-counting available stock across channels. |
| **Recommendation** | Campaign setup creates explicit ring-fence reservation reducing general ATP. |

---

### OV-007 — BR-023 Write-Off Authorization vs. BR-021 Material Adjustment Approval

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Scope Overlap |
| **Shared Scope** | Authorization for inventory value removal |
| **Distinction** | BR-023: evidence and authorization specific to write-offs. BR-021: independent approver for material adjustments generally. |
| **Business Impact** | Write-off may satisfy BR-023 documentation but still need BR-021 approver if above threshold; or low-value write-off may need BR-023 evidence but not BR-021 escalation. |
| **Recommendation** | All write-offs require BR-023; material write-offs also require BR-021 independent approver. |

---

### OV-008 — BR-025 Return Authorization vs. BR-028 Backorder Acknowledgment

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Overlap Type** | Scope Overlap (Principle) |
| **Shared Scope** | Explicit customer consent before recording commercial inventory state |
| **Distinction** | BR-025: inbound return acceptance. BR-028: outbound delay acceptance. |
| **Business Impact** | Inconsistent consent standards between returns and backorders erode customer trust policy coherence. |
| **Recommendation** | Unified "customer acknowledgment required" policy in training; separate process paths. |

## 6. High-Risk Dependency Failures

| Risk ID | Broken Dependency | Likely Symptom | Affected Objectives |

| RK-001 | DEP-001 (BR-005 → BR-001) | Overselling received-but-not-located stock | BO-03 accuracy, BO-08 cancellation reduction |

| RK-005 | DEP-038–040 (Count governance chain) | Adjustments without investigation or independent approval | BO-02 accuracy, fraud exposure |
| RK-006 | CF-005 / OV-006 (Promo vs ATP) | Campaign stockout despite warehouse availability | BO-14 promotional readiness |
| RK-007 | DEP-051–052 (Returns → ATP) | Damaged returns in sellable stock | Returns rate, customer complaints |

| Attribute | Detail |

| **Document Title** | Use Case Main Flows — Inventory Management System |

### Purpose

This document describes the main flow for each of the 48 use cases identified in the Use Case Catalog. Each flow specifies the actor action and corresponding system response for the successful completion of the business interaction.

### Flow Legend

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Step** | Sequential step number within the main flow |
| **Actor Action** | Action performed by the primary or supporting actor |
| **System Response** | Observable system behavior or outcome in response to the actor action |

---

## Domain 1: Master Data & Governance

### UC-001 — Manage Product Master Data

**Primary Actor:** Inventory Controller

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Inventory Controller opens the product master management function. | System displays the product catalog with search and filter options. |
| 2 | Inventory Controller selects to create a new product or edit an existing product record. | System presents the product data entry form with required fields (SKU, name, description, unit of measure, category). |
| 3 | Inventory Controller enters or updates product attributes and product identifier (barcode) where applicable. | System validates required fields and checks for duplicate SKU or identifier. |
| 4 | Inventory Controller submits the product record for saving. | System saves the product master record and confirms successful creation or update. |
| 5 | Inventory Controller reviews the saved product record. | System displays the complete product profile with current status and attributes. |

---

### UC-002 — Configure Inventory Locations

**Primary Actor:** Inventory Controller

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Inventory Controller opens the location management function. | System displays the inventory location network and hierarchy view. |
| 2 | Inventory Controller selects to create a new location or update an existing location. | System presents the location configuration form (name, type, parent location, status). |
| 3 | Inventory Controller defines location hierarchy and location attributes. | System validates location structure and confirms hierarchy assignment. |
| 4 | Inventory Controller establishes opening stock balances for location go-live where required. | System accepts opening balance entries by product and records initial on-hand quantities. |
| 5 | Inventory Controller activates the location for inventory operations. | System confirms location is active and available for stock assignment and transactions. |

---

### UC-003 — Define Stock Policies and Thresholds

**Primary Actor:** Inventory Controller

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Inventory Controller opens stock policy configuration for a product or product group. | System displays current reorder level, minimum threshold, and safety stock settings. |
| 2 | Inventory Controller sets or updates reorder level and minimum stock threshold. | System accepts threshold values and validates against business policy limits. |
| 3 | Inventory Controller defines safety stock buffer quantity where applicable. | System records safety stock policy and associates it with the product and location scope. |
| 4 | Inventory Controller saves the stock policy configuration. | System confirms policy is saved and applies thresholds to availability monitoring. |
| 5 | Inventory Controller reviews the effective policy summary. | System displays the active policy with effective date and scope (product, location). |

---

### UC-004 — Classify Products by ABC Priority

**Primary Actor:** Inventory Controller

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Inventory Controller opens ABC classification management. | System displays products with current classification status and classification criteria. |
| 2 | Inventory Controller reviews product velocity, revenue contribution, or criticality data. | System presents supporting product performance data for classification decisions. |
| 3 | Inventory Controller assigns ABC class (A, B, or C) to each product. | System accepts classification assignment per product. |
| 4 | Inventory Controller saves the classification update. | System confirms classification is saved and applies class-based monitoring and count frequency rules. |
| 5 | Inventory Controller reviews the updated ABC classification report. | System displays products grouped by class with classification effective date. |

---

### UC-005 — Maintain Governance Policies and Reason Codes

**Primary Actor:** Inventory Controller

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Inventory Controller opens governance policy and reason code administration. | System displays the current reason code catalog and active governance policies. |
| 2 | Inventory Controller creates or updates a reason code category (e.g., adjustment, shrinkage, exception). | System presents reason code entry form with category and description fields. |
| 3 | Inventory Controller defines or updates inventory governance policy parameters. | System accepts policy definitions and associates them with applicable transaction types. |
| 4 | Inventory Controller activates the reason code or policy for operational use. | System validates completeness and confirms activation. |
| 5 | Inventory Controller reviews the published reason code and policy catalog. | System displays the active catalog available for use in inventory transactions. |

---

## Domain 2: Inbound & Receiving

### UC-006 — Place and Manage Purchase Orders

**Primary Actor:** Buyer

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Buyer opens purchase order management. | System displays open, pending, and historical purchase orders. |
| 2 | Buyer creates a new purchase order and selects supplier. | System presents purchase order entry form linked to supplier and authorized products. |
| 3 | Buyer enters product lines, quantities, expected delivery date, and delivery location. | System validates product eligibility (active status, not discontinued) and calculates order totals. |
| 4 | Buyer submits the purchase order for approval. | System routes the purchase order to Purchasing Manager and records pending approval status. |
| 5 | Purchasing Manager approves the purchase order. | System confirms purchase order as authorized and records expected inbound supply. |
| 6 | Buyer reviews the confirmed purchase order. | System displays approved purchase order with status, line details, and expected delivery information. |

---

### UC-007 — Plan Expected Inbound Deliveries

**Primary Actor:** Buyer

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Buyer opens inbound delivery planning for approved purchase orders. | System displays purchase orders with expected delivery dates and shipment status. |
| 2 | Buyer records or updates expected shipment date and carrier information from supplier confirmation. | System accepts delivery schedule and associates it with the purchase order. |
| 3 | Buyer communicates planned arrival to receiving location. | System updates inbound supply visibility for the destination warehouse. |
| 4 | Buyer confirms the inbound delivery plan. | System records planned inbound delivery and makes it visible to receiving and replenishment functions. |
| 5 | Buyer reviews the inbound delivery schedule. | System displays expected arrivals by date, location, and purchase order reference. |

---

### UC-008 — Receive and Verify Supplier Goods

**Primary Actor:** Receiving Clerk

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Receiving Clerk opens goods receipt for an arriving supplier shipment. | System displays expected purchase order lines and quantities for the delivery location. |
| 2 | Receiving Clerk identifies the shipment against the purchase order reference. | System retrieves matching purchase order and presents expected products and quantities. |
| 3 | Receiving Clerk scans or enters product identifier and verifies quantity and condition of each line. | System validates product identity against purchase order and records received quantities. |
| 4 | Receiving Clerk captures lot or batch number and shelf-life data for traceable products where required. | System records lot/batch attribution and validates minimum remaining shelf life. |
| 5 | Receiving Clerk confirms receipt verification is complete. | System records verified goods receipt, updates receipt status, and stages stock for put-away (not yet available for sale). |

---

### UC-009 — Document and Resolve Receipt Discrepancies

**Primary Actor:** Receiving Clerk

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Receiving Clerk identifies a discrepancy during goods verification (short, over, wrong item, or damage). | System presents discrepancy documentation form linked to the receipt line. |
| 2 | Receiving Clerk records discrepancy type, quantity variance, and supporting notes or evidence. | System captures discrepancy details with mandatory reason code and timestamp. |
| 3 | Receiving Clerk accepts verified quantities and documents unresolved variance separately. | System records accepted quantity for inventory and holds discrepancy record for resolution. |
| 4 | Warehouse Manager reviews and approves discrepancy resolution. | System confirms resolution action and updates receipt and discrepancy status. |
| 5 | Receiving Clerk completes the receipt with documented discrepancy. | System finalizes receipt record with accepted quantities and linked discrepancy documentation. |

---

### UC-010 — Perform Stock Put-Away

**Primary Actor:** Warehouse Staff

| Step | Actor Action | System Response |
|------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Warehouse Staff opens put-away tasks for verified received stock. | System displays received stock awaiting put-away with product, quantity, and suggested storage location. |
| 2 | Warehouse Staff retrieves stock from receiving area and moves it to designated storage location. | System records put-away in progress against the receipt reference. |
| 3 | Warehouse Staff confirms product, quantity, and destination storage location. | System validates storage location assignment and rotation rules (FIFO/FEFO) where applicable. |

| 3 | Warehouse Staff perform wall-to-wall counts and enter physical quantities. | System records all count entries with counter identity and timestamp under freeze conditions. |
| 4 | Inventory Controller reviews count completion status across the location. | System displays count progress and identifies any uncounted locations or products. |
| 5 | Inventory Controller closes the physical count session. | System finalizes count snapshot, releases inventory freeze, and generates variance report for investigation. |

# Use Case Alternate Flows
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-UC-003 |
| **Document Title** | Use Case Alternate Flows — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Business Analyst |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog), SRS-UC-002 (Use Case Main Flows) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Valid business alternatives only — no error or exception paths |

### Purpose

This document identifies alternate flows for each of the 48 use cases in the Inventory Management System. An alternate flow branches from the main flow at a defined step when a valid business condition applies, leading to a different but equally legitimate business outcome. Error conditions, system failures, and validation rejections are excluded.

### Alternate Flow Legend

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | Unique identifier in format UC-XXX-AF-NN |
| **Starting Step** | Main flow step number where the alternate path diverges |
| **Business Condition** | Valid business circumstance triggering the alternate path |
| **Alternative Actions** | Actor and system actions taken along the alternate path |
| **Business Outcome** | Resulting business state upon successful completion of the alternate path |

---

## Domain 1: Master Data & Governance

### UC-001 — Manage Product Master Data

#### UC-001-AF-01 — Update Existing Product Record

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-001-AF-01 |
| **Starting Step** | 2 |
| **Business Condition** | An existing product record requires attribute correction, identifier update, or description change rather than creation of a new SKU. |
| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller searches and selects the existing product from the catalog. System loads the current product profile into the edit form. Inventory Controller updates the required attributes and submits the changes. System saves the revised record while preserving SKU identity and transaction history. |
| **Business Outcome** | Existing product master is updated with corrected attributes; all historical inventory transactions remain linked to the same SKU. |

#### UC-001-AF-02 — Change Product Lifecycle Status

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-001-AF-02 |
| **Starting Step** | 3 |
| **Business Condition** | Business decision requires changing product status to inactive or discontinued rather than modifying descriptive attributes. |
| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller selects the product and chooses status change action. System presents status options (active, inactive, discontinued) with business impact summary. Inventory Controller sets new status and confirms. System applies status change, enforces discontinued reorder prohibition, and retains product record for historical reference. |
| **Business Outcome** | Product status reflects current commercial position; discontinued products are blocked from new replenishment while remaining visible in history and reporting. |

#### UC-001-AF-03 — Resolve Duplicate Product Record

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-001-AF-03 |
| **Starting Step** | 3 |
| **Business Condition** | System detects a potential duplicate SKU or identifier during create or update, and Inventory Controller confirms a merge or deduplication is required. |
| **Alternative Actions** | System presents duplicate match candidates. Inventory Controller designates the authoritative master record and selects the duplicate for resolution. Inventory Controller confirms merge or deactivation of the duplicate record. System consolidates references to the authoritative SKU and retires the duplicate. |
| **Business Outcome** | Single authoritative product identity is maintained; duplicate records are eliminated without loss of transaction traceability. |

#### UC-002-AF-01 — Update Existing Location Configuration

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-002-AF-01 |
| **Starting Step** | 2 |
| **Business Condition** | An existing location requires hierarchy adjustment, attribute update, or status change rather than creation of a new location. |
| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller selects the existing location from the network view. System loads current location configuration. Inventory Controller updates hierarchy, attributes, or operational status and saves. System applies changes and confirms updated location definition. |
| **Business Outcome** | Location configuration reflects current operational structure; stock assignments and transactions remain associated with the updated location. |

#### UC-002-AF-02 — Plan Location Closure and Stock Disposition

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-002-AF-02 |
| **Starting Step** | 4 |
| **Business Condition** | A location is scheduled for closure and requires stock disposition planning before deactivation rather than go-live activation. |
| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller initiates location closure planning. System displays on-hand stock by product at the location. Inventory Controller defines disposition plan (transfer to other locations, sell-down, or write-off). System records closure plan and schedules stock movement or depletion actions. Inventory Controller confirms closure readiness when stock is dispositioned. |
| **Business Outcome** | Location closure is planned with defined stock disposition; location is deactivated without stranded inventory. |

| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-003-AF-01 |
| **Starting Step** | 1 |
| **Business Condition** | Stock policy applies uniformly to a product category or group rather than individual SKUs. |
| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller selects product group or category for policy configuration. System displays group members and current policy defaults. Inventory Controller sets reorder level, minimum threshold, and safety stock for the group. System applies policy to all group members and confirms group-level policy activation. |
| **Business Outcome** | Consistent stock policy is applied across the product group; monitoring and alerts operate at group-defined thresholds. |

#### UC-003-AF-02 — Apply Location-Specific Threshold Override

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-003-AF-02 |
| **Starting Step** | 2 |
| **Business Condition** | A specific location requires different thresholds than the network default due to local demand, lead time, or service-level requirements. |
| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller selects product and overrides thresholds for a specific location. System displays network default and location-specific fields. Inventory Controller enters location-specific reorder level and minimum threshold. System saves location override while retaining network default for other locations. |
| **Business Outcome** | Location-specific thresholds reflect local operating conditions; replenishment alerts trigger based on location-appropriate levels. |

| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller requests ABC analysis report. System generates recommended classifications based on defined criteria. Inventory Controller reviews recommendations and accepts bulk classification update. System applies new classifications and updates count frequency and monitoring rules. |
| **Business Outcome** | Product ABC classifications are refreshed based on current performance data; operational priorities align with updated segmentation. |

| **Business Outcome** | Strategically important product receives appropriate operational priority regardless of current velocity metrics. |

| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller selects existing reason code and initiates deactivation. System confirms no mandatory dependency on active policies. Inventory Controller deactivates the reason code. System marks code as inactive for new transactions while retaining it in historical records. |
| **Business Outcome** | Reason code catalog remains current; retired codes are unavailable for new transactions but visible in historical audit data. |

| **Alternative Actions** | Inventory Controller opens governance policy configuration. System displays current policy parameters by transaction type. Inventory Controller updates policy thresholds or rules and saves. System applies updated governance policy to future transactions. |
| **Business Outcome** | Inventory governance rules reflect current business policy; reason code catalog remains unchanged. |

#### UC-006-AF-01 — Amend Existing Open Purchase Order

| **Alternative Actions** | Buyer selects existing open purchase order. System displays current order lines and status. Buyer modifies quantities, dates, or lines and submits amendment. System routes amendment for approval if required and updates expected inbound supply. |
| **Business Outcome** | Purchase order reflects revised commercial commitment; inbound supply visibility is updated accordingly. |

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Alternate Flow ID** | UC-006-AF-02 |
| **Starting Step** | 4 |
| **Business Condition** | Business need for the purchase order no longer exists or supplier confirms order cancellation before any goods are received. |
| **Alternative Actions** | Buyer selects purchase order and initiates cancellation. System verifies no goods have been received against the order. Purchasing Manager approves cancellation. System closes purchase order, removes expected inbound supply, and records cancellation reason. |
| **Business Outcome** | Purchase order is formally cancelled; no further receipt is expected and replenishment planning reflects removed inbound supply. |

| **Business Outcome** | Inbound delivery plan reflects current supplier commitment; downstream planning uses updated arrival expectations. |

System records partial receipt against purchase order and retains outstanding quantity as open. Receiving Clerk confirms partial receipt completion. System stages received quantity for put-away and maintains open PO balance for future deliveries. |
| **Business Outcome** | Partial delivery is accurately recorded; purchase order remains open for remaining expected quantity. |

| **Alternative Actions** | Receiving Clerk selects ad-hoc receipt option and enters approval reference. System validates authorization and presents expected receipt details. Receiving Clerk verifies and records goods per authorization. System records receipt linked to ad-hoc approval and stages for put-away. |
| **Business Outcome** | Non-standard inbound supply is received under documented authorization with full traceability. |

| **Business Outcome** | Count accuracy is validated through targeted recount; final variance report reflects verified quantities. |

# Use Case Exception Flows
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-UC-004 |
| **Document Title** | Use Case Exception Flows — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Business Analyst |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog), SRS-UC-002 (Use Case Main Flows), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rule Catalog) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business exceptions only — technical infrastructure failures are out of scope |

### Purpose

This document identifies exception flows for each of the 48 use cases in the Inventory Management System. A business exception occurs when a valid business rule, authorization constraint, or operational condition prevents the main flow from completing as intended. Each exception describes how the system must respond and what business outcome results.

### Exception Legend

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Exception ID** | Unique identifier in format UC-XXX-EX-NN |
| **Trigger** | Business event or condition that causes the exception |
| **Failed Step** | Main flow step where processing cannot complete successfully |
| **Expected System Behavior** | Required system response to the business exception |
| **User Notification** | Message or alert presented to the affected user or role |
| **Business Outcome** | Resulting business state; transaction is blocked, deferred, or routed for resolution |

---

## Domain 1: Master Data & Governance

### UC-001 — Manage Product Master Data

#### UC-001-EX-01 — Duplicate SKU or Identifier Detected

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-001-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller submits a new or updated product record with a SKU or barcode that already exists on another active product record. |
| **Failed Step** | 3 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks save, displays the conflicting existing product record, and prevents duplicate identity creation until resolved. |
| **User Notification** | "Duplicate SKU [or identifier] detected. Product [existing SKU/name] already uses this identifier. Resolve duplicate before saving." |
| **Business Outcome** | Product master integrity is preserved; no duplicate SKU enters the catalog. Inventory Controller must merge, correct, or choose a unique identifier. |

#### UC-001-EX-02 — Required Product Attributes Missing

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-001-EX-02 |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller submits product record without mandatory attributes (SKU, name, unit of measure, or category). |
| **Failed Step** | 4 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System rejects submission, highlights missing required fields, and retains entered data for correction. |
| **User Notification** | "Required fields missing: [field list]. Complete all mandatory product attributes before saving." |
| **Business Outcome** | Incomplete product records are not saved; catalog quality standards are enforced. |

#### UC-001-EX-03 — Discontinued Product Reactivation Without Authorization

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-001-EX-03 |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller attempts to reactivate a discontinued product to active status without Operations Director authorization. |
| **Failed Step** | 4 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks status change and routes reactivation request for management approval per governance policy. |
| **User Notification** | "Discontinued product reactivation requires Operations Director approval. Request submitted for authorization." |
| **Business Outcome** | Discontinued product status is not changed without authorized review; obsolete inventory risk is controlled. |

---

#### UC-002-EX-01 — Invalid Location Hierarchy

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-002-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller defines a location hierarchy that creates circular parent-child reference or assigns invalid parent location type. |
| **Failed Step** | 3 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System rejects hierarchy assignment and displays hierarchy validation failure detail. |
| **User Notification** | "Location hierarchy is invalid: [reason]. Correct parent assignment before saving." |
| **Business Outcome** | Location network structure remains valid; stock assignment and reporting hierarchy are not corrupted. |

#### UC-002-EX-02 — Location Activation with Unverified Opening Balances

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-002-EX-02 |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller attempts to activate a new location for operations without verified opening stock balances where go-live policy requires them. |
| **Failed Step** | 5 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks location activation and lists products missing opening balance entry or verification sign-off. |
| **User Notification** | "Location cannot be activated. Opening stock balances are unverified for [N] products. Complete verification before go-live." |
| **Business Outcome** | Location does not go live with embedded inventory errors; cutover integrity is protected. |

#### UC-002-EX-03 — Location Closure with Remaining On-Hand Stock

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-002-EX-03 |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller attempts to deactivate or close a location that still holds on-hand inventory without a completed disposition plan. |
| **Failed Step** | 5 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks deactivation and displays remaining on-hand stock by product requiring disposition. |
| **User Notification** | "Location closure blocked. [N] products with remaining on-hand stock require disposition (transfer, sell-down, or write-off) before deactivation." |
| **Business Outcome** | No location is closed with stranded inventory; stock must be dispositioned per closure policy. |

| **Trigger** | Internal Auditor samples adjustment transaction missing mandatory reason code per BR-020 (legacy or policy breach). |
| **Failed Step** | 4 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System flags transaction as policy non-compliance and includes in audit findings report. |
| **User Notification** | "Policy non-compliance: Adjustment [reference] missing reason code. Include in audit findings and assign corrective action." |
| **Business Outcome** | Governance gap is documented; reason code compliance enforcement is reinforced. |

## Domain 11: Cross-Cutting System Interactions

### UC-042 — View Inventory Movement and Transaction History

#### UC-042-EX-01 — No Transactions Found for Search Criteria

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-042-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller searches movement history with criteria that match no transactions in the selected period. |
| **Failed Step** | 2 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System returns empty result set with search criteria summary and suggests broadening filters. |
| **User Notification** | "No movement transactions found for selected criteria. Broaden date range, location, or product filters." |
| **Business Outcome** | User is informed no matching history exists; investigation scope can be adjusted. |

---

### UC-043 — Query and Review Audit Trail

#### UC-043-EX-01 — Audit Query Exceeds Authorized Scope

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-043-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | Internal Auditor attempts audit trail query for entity types or locations outside authorized audit scope. |
| **Failed Step** | 2 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System restricts query results to authorized audit scope and logs access attempt. |
| **User Notification** | "Audit query scope restricted. Results limited to authorized entities. Contact System Administrator for expanded audit access." |
| **Business Outcome** | Audit access is controlled; sensitive data beyond audit mandate is not exposed. |

---

### UC-044 — Manage User Accounts and Role Assignments

#### UC-044-EX-01 — Segregation of Duties Conflict in Role Assignment

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-044-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | System Administrator assigns role combination that creates segregation of duties conflict (e.g., Buyer and Purchasing Manager on same user). |
| **Failed Step** | 3 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks role assignment and displays conflicting SoD rule. |
| **User Notification** | "Role assignment blocked. Conflicts with segregation of duties rule [SOD-XXX]: [conflict description]. Assign non-conflicting roles." |
| **Business Outcome** | User accounts do not combine conflicting duties; control framework integrity is maintained. |

#### UC-044-EX-02 — Deactivate User with Pending Approvals

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-044-EX-02 |
| **Trigger** | System Administrator attempts to deactivate user account with pending approval items in user's queue. |
| **Failed Step** | 4 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks deactivation and displays pending approval count requiring reassignment. |
| **User Notification** | "User cannot be deactivated. [N] pending approvals in queue. Reassign approvals before deactivation." |
| **Business Outcome** | Approval workflow is not orphaned; pending business decisions are reassigned before access removal. |

---

### UC-045 — Enforce Role-Based and Location-Scoped Access

#### UC-045-EX-01 — Unauthorized Function Access Attempt

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-045-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | User attempts to access function or transaction type not granted by assigned role per FR-081. |
| **Failed Step** | 4 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System denies access, does not display restricted function, and logs access denial per FR-083. |
| **User Notification** | "Access denied. Your role [role] does not have permission for [function]. Contact System Administrator if access is required." |
| **Business Outcome** | Least-privilege access is enforced; unauthorized business actions are prevented. |

#### UC-045-EX-02 — Cross-Location Transaction Without Authorization

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-045-EX-02 |
| **Trigger** | Transactional user attempts inventory transaction at location outside assigned location scope per FR-082 and NFR-SEC-006. |
| **Failed Step** | 4 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks transaction and displays user's authorized location scope. |
| **User Notification** | "Transaction blocked. Location [location] is outside your authorized scope. Authorized locations: [list]." |
| **Business Outcome** | Location-scoped access is enforced; cross-location transactions by unauthorized users are prevented. |

#### UC-045-EX-03 — SoD Violation on Transaction Attempt

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-045-EX-03 |
| **Trigger** | User attempts action that combines initiator and approver roles prohibited by segregation of duties (e.g., count and approve same variance). |
| **Failed Step** | 4 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System blocks action and identifies conflicting SoD rule; routes to independent actor if applicable. |
| **User Notification** | "Action blocked per segregation of duties [SOD-XXX]. This action requires a different authorized role." |
| **Business Outcome** | Conflicting duties cannot be performed by same user; fraud and error risk controls are enforced. |

### UC-046 — Import Initial Product and Stock Master Data

#### UC-046-EX-01 — Import File Contains Duplicate SKUs

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-046-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | Import validation detects duplicate SKU entries within the import file or against existing catalog. |
| **Failed Step** | 3 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System rejects duplicate records, displays duplicate list, and processes only unique valid records if partial import is selected. |
| **User Notification** | "Import validation failed: [N] duplicate SKUs detected. [list]. Correct file and re-import or proceed with non-duplicate records only." |
| **Business Outcome** | Catalog integrity is protected at go-live; duplicate identities are not bulk-loaded. |

#### UC-046-EX-02 — Import References Unknown Location

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-046-EX-02 |
| **Trigger** | Stock balance import references location code not defined in location master. |
| **Failed Step** | 3 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System rejects affected stock balance records and lists unknown location references. |
| **User Notification** | "Import blocked for [N] records. Unknown location codes: [list]. Configure locations before importing stock balances." |
| **Business Outcome** | Opening balances are not assigned to undefined locations; location master precedes stock data load. |

---

### UC-047 — Receive and Respond to Operational Notifications

#### UC-047-EX-01 — Notification Action Deadline Passed

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-047-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | Warehouse Manager opens notification after business-defined response deadline (e.g., Class A low-stock alert exceeding replenishment SLA). |
| **Failed Step** | 1 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System displays notification as overdue, escalates to Operations Director or Purchasing Manager, and retains overdue status. |
| **User Notification** | "OVERDUE: [notification type] for [SKU/location]. Response deadline [date/time] passed. Escalated to [escalation role]." |
| **Business Outcome** | Overdue operational conditions receive management escalation; SLA breaches are visible and tracked. |

---

### UC-048 — Support Multi-Location Split Fulfillment

#### UC-048-EX-01 — Network ATP Insufficient for Full Order Despite Multi-Location Option

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-048-EX-01 |
| **Trigger** | Combined ATP across all locations is still less than total order quantity after multi-location split evaluation. |
| **Failed Step** | 2 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System displays network ATP shortfall and blocks full split fulfillment plan; routes to partial fulfillment or backorder workflow. |
| **User Notification** | "Network ATP insufficient for full order. Total available: [N], ordered: [M]. Proceed with partial fulfillment or backorder for shortfall." |
| **Business Outcome** | Full order commitment is not made when network cannot supply; customer commitment aligns with total available stock. |

#### UC-048-EX-02 — Split Fulfillment Blocked by Source Minimum on Contributing Location

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Exception ID** | UC-048-EX-02 |
| **Trigger** | Proposed split allocation from a contributing location would breach that location's minimum threshold per BR-012. |
| **Failed Step** | 3 |
| **Expected System Behavior** | System reduces or removes allocation from affected location and recalculates split plan with source protection applied. |
| **User Notification** | "Split allocation adjusted. Location [location] contribution reduced to [N] to protect minimum threshold. Revised plan displayed." |
| **Business Outcome** | Multi-location fulfillment does not deplete contributing locations below service levels; split plan respects network balance rules. |

# Use Case Preconditions and Postconditions
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-UC-005 |
| **Document Title** | Use Case Preconditions and Postconditions — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Business Analyst |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog), SRS-UC-002 (Main Flows), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rule Catalog) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Successful completion scenario — conditions for main flow outcome |

### Purpose

This document defines preconditions and postconditions for each of the 48 use cases in the Inventory Management System. Preconditions describe what must be true before a use case can execute successfully. Postconditions describe what will be true after successful completion. Business rule references use the identifiers defined in SRS-BR-001 (BR-001 through BR-032).

### Condition Legend

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **[BR-xxx]** | Condition directly enforced by or derived from business rule BR-xxx |
| **(FR-xxx)** | Condition supported by functional requirement (referenced when no direct business rule applies) |

---

## Domain 1: Master Data & Governance

### UC-001 — Manage Product Master Data

**Primary Actor:** Inventory Controller

#### Preconditions

| # | Condition | Business Rule |
|---|-----------|---------------|
| P1 | Primary actor is authenticated with product master management permission (PG-01). | (FR-081) |
| P2 | Product category and unit of measure reference data are configured in the system. | — |
| P3 | For product updates, the target SKU exists as an active or inactive record in the product catalog. | — |
| P4 | For new products, the proposed SKU and identifier are not already assigned to another active product. | — |

#### Postconditions

| # | Condition | Business Rule |
|---|-----------|---------------|
| PO1 | Product master record exists with unique SKU, required attributes, and current lifecycle status. | — |
| PO2 | Product identifier (barcode) is registered and available for operational lookup. | (FR-003) |
| PO3 | If status is discontinued, the product is blocked from new purchase orders and replenishment requisitions. | [BR-027] |
| PO4 | Product creation or update is recorded in the audit trail with user, timestamp, and changed attributes. | (FR-086) |

| PO4 | Location configuration change is recorded in the audit trail. | (FR-086) |

| P1 | Primary actor is authenticated with notification access for relevant notification types. | (FR-076) |
| P2 | Pending notification exists (alert, approval, exception, inbound delay, campaign). | — |
| P3 | Linked business context (product, order, transfer, campaign) is accessible to actor. | — |

#### Postconditions

| # | Condition | Business Rule |
|---|-----------|---------------|
| PO1 | Notification action is completed or delegated with recorded outcome. | — |
| PO2 | Linked business record reflects action taken (acknowledgment, approval, resolution). | [BR-009] |
| PO3 | Notification is archived or removed from active pending queue. | — |
| PO4 | Notification handling is recorded with user and timestamp. | (FR-083) |

---

### UC-048 — Support Multi-Location Split Fulfillment

**Primary Actor:** Warehouse Manager

#### Preconditions

| # | Condition | Business Rule |
|---|-----------|---------------|
| P1 | Primary actor is authenticated with multi-location fulfillment permission (PG-08). | (FR-048) |
| P2 | Customer order is confirmed with lines requiring fulfillment. | [BR-002] |
| P3 | Single fulfillment location has insufficient ATP; network-wide ATP can satisfy order (fully or partially). | [BR-001] |
| P4 | Contributing source locations have available stock above minimum thresholds. | [BR-012] |
| P5 | Availability confirmation is complete or current network ATP is validated. | [BR-001] |

#### Postconditions

| # | Condition | Business Rule |
|---|-----------|---------------|
| PO1 | Location-specific reservations exist for each contributing fulfillment location. | [BR-002] |
| PO2 | ATP is reduced at each contributing location by allocated quantity. | [BR-001] |
| PO3 | Pick tasks are routed to each source location with linked parent order reference. | — |
| PO4 | Consolidated order status reflects multi-location fulfillment progress. | — |
| PO5 | Source locations remain above minimum threshold after allocation. | [BR-012] |
| PO6 | Split fulfillment plan is recorded in audit trail. | (FR-086) |

---
