# Domain Value Objects
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-DM-002 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Value Objects — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | BRD-IMS-001 (v1.0), SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entity Model, v1.0), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules, v1.0), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog, v1.0) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Immutable business concepts only — no database columns, API payloads, or implementation detail |

### Purpose

This document identifies **Value Objects** in the Inventory Management System domain. A value object is a business concept defined entirely by its attribute values, with no independent identity or lifecycle. Two instances with the same values are interchangeable. When business meaning changes, the value object is replaced — not mutated.

This catalog complements **SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entity Model)**, which documents entities that carry identity and lifecycle.

### Value Object vs. Entity — Quick Reference

| Characteristic | Entity | Value Object |
|----------------|--------|--------------|
| Identity | Has a unique business identifier | No identity — equality by value |
| Mutability | Lifecycle with state changes | Immutable — replace when values change |
| Example | Purchase Order (PO-2026-0042) | Monetary Amount ($12.50 USD) |

### Value Object Domain Map

| Domain | Value Objects |
|--------|---------------|
| **Measurement & Quantity** | Quantity, Unit of Measure, Monetary Amount, Lead Time Duration |
| **Product & Classification** | Product Identifier, Product Category, Product Lifecycle Status, ABC Classification, Rotation Policy, Shelf Life Profile |
| **Stock & Availability** | Stock Availability Breakdown, Stock Status Indicator, Ownership Classification, Stock Threshold Set |
| **Location & Address** | Physical Address, Storage Position Address, Location Type |
| **Time & Period** | Effective Period, Campaign Period |
| **Transaction Lines** | Purchase Order Line, Order Line Quantity, Receipt Line Detail, Transfer Line Detail, Invoice Line Detail, Shipment Line Detail, Pick Line Detail, Requisition Line Detail |
| **Variance & Inspection** | Quantity Variance, Condition Grade, Discrepancy Classification, Disposition Decision |
| **Governance & Control** | Reason Code Attribution, Approval Threshold, Quantity Tolerance, Three-Way Match Result, User Action Attribution, Audit Quantity Snapshot |
| **Fulfillment & Commercial** | Fulfillment Quantity Breakdown, Customer Acknowledgment, Channel Designation, Payment Terms |
| **Movement & Status** | Movement Classification, Hold Reason Classification, Alert Priority |
| **Financial & Traceability** | Valuation Line Amount, Lot Identity |

**Total Value Objects:** 46

---

## Domain 1: Measurement & Quantity

---

### 1. Quantity

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A non-negative numeric amount of a product expressed in a specific unit of measure. Quantity is the fundamental measure for all inventory balances, movements, orders, and counts. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | A quantity of "50 Each" has no identity of its own — only meaning through its numeric amount and unit. Two quantities with the same amount and unit are identical. When count changes, a new quantity replaces the old one rather than mutating it in place. |
| **Attributes** | Amount (non-negative number), unit of measure |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Position, Goods Receipt, Shipment, Stock Adjustment, Inventory Reservation, Cycle Count, Count Variance, Purchase Order, Customer Order |
| **Example** | `Quantity(50, Each)` — fifty units of a product counted, ordered, or moved |

---

### 2. Unit of Measure

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The standard unit in which a product is counted, ordered, stored, and sold — such as Each, Case, Pallet, Kilogram, or Liter. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | UOM is a classification label with no lifecycle. "Case" means the same regardless of where it appears. It is defined by its code and description, not by a unique identifier. |
| **Attributes** | UOM code, display name, base-unit indicator (whether this is the product's primary counting unit) |
| **Related Entities** | Product, Quantity (embedded), Purchase Order Line, Order Line Quantity |
| **Example** | `UnitOfMeasure(CS, Case, baseUnit=false)` — one case as a ordering unit distinct from the each-level base unit |

---

### 3. Monetary Amount

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A monetary value expressed as an amount in a specific currency, used for purchase pricing, invoice matching, adjustment valuation, and write-off financial impact. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | "$1,250.00 USD" has no independent identity — it is fully defined by amount and currency. Arithmetic and comparison operate on values; changing amount creates a new monetary amount. |
| **Attributes** | Amount (decimal), currency code (e.g., USD, EUR) |
| **Related Entities** | Purchase Order, Supplier Invoice, Inventory Write-Off, Stock Adjustment, Inventory Valuation Snapshot, Approval Threshold |
| **Example** | `MonetaryAmount(1250.00, USD)` — extended line value on a purchase order |

---

### 4. Lead Time Duration

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The elapsed business time assumed between placing a replenishment order and having goods available for sale or use at a location. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Lead time is a planning assumption defined by its duration value and unit — not tracked as a separate business object. Replacing "14 days" with "21 days" means replacing the whole value. |
| **Attributes** | Duration value (positive integer), duration unit (business days / calendar days), source (supplier default / product-specific / location override) |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Policy, Supplier, Purchase Order, Expected Inbound Delivery |
| **Example** | `LeadTimeDuration(14, businessDays, supplierDefault)` — two-week supplier lead time for replenishment planning |

---

## Domain 2: Product & Classification

---

### 5. Product Identifier

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A typed product lookup code — SKU, barcode, or alternate identifier — used to reference a product in operational transactions without carrying full product master data. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | The identifier string "SKU-8842" paired with type "SKU" is a value tuple. It identifies a product concept but has no lifecycle separate from the Product entity it references. |
| **Attributes** | Identifier type (SKU / barcode / alternate), identifier value (non-empty string) |
| **Related Entities** | Product, Goods Receipt, Fulfillment Execution, Cycle Count, Customer Return |
| **Example** | `ProductIdentifier(SKU, SKU-8842)` — scanned or entered at receiving dock to match purchase order line |

---

### 6. Product Category

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A business grouping label that classifies products for reporting, filtering, and operational segmentation. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Category is defined by its code and name. "Electronics" is the same category wherever referenced; renaming creates a new category value applied going forward. |
| **Attributes** | Category code, category name, parent category code (optional, for hierarchy) |
| **Related Entities** | Product, Inventory Valuation Snapshot, Operational Alert (filtering scope) |
| **Example** | `ProductCategory(ELEC, Electronics)` — classifies a product for dashboard filtering |

---

### 7. Product Lifecycle Status

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The current commercial availability state of a product: active (orderable and fulfillable), inactive (not sold but may hold stock), or discontinued (exit from assortment, no reorder). |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Status is an enumerated business state without its own identity. `Active` equals `Active` everywhere. Transition from active to discontinued replaces the status value on the Product entity. |
| **Attributes** | Status value (active / inactive / discontinued) |
| **Related Entities** | Product, Purchase Order, Purchase Requisition, Inventory Reservation, Customer Order |
| **Example** | `ProductLifecycleStatus(discontinued)` — blocks new purchase requisitions per BR-027 |

---

### 8. ABC Classification

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A priority segment (A, B, or C) assigned to a product based on business importance — revenue contribution, velocity, or criticality — to prioritize operational effort. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Class "A" is a label with fixed meaning across the catalog. It has no identity beyond its letter value and the classification criteria snapshot may accompany it. |
| **Attributes** | Class value (A / B / C), classification basis note (optional: revenue / velocity / criticality) |
| **Related Entities** | Product, Cycle Count, Operational Alert, Stock Policy |
| **Example** | `ABCClassification(A, revenue)` — triggers highest cycle count frequency per BR-032 |

---

### 9. Rotation Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The required stock rotation discipline for a product: FIFO (first-in, first-out) for standard goods or FEFO (first-expired, first-out) for shelf-life products. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Rotation policy is a rule classification with no independent existence. Two products both assigned `FEFO` share the same policy value. |
| **Attributes** | Policy type (FIFO / FEFO), shelf-life applicability indicator |
| **Related Entities** | Product, Put-Away, Fulfillment Execution, Storage Position |
| **Example** | `RotationPolicy(FEFO, shelfLifeApplicable=true)` — pick instructions prioritize earliest expiration per BR-014 |

---

### 10. Shelf Life Profile

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A point-in-time capture of shelf-life attributes for a received or held lot — expiration date, manufacture date, and remaining shelf life at receipt — used to enforce MRSL and FEFO decisions. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | The tuple of dates and remaining days at a specific moment is immutable fact. When re-measured, a new profile replaces the prior snapshot. It describes condition, not a tracked object. |
| **Attributes** | Expiration date, manufacture date (optional), remaining shelf life in days (at capture point), MRSL policy threshold in days |
| **Related Entities** | Lot/Batch, Goods Receipt, Receipt Line Detail, Receipt Discrepancy, Fulfillment Execution |
| **Example** | `ShelfLifeProfile(expiration=2026-12-01, remainingDays=180, mrslThreshold=90)` — passes MRSL check at receipt per BR-016 |

---

## Domain 3: Stock & Availability

---

### 11. Stock Availability Breakdown

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The decomposed view of inventory quantity at a point in time showing on-hand, reserved, available-to-promise (ATP), and optionally inbound expected — each as distinct quantity components. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | The breakdown is a computed snapshot defined entirely by its component quantities. Two breakdowns with identical components represent the same availability state. ATP is derived, not independently identified. |
| **Attributes** | On-hand quantity, reserved quantity, ATP quantity, inbound expected quantity (optional), quarantined quantity (optional) |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Position, Customer Order, Inventory Reservation, Operational Alert |
| **Example** | `StockAvailabilityBreakdown(onHand=100, reserved=30, atp=65, quarantined=5)` — 65 units quotable to new customers per BR-001 |

---

### 12. Stock Status Indicator

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A derived classification of inventory health for a product at a location: in stock, low stock, out of stock, or overstock — based on comparison against stock policy thresholds. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | The indicator is a computed label with no identity. `Low Stock` at one moment is replaced by `Out of Stock` when thresholds are crossed — a new value, not a mutation. |
| **Attributes** | Status value (inStock / lowStock / outOfStock / overstock), evaluated against threshold reference (optional) |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Position, Stock Policy, Operational Alert |
| **Example** | `StockStatusIndicator(lowStock, reorderLevel)` — triggers replenishment alert per BR-009 |

---

### 13. Ownership Classification

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The legal and financial ownership state of held inventory: owned (organization asset), consignment (supplier-owned until consumption), or bonded (customs-controlled until clearance). |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Ownership type is an enumerated classification without lifecycle. It determines valuation and availability rules but is not itself a trackable business object. |
| **Attributes** | Ownership type (owned / consignment / bonded), ownership transfer trigger (for consignment: consumption / sale / issue) |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Position, Quarantine Hold, Goods Receipt, Inventory Valuation Snapshot |
| **Example** | `OwnershipClassification(consignment, transferOnConsumption)` — excluded from owned valuation until consumption per BR-031 |

---

### 14. Stock Threshold Set

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The replenishment policy limits for a product at a location: reorder level, minimum threshold, safety stock buffer, and maximum (overstock) level. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Thresholds are a coherent set of numeric limits that define policy at a point in time. When recalibrated, the entire set is replaced with a new effective threshold set — preserving history as immutable snapshots. |
| **Attributes** | Reorder level (quantity), minimum threshold (quantity), safety stock (quantity), maximum level (quantity) |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Policy, Stock Position, Transfer Request, Operational Alert |
| **Example** | `StockThresholdSet(reorder=50, minimum=20, safety=15, maximum=200)` — reorder action triggers when ATP reaches 50 |

---

## Domain 4: Location & Address

---

### 15. Physical Address

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The geographic address of an inventory location used for logistics, regional reporting, and network hierarchy grouping. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | An address is defined by its component lines and region. Correcting a postal code replaces the address value — it has no independent business identity. |
| **Attributes** | Street lines, city, state or region, postal code, country |
| **Related Entities** | Inventory Location, Supplier |
| **Example** | `PhysicalAddress(100 Warehouse Blvd, Dallas, TX, 75201, US)` — regional grouping for network reporting |

---

### 16. Storage Position Address

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The within-location address of a storage area — zone, aisle, bin, or shelf — where stock is physically placed after put-away. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | "Zone A / Aisle 3 / Bin 12" is a composite location value with no lifecycle. Two pickers directed to the same address are going to the same place. |
| **Attributes** | Zone, aisle, bin/shelf, storage type (bulk / pickFace / quarantine / bonded) |
| **Related Entities** | Storage Position, Put-Away, Fulfillment Execution, Cycle Count |
| **Example** | `StoragePositionAddress(zone=A, aisle=3, bin=12, type=pickFace)` — pick path destination for order line |

---

### 17. Location Type

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The operational classification of an inventory location: warehouse, store, or distribution point — determining its role in the network. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Location type is a fixed enumeration. "Warehouse" carries the same business meaning across all locations of that type. |
| **Attributes** | Type value (warehouse / store / distributionPoint) |
| **Related Entities** | Inventory Location |
| **Example** | `LocationType(warehouse)` — central fulfillment site in the distribution network |

---

## Domain 5: Time & Period

---

### 18. Effective Period

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A bounded date range during which a business policy, threshold set, or governance rule is in force. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | A period from July 1 to September 30 is defined by its start and end dates. Changing the end date creates a new period value; historical periods remain immutable records. |
| **Attributes** | Start date, end date (optional — open-ended if null), period label (optional) |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Policy, Governance Policy, Promotional Stock Allocation, Role Assignment |
| **Example** | `EffectivePeriod(2026-07-01, 2026-09-30, Q3-2026 Policy)` — stock threshold set valid for one quarter |

---

### 19. Campaign Period

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The bounded date range and commercial scope of a promotional campaign or product launch during which ring-fenced inventory is protected. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Campaign timing is a commercial fact defined by dates and name. It has no identity separate from the promotional allocation entity that references it. |
| **Attributes** | Campaign name, start date, end date, channel scope reference |
| **Related Entities** | Promotional Stock Allocation, Operational Alert, Customer Order |
| **Example** | `CampaignPeriod(Summer Sale 2026, 2026-06-01, 2026-08-31, eCommerce)` — ring-fenced stock protected per BR-029 |

---

## Domain 6: Transaction Lines

Transaction line value objects represent immutable product-quantity-price tuples embedded within document entities. They carry no independent identity — line sequence provides ordering context only.

---

### 20. Purchase Order Line

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A single product line on a purchase order specifying ordered quantity, unit price, and expected receipt quantity tracking. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | PO line meaning is fully defined by product, quantity, and price. Amending a line replaces it with a new line value; the tuple "Product X, 100 units, $5.00" has no identity beyond its content. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, ordered quantity, unit price (monetary amount), received quantity to date, line status (open / partial / closed) |
| **Related Entities** | Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Supplier Invoice, Expected Inbound Delivery |
| **Example** | `PurchaseOrderLine(SKU-4420, Quantity(100, Each), $5.00 USD, received=60, partial)` — open PO line awaiting balance receipt |

---

### 21. Requisition Line Detail

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A product and requested quantity on an internal purchase requisition before commercial PO creation. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | The requisition line is a need statement — product plus quantity — with no independent lifecycle. Approval converts it to a PO line value. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, requested quantity, target location, requested delivery date |
| **Related Entities** | Purchase Requisition, Purchase Order, Operational Alert |
| **Example** | `RequisitionLineDetail(SKU-4420, Quantity(200, Each), WH-DALLAS, 2026-07-15)` — replenishment need from low-stock alert |

---

### 22. Receipt Line Detail

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A verified inbound line recording product, received quantity, condition assessment, and optional lot identity captured at goods receipt. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | What was received is an immutable fact at receipt time. Correcting a receipt creates a new receipt line value or adjustment — the original received tuple remains historical truth. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, received quantity, condition grade, lot identity (optional), shelf life profile (optional), verification outcome (accepted / rejected / hold) |
| **Related Entities** | Goods Receipt, Receipt Discrepancy, Put-Away, Lot/Batch |
| **Example** | `ReceiptLineDetail(SKU-4420, Quantity(98, Each), good, LotIdentity(L20260701), accepted)` — two units short triggers discrepancy |

---

### 23. Order Line Quantity

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The quantity breakdown for a customer order line showing requested, reserved, fulfilled, and backordered amounts. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Line quantities at a snapshot moment are a value decomposition. As fulfillment progresses, new quantity breakdown values replace prior ones. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, requested quantity, reserved quantity, fulfilled quantity, backordered quantity |
| **Related Entities** | Customer Order, Inventory Reservation, Fulfillment Execution, Backorder |
| **Example** | `OrderLineQuantity(SKU-4420, requested=50, reserved=50, fulfilled=30, backordered=20)` — partial fulfillment state |

---

### 24. Transfer Line Detail

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A product and quantity tuple on an inter-location transfer, optionally specifying lot identity for traceable products. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Transfer line content defines what moves. The tuple has no identity beyond product, quantity, and lot — embedded in the Stock Transfer entity. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, transfer quantity, lot identity (optional), source storage position address (optional) |
| **Related Entities** | Transfer Request, Stock Transfer, In-Transit Stock |
| **Example** | `TransferLineDetail(SKU-4420, Quantity(25, Each), LotIdentity(L20260701))` — traceable transfer between locations per BR-017 |

---

### 25. Invoice Line Detail

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A billed product line on a supplier invoice specifying billed quantity and unit price for three-way match evaluation. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Invoice line is a financial fact tuple. Matching compares values across PO line and receipt line — the invoice line itself has no independent identity. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, billed quantity, unit price (monetary amount), extended amount (monetary amount) |
| **Related Entities** | Supplier Invoice, Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Three-Way Match Result |
| **Example** | `InvoiceLineDetail(SKU-4420, Quantity(98, Each), $5.00 USD, $490.00 USD)` — matched against PO and receipt for payment per BR-008 |

---

### 26. Pick Line Detail

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The pick execution record for an order line showing requested versus picked quantity, storage source, and lot applied during fulfillment. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Pick result is an immutable operational fact at verification time. Failed picks generate new pick line values or exceptions — the verified pick tuple does not mutate. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, requested quantity, picked quantity, lot identity (optional), source storage position address, pick verification status (pending / verified / short) |
| **Related Entities** | Fulfillment Execution, Shipment, Lot/Batch, Storage Position |
| **Example** | `PickLineDetail(SKU-4420, requested=10, picked=10, LotIdentity(L20260701), verified)` — verified pick enables shipment per BR-003 |

---

### 27. Shipment Line Detail

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A dispatched product line on a shipment recording shipped quantity and lot attribution at carrier handoff. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | What left the building is an immutable dispatch fact. The shipped tuple defines the outbound movement — no separate identity required. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, shipped quantity, lot identity (optional), order line reference |
| **Related Entities** | Shipment, Fulfillment Execution, Inventory Movement Record |
| **Example** | `ShipmentLineDetail(SKU-4420, Quantity(10, Each), LotIdentity(L20260701))` — inventory deduction at dispatch |

---

## Domain 7: Variance & Inspection

---

### 28. Quantity Variance

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The calculated difference between system-recorded quantity and physically counted or expected quantity, expressed as absolute and signed variance. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Variance is a mathematical result defined by two input quantities. System=100, Physical=95 yields Variance=−5 regardless of when or where calculated. |
| **Attributes** | System quantity, physical or expected quantity, variance quantity (signed), variance direction (short / over / match) |
| **Related Entities** | Count Variance, Cycle Count, Physical Inventory Count, Receipt Discrepancy, Stock Adjustment |
| **Example** | `QuantityVariance(system=100, physical=95, variance=-5, short)` — triggers count variance investigation per BR-022 |

---

### 29. Condition Grade

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The assessed physical and resale condition of received or returned goods at inspection time. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Condition is an evaluated classification at a moment in time. "Damaged — not resalable" is a value judgment captured once; reassessment produces a new grade value. |
| **Attributes** | Grade value (new / good / acceptable / damaged / defective / expired), inspection notes (optional), resalable indicator (yes / no) |
| **Related Entities** | Receipt Line Detail, Customer Return, Return Disposition, Goods Receipt |
| **Example** | `ConditionGrade(damaged, resalable=false)` — returned goods routed to write-off per BR-026 |

---

### 30. Discrepancy Classification

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The categorized type of receipt variance: short shipment, over-shipment, wrong item, damage, or shelf-life non-compliance. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Discrepancy type is an enumerated classification of a variance event. It carries business meaning for resolution workflow but has no independent identity. |
| **Attributes** | Discrepancy type (short / over / wrongItem / damage / shelfLifeNonCompliance), severity indicator (optional) |
| **Related Entities** | Receipt Discrepancy, Goods Receipt, Receipt Line Detail |
| **Example** | `DiscrepancyClassification(shortShipment)` — documented at receipt before acceptance per BR-006 |

---

### 31. Disposition Decision

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The outcome decision for returned or non-conforming goods: restock to sellable inventory, place in quarantine, or write off. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | A disposition is a final classification applied at decision time. Changing decision replaces the value — the decision moment and outcome form an immutable tuple with condition grade. |
| **Attributes** | Decision value (restock / quarantine / writeOff), decision basis (condition grade reference), decision date |
| **Related Entities** | Return Disposition, Customer Return, Quarantine Hold, Inventory Write-Off |
| **Example** | `DispositionDecision(restock, ConditionGrade(good), 2026-07-05)` — returned item returns to sellable ATP |

---

## Domain 8: Governance & Control

---

### 32. Reason Code Attribution

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | An immutable snapshot of the reason code and description applied to an inventory adjustment, write-off, or exception at the time of the transaction — preserving meaning even if the master reason code is later retired. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Historical transactions must retain why they occurred. Capturing `{code: SHRINK, description: "Unexplained loss"}` at transaction time creates an immutable attribution value independent of the Reason Code entity lifecycle. |
| **Attributes** | Reason code, reason description, reason category (adjustment / shrinkage / damage / obsolescence / receipt / return) |
| **Related Entities** | Stock Adjustment, Inventory Write-Off, Receipt Discrepancy, Inventory Movement Record, Reason Code (master reference entity) |
| **Example** | `ReasonCodeAttribution(SHRINK, Unexplained loss, shrinkage)` — mandatory on every adjustment per BR-020 |

---

### 33. Approval Threshold

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A governance limit — expressed as quantity, monetary amount, or both — above which independent approval is required before an inventory action takes effect. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Threshold limits are policy numbers without identity. "$5,000 adjustment requires director approval" is a rule value applied at evaluation time. |
| **Attributes** | Threshold type (quantity / monetary / both), quantity limit (optional), monetary limit (optional), required approver role |
| **Related Entities** | Governance Policy, Stock Adjustment, Count Variance, Inventory Write-Off |
| **Example** | `ApprovalThreshold(monetary, limit=$5000, approver=OperationsDirector)` — independent approval per BR-021 |

---

### 34. Quantity Tolerance

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The acceptable variance range between ordered, received, and billed quantities or amounts within which automatic match approval is permitted. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Tolerance of "±2% or ±5 units" is a policy parameter value. It defines acceptable bounds — not a tracked business object. |
| **Attributes** | Tolerance type (percentage / absolute quantity / absolute monetary), tolerance value, evaluation basis (quantity / amount) |
| **Related Entities** | Governance Policy, Receipt Discrepancy, Three-Way Match Result, Supplier Invoice |
| **Example** | `QuantityTolerance(percentage, 2%, quantity)` — receipt within 2% auto-accepted; beyond triggers discrepancy |

---

### 35. Three-Way Match Result

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The outcome of comparing purchase order, goods receipt, and supplier invoice lines — indicating matched within tolerance or exception requiring resolution. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Match result is a computed evaluation at a point in time: matched, quantity exception, price exception, or unmatched. Same inputs yield same result — no independent identity. |
| **Attributes** | Match status (matched / quantityException / priceException / unmatched), variance quantity (optional), variance amount (optional), tolerance applied |
| **Related Entities** | Supplier Invoice, Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Supplier |
| **Example** | `ThreeWayMatchResult(matched, tolerance=QuantityTolerance(2%))` — payment authorized per BR-008 |

---

### 36. User Action Attribution

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | An immutable record of who performed or approved a business action, including user identity and role at the time of action — supporting accountability and segregation of duties. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | The tuple `{user: J.Smith, role: WarehouseManager, timestamp: 2026-07-05T14:30}` at action time is historical fact. Role changes later do not alter the captured attribution value. |
| **Attributes** | User identifier, user display name, role at time of action, action timestamp |
| **Related Entities** | Inventory Movement Record, Audit Trail Record, Stock Adjustment, Count Variance, Inventory Write-Off, User Account |
| **Example** | `UserActionAttribution(WH-MGR-007, Jane Smith, WarehouseManager, 2026-07-05T14:30)` — approver distinct from counter per BR-019 |

---

### 37. Audit Quantity Snapshot

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | A before-and-after capture of inventory quantity or status at the moment of a material change, forming the evidential basis of audit trail records. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Snapshot `{before: 100, after: 95}` is immutable historical fact. It describes state transition — not an entity with its own lifecycle. |
| **Attributes** | Before quantity, after quantity, before status (optional), after status (optional), snapshot timestamp |
| **Related Entities** | Audit Trail Record, Stock Adjustment, Inventory Movement Record, Count Variance |
| **Example** | `AuditQuantitySnapshot(before=100, after=95, timestamp=2026-07-05T14:30)` — records adjustment impact for audit |

---

## Domain 9: Fulfillment & Commercial

---

### 38. Fulfillment Quantity Breakdown

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The decomposition of an order line's quantity into fulfilled, backordered, and cancelled portions after availability confirmation or pick execution. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Breakdown `{requested: 50, fulfilled: 30, backordered: 20}` is a state summary defined by its components. Progress replaces the breakdown value — it does not mutate in place. |
| **Attributes** | Requested quantity, fulfilled quantity, backordered quantity, cancelled quantity |
| **Related Entities** | Customer Order, Backorder, Fulfillment Execution, Shipment |
| **Example** | `FulfillmentQuantityBreakdown(requested=50, fulfilled=30, backordered=20, cancelled=0)` — partial fulfillment with customer acknowledgment per BR-028 |

---

### 39. Customer Acknowledgment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | Explicit customer consent to accept a backorder or partial delivery, including acknowledgment method and timestamp — elevating backorder from internal note to mutual agreement. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Acknowledgment is a captured fact: who agreed, when, and how. It has no lifecycle — either the acknowledgment value exists or it does not. |
| **Attributes** | Acknowledgment status (pending / acknowledged / declined), acknowledgment method (phone / email / portal), acknowledgment timestamp, acknowledged by (customer contact reference) |
| **Related Entities** | Backorder, Customer Order, Fulfillment Quantity Breakdown |
| **Example** | `CustomerAcknowledgment(acknowledged, email, 2026-07-05T10:15, customerContact=ORD-Acct-442)` — required before backorder recorded per BR-028 |

---

### 40. Channel Designation

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The sales or fulfillment channel to which promotional stock or an order is attributed — such as eCommerce, retail store, B2B, or promotional campaign. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Channel label is a commercial classification without identity. "eCommerce" means the same across all orders and allocations referencing it. |
| **Attributes** | Channel code, channel name, channel type (direct / partner / promotional) |
| **Related Entities** | Customer Order, Promotional Stock Allocation, Campaign Period |
| **Example** | `ChannelDesignation(B2B, Business Direct, direct)` — order fulfilled from B2B allocation pool |

---

### 41. Payment Terms

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The agreed commercial payment conditions between the organization and a supplier, governing invoice due dates and payment authorization timing. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | "Net 30" is a terms classification defined by its code and due-day count. It has no lifecycle independent of the supplier relationship context. |
| **Attributes** | Terms code (e.g., NET30, NET60, COD), due days, discount terms (optional: percentage and days) |
| **Related Entities** | Supplier, Purchase Order, Supplier Invoice |
| **Example** | `PaymentTerms(NET30, dueDays=30)` — invoice due 30 days from receipt on supplier agreement |

---

## Domain 10: Movement & Status Classification

---

### 42. Movement Classification

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The categorized type of inventory movement event: receipt, shipment, transfer, adjustment, write-off, reservation, return, or put-away. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Movement type is an enumerated label classifying what happened. Two receipt movements share the same classification value — identity belongs to the movement record entity. |
| **Attributes** | Movement type (receipt / shipment / transfer / adjustment / writeOff / reservation / return / putAway), direction (inbound / outbound / neutral) |
| **Related Entities** | Inventory Movement Record, Goods Receipt, Shipment, Stock Transfer, Stock Adjustment |
| **Example** | `MovementClassification(transfer, neutral)` — inter-location stock movement between source and destination |

---

### 43. Hold Reason Classification

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The categorized reason inventory is placed under quarantine or hold: quality investigation, regulatory restriction, product recall, or customs/bonded clearance pending. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Hold reason is a classification enum determining exclusion from ATP. The reason value defines business treatment — not a separately tracked object. |
| **Attributes** | Hold type (quality / regulatory / recall / customs / investigation), sellable exclusion indicator (always true for holds) |
| **Related Entities** | Quarantine Hold, Stock Position, Goods Receipt |
| **Example** | `HoldReasonClassification(customs, sellableExcluded=true)` — bonded stock excluded from ATP per BR-030 |

---

### 44. Alert Priority

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The urgency classification assigned to an operational alert based on severity of the underlying condition — such as Class A stockout versus routine low-stock warning. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Priority is a severity label (critical / high / medium / low) with no identity. Same condition severity always maps to the same priority value. |
| **Attributes** | Priority level (critical / high / medium / low), escalation indicator, response time expectation (optional) |
| **Related Entities** | Operational Alert, Stock Status Indicator, ABC Classification |
| **Example** | `AlertPriority(critical, escalation=true, responseTime=sameDay)` — Class A stockout alert per BR-032 |

---

## Domain 11: Financial & Traceability

---

### 45. Valuation Line Amount

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The financial value of an inventory quantity calculated as unit cost multiplied by quantity — used in valuation snapshots and write-off impact assessment. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Extended value is a computed financial tuple (quantity × unit cost). Same inputs always produce the same value — no independent business identity. |
| **Attributes** | Product identifier, quantity, unit cost (monetary amount), extended value (monetary amount), ownership classification |
| **Related Entities** | Inventory Valuation Snapshot, Inventory Write-Off, Stock Adjustment |
| **Example** | `ValuationLineAmount(SKU-4420, Quantity(100, Each), $5.00 USD, $500.00 USD, owned)` — month-end valuation line |

---

### 46. Lot Identity

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Definition** | The identifying tuple for a traceable production or receipt batch — lot number combined with key dates — captured on movements without referencing the full Lot/Batch entity state. |
| **Why It Is a Value Object** | Lot identity `{number: L20260701, expiration: 2026-12-01}` on a pick line is an immutable identifier tuple embedded in transactions. It describes which batch was touched — the Lot/Batch entity carries ongoing stock state. |
| **Attributes** | Lot/batch number, expiration date (optional), manufacture date (optional) |
| **Related Entities** | Lot/Batch, Receipt Line Detail, Pick Line Detail, Transfer Line Detail, Shipment Line Detail, Inventory Movement Record |
| **Example** | `LotIdentity(L20260701, expiration=2026-12-01)` — captured on pick for traceability per BR-017 |

---

| **Inventory Location** | Physical Address, Location Type |
| **Storage Position** | Storage Position Address |
| **Purchase Order** | Purchase Order Line (collection), Payment Terms, Lead Time Duration |
| **Goods Receipt** | Receipt Line Detail (collection), User Action Attribution |
| **Customer Order** | Order Line Quantity (collection), Fulfillment Quantity Breakdown, Channel Designation |
| **Count Variance** | Quantity Variance, Reason Code Attribution, User Action Attribution |
| **Stock Adjustment** | Quantity, Reason Code Attribution, Audit Quantity Snapshot, Approval Threshold (evaluated) |
| **Supplier Invoice** | Invoice Line Detail (collection), Three-Way Match Result |
| **Promotional Stock Allocation** | Campaign Period, Channel Designation, Quantity |
| **Inventory Movement Record** | Movement Classification, Quantity, Lot Identity, Reason Code Attribution, User Action Attribution, Audit Quantity Snapshot |
| **Return Disposition** | Condition Grade, Disposition Decision |

# Domain Aggregates
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-DM-003 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Aggregates — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | DDD Solution Architect |
| **Source Documents** | BRD-IMS-001 (v1.0), SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entity Model, v1.0), SRS-DM-002 (Domain Value Objects, v1.0), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules, v1.0) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Aggregate design only — no persistence, repositories, or infrastructure |

### Purpose

This document defines **Domain-Driven Design aggregates** for the Inventory Management System. Each aggregate is a consistency boundary: a cluster of entities and value objects mutated together in a single business transaction, accessed only through the aggregate root. External references use identity only — never direct navigation into aggregate internals.

### Aggregate Design Principles Applied

| Principle | Application in IMS |
|-----------|-------------------|
| **One transaction, one aggregate** | Stock deduction and reservation never share a transaction with PO creation |
| **Reference by identity** | Fulfillment references `StockPosition` by product + location; does not hold object references |
| **Small, business-meaningful boundaries** | Stock Position scoped to one product at one location — not entire warehouse |
| **Invariants enforced at root** | All quantity changes pass through aggregate root methods that validate business rules |
| **Eventual consistency across aggregates** | Goods Receipt completion raises domain event consumed by Stock Position aggregate |

### Bounded Context Overview

| Bounded Context | Aggregates |
|-----------------|------------|
| **Catalog & Network** | Product Catalog, Inventory Location, Supplier, Inventory Governance |
| **Inventory Balance** | Stock Position, Stock Policy |
| **Procurement & Inbound** | Purchase Requisition, Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Supplier Invoice |
| **Order Fulfillment** | Customer Order Fulfillment |
| **Network Transfer** | Stock Transfer |
| **Inventory Accuracy** | Cycle Count, Physical Inventory Count, Inventory Adjustment Case |
| **Returns** | Customer Return Case |
| **Commercial** | Promotional Stock Allocation |
| **Identity & Access** | User Account |

**Total Aggregates:** 18

---

## Bounded Context 1: Catalog & Network

---

### Aggregate 1: Product Catalog

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Product |
| **Included Entities** | None *(Product is a single-entity aggregate; classification and identifiers are value objects on the root)* |
| **Included Value Objects** | Product Identifier, Product Category, Product Lifecycle Status, ABC Classification, Rotation Policy, Shelf Life Profile (MRSL policy), Unit of Measure |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | SKU must be unique across the catalog. Product name and unit of measure are mandatory. Discontinued products must not be eligible for new replenishment or purchase orders (BR-027). Inactive or discontinued products must be blocked from new reservations unless an authorized exception exists. ABC classification must be A, B, or C when assigned (BR-032 context). Traceable products must declare lot/batch requirement and rotation policy (FIFO or FEFO). Product status transitions must record prior status, new status, and attribution. |
| **Responsibilities** | Maintain the single authoritative product identity (SKU) used across all locations and processes. Govern product lifecycle from introduction through discontinuation. Assign operational classification (ABC) and rotation/traceability attributes that downstream aggregates enforce. Detect and resolve duplicate product identity conflicts. |
| **Business Justification** | Product master data is referenced by every inventory transaction but changes infrequently and independently of stock quantities. A dedicated aggregate prevents catalog edits from coupling to high-frequency stock mutations. Discontinued status must be enforced before any procurement aggregate accepts an order line — the Product root is the gatekeeper of assortment validity. |

---

### Aggregate 2: Inventory Location

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Inventory Location |
| **Included Entities** | Storage Position |
| **Included Value Objects** | Physical Address, Location Type, Location Hierarchy Path (parent reference by identity), Effective Period (go-live / closure) |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Location name, type, and operational status are mandatory. A location cannot be its own parent or ancestor in the hierarchy. Deactivated or closing locations must not accept new receipts, reservations, or fulfillments except authorized disposition activity. Location activation for transactions requires approved opening balances when go-live policy applies. Physical inventory freeze (BR-024) must block all receiving, shipping, transfers, and adjustments at the location while a Physical Inventory Count aggregate reports active freeze for this location. Closure is blocked while on-hand stock remains unless a disposition plan is documented or waived. |
| **Responsibilities** | Define the network of places where stock is held and operated. Manage storage position structure within a location. Control location operational status (active, planned, closing). Enforce freeze compliance during wall-to-wall counts. Support location go-live and closure lifecycle. |
| **Business Justification** | Location configuration and storage layout change independently of stock balances. Storage Positions belong to exactly one location and are meaningless outside it — they share the location's lifecycle. Freeze enforcement requires the location aggregate to expose a single authoritative "frozen" state that all other aggregates consult before permitting mutations at that site. |

---

### Aggregate 3: Supplier

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Supplier |
| **Included Entities** | None |
| **Included Value Objects** | Contact Details, Payment Terms, Lead Time Duration (default) |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Supplier code must be unique. Supplier must be active to appear on new purchase orders. Consignment agreement indicator governs ownership classification applied at receipt — consignment stock is not owned until consumption (BR-031). Payment terms must be defined before purchase orders are issued to the supplier. |
| **Responsibilities** | Maintain supplier commercial identity and default procurement terms. Indicate consignment relationship where ownership rules differ from standard purchase. Support supplier delivery performance tracking references. |
| **Business Justification** | Supplier is master data referenced by Purchase Order and Goods Receipt aggregates by identity. Commercial terms belong with the supplier definition and must remain consistent across all open POs — isolating suppliers prevents PO line edits from corrupting supplier master data. |

---

### Aggregate 4: Inventory Governance

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Governance Policy |
| **Included Entities** | Reason Code |
| **Included Value Objects** | Approval Threshold, Quantity Tolerance, Effective Period |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Reason codes must be unique; retired codes must not be selectable for new transactions (BR-020 context). Every adjustment, write-off, and receipt discrepancy requires an active reason code at submission time. Only one governance policy version may be effective for a given parameter at any point in time. Adjustments above defined financial or quantity thresholds require independent approval (BR-021). Receipt quantity tolerance limits govern auto-acceptance vs. discrepancy creation (BR-006, BR-008). Segregation-of-duties rules: counter must not approve adjustments from their own count (BR-019). |
| **Responsibilities** | Maintain the standardized reason code taxonomy for all inventory exceptions and corrections. Define approval thresholds, tolerance limits, and exception policies that other aggregates consult during validation. Govern policy versioning with non-overlapping effective periods. |
| **Business Justification** | Reason codes and governance thresholds are organization-wide reference data that many aggregates consult but none should own. Centralizing them in one aggregate ensures a single policy source — when a threshold changes, all aggregates evaluate against the same effective policy without embedding rules in each aggregate. |

---

## Bounded Context 2: Inventory Balance

---

### Aggregate 5: Stock Position

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Stock Position |
| **Included Entities** | Lot/Batch *(when product is traceable)*, Quarantine Hold |
| **Included Value Objects** | Stock Availability Breakdown, Stock Status Indicator, Ownership Classification, Quantity, Lot Identity, Hold Reason Classification, Reason Code Attribution, Audit Quantity Snapshot, User Action Attribution |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | On-hand quantity must never be negative. Available-to-promise (ATP) = on-hand minus reserved minus quarantined/hold quantities — ATP must never exceed on-hand (BR-001, BR-013). Quarantined and bonded stock must be excluded from ATP (BR-013, BR-030). Consignment stock must not be treated as owned for fulfillment until ownership transfer event (BR-031). Safety stock buffer must not be consumed below policy minimum without authorized exception (BR-010). Lot/batch identity must be captured for all movements on traceable products (BR-017). Stock status indicator must be recalculated when quantities cross policy thresholds. All quantity mutations must produce an Inventory Movement Record as a domain event — movement history is immutable. Location must not be frozen (consult Inventory Location aggregate) when accepting quantity changes except authorized count adjustments. |
| **Responsibilities** | Maintain authoritative on-hand, reserved, and ATP quantities for one product at one location. Manage lot/batch-level quantities for traceable products. Apply and release quarantine holds. Enforce ownership classification effects on availability and valuation treatment. Accept inbound quantity increases (from receipt, transfer-in, return restock) and outbound decreases (from shipment, transfer-out, adjustment, write-off) only through root operations. Emit domain events on every balance change for audit and reporting consumers. |
| **Business Justification** | Stock Position is the system's most contended consistency boundary — reservations, picks, receipts, and adjustments all compete for the same quantities. Scoping the aggregate to one product at one location minimizes lock contention while guaranteeing ATP is always mathematically consistent within the boundary. Lot/Batch and Quarantine Hold entities belong inside because hold application immediately reduces ATP — partial updates across separate aggregates would allow overselling. |

---

### Aggregate 6: Stock Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Stock Policy |
| **Included Entities** | None |
| **Included Value Objects** | Stock Threshold Set, Lead Time Duration, Effective Period |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Reorder level, minimum threshold, and safety stock must be zero or positive. Minimum threshold must not exceed reorder level unless an explicitly authorized inverted configuration exists. Threshold changes must include an effective date and retain prior values as immutable history. Replenishment action must trigger when ATP reaches reorder level (BR-009). Safety stock must not be bypassed without documented approval and replenishment plan (BR-010). Source location minimum must be enforced when this policy governs a transfer source (BR-012). |
| **Responsibilities** | Define replenishment thresholds for a specific product at a specific location. Maintain threshold change history with effective dating. Provide the policy reference that Stock Position uses to compute stock status indicators and that replenishment processes use to trigger alerts. |
| **Business Justification** | Stock policy changes are infrequent, approval-governed events distinct from high-frequency quantity mutations. Separating policy from Stock Position allows threshold recalibration without locking stock during active fulfillment. The product + location identity key aligns with how planners think about replenishment — one policy per SKU per site. |

---

## Bounded Context 3: Procurement & Inbound

---

### Aggregate 7: Purchase Requisition

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Purchase Requisition |
| **Included Entities** | None *(requisition lines are value objects)* |
| **Included Value Objects** | Requisition Line Detail (collection), User Action Attribution |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Requisition lines must reference active products — discontinued products are prohibited (BR-027). Requested quantities must be greater than zero. Network availability must be evaluated before requisition approval — excess at other locations should trigger transfer consideration before procurement (BR-011). Safety stock must not be implicitly bypassed by requisition quantity decisions (BR-010). Requisition must reach approved status before conversion to a Purchase Order. |
| **Responsibilities** | Capture internal replenishment need with product, quantity, and target location. Route through approval workflow. Convert to Purchase Order upon approval. Link to triggering low-stock alert reference when applicable. |
| **Business Justification** | Requisition is an internal intent document with its own approval lifecycle, distinct from the commercial PO commitment. Keeping it as a separate aggregate allows rejection or amendment without affecting supplier-facing PO records. Conversion to PO is a cross-aggregate operation creating a new Purchase Order aggregate from approved requisition identity. |

---

### Aggregate 8: Purchase Order

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Purchase Order |
| **Included Entities** | Expected Inbound Delivery |
| **Included Value Objects** | Purchase Order Line (collection), Payment Terms, Lead Time Duration, Monetary Amount |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | PO must include supplier reference, receiving location, product lines, and expected delivery date. PO lines must reference active products and active receiving locations — discontinued products prohibited (BR-027). Ordered quantity must be greater than zero. A valid PO is required before supplier goods receipt except explicitly approved ad-hoc exceptions (BR-007). Received quantity per line must not exceed ordered quantity plus defined tolerance without discrepancy workflow. PO status transitions: open → partial → closed/cancelled; cancelled POs must not accept receipts. Expected inbound delivery dates must be valid and associated with an open PO line. |
| **Responsibilities** | Record authorized commercial commitment to a supplier. Track ordered vs. received quantities per line. Manage expected inbound delivery schedules. Support PO amendment and cancellation with receipt implications. Provide the reference document for goods receipt verification and three-way match. |
| **Business Justification** | Purchase Order is the commercial control document governing inbound supply. Expected Inbound Delivery entities belong inside because delivery schedule changes are part of the same procurement commitment — splitting them risks inconsistent inbound visibility. PO enforces BR-007 as the gate for the Goods Receipt aggregate. |

---

### Aggregate 9: Goods Receipt

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Goods Receipt |
| **Included Entities** | Receipt Discrepancy, Put-Away |
| **Included Value Objects** | Receipt Line Detail (collection), Condition Grade, Discrepancy Classification, Quantity Variance, Shelf Life Profile, Lot Identity, User Action Attribution |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Inbound goods must be verified before acceptance — quantity, product identity, and condition confirmed (BR-004). Valid PO reference required except approved ad-hoc exception (BR-007). Receipt discrepancies must be documented before acceptance of affected quantities (BR-006). Minimum remaining shelf life (MRSL) must be met for shelf-life products — non-compliant deliveries rejected or dispositioned (BR-016). Lot/batch identity must be captured for traceable products at receipt (BR-017). Bonded inventory must remain on hold until customs clearance — not released to sellable via put-away (BR-030). Received stock is not available for sale until put-away is confirmed (BR-005). Put-away must assign storage position and apply rotation placement (BR-014, BR-015). Received quantity must not be accepted into stock position until put-away completion triggers cross-aggregate notification. |
| **Responsibilities** | Orchestrate the inbound verification workflow from dock arrival through put-away confirmation. Document and resolve receipt discrepancies with evidence. Capture lot/batch and shelf-life data at receipt. Manage put-away as the final step before stock becomes available. Emit domain event on put-away completion for Stock Position aggregate to increase on-hand quantity. |
| **Business Justification** | Receipt, discrepancy resolution, and put-away are one operational unit of work at the receiving dock — a receiver verifies, documents exceptions, and stows goods in a continuous flow. Combining them ensures stock is never marked available (BR-005) without verified receipt and confirmed put-away within the same consistency boundary. Put-Away as an entity inside (not separate aggregate) prevents orphan "received but not stowed" states. |

---

### Aggregate 10: Supplier Invoice

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Supplier Invoice |
| **Included Entities** | None *(invoice lines are value objects)* |
| **Included Value Objects** | Invoice Line Detail (collection), Three-Way Match Result, Quantity Tolerance, Monetary Amount |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Three-way match must be confirmed among PO, goods receipt, and invoice within defined tolerance before payment authorization (BR-008). Payment for unordered, unreceived, or mispriced goods is prohibited. Invoice lines must reference products and quantities that exist on the linked PO and receipt. Match exceptions must be documented and resolved or waived by authorized approver before payment status transitions to authorized. |
| **Responsibilities** | Record supplier billing document. Execute three-way match evaluation against Purchase Order and Goods Receipt aggregates (referenced by identity). Track match status and payment authorization gate. Document match exceptions for finance resolution. |
| **Business Justification** | Invoice matching is a financial control boundary that compares three independent documents. The Supplier Invoice aggregate owns the match outcome — it consults PO and GR by identity but does not mutate them. This isolates financial approval workflow from operational receipt processing while enforcing BR-008 as a single coherent decision. |

---

## Bounded Context 4: Order Fulfillment

---

### Aggregate 11: Customer Order Fulfillment

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Customer Order |
| **Included Entities** | Inventory Reservation, Fulfillment Execution, Backorder, Shipment |
| **Included Value Objects** | Order Line Quantity (collection), Fulfillment Quantity Breakdown, Customer Acknowledgment, Pick Line Detail, Shipment Line Detail, Channel Designation, User Action Attribution |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Availability confirmation must use ATP only — not total on-hand (BR-001). Stock must be reserved at order confirmation; reserved quantity removed from ATP until fulfilled or released (BR-002). Reservation must reference active products at authorized locations. Safety stock and promotional ring-fence rules must be respected when reserving (BR-010, BR-029). Verified pick must complete before shipment recording — no ship without pick confirmation (BR-003). FEFO/FIFO rotation must be applied during pick line assignment (BR-014, BR-015). Lot/batch must be captured on pick for traceable products (BR-017). Backorder requires explicit customer acknowledgment before recording (BR-028). Partial fulfillment must decompose order line into fulfilled and backordered quantities consistently. Shipment deducts stock only after verified pick — emits domain event to Stock Position aggregate. Reservation release on cancellation must restore ATP via cross-aggregate command. |
| **Responsibilities** | Manage the complete customer order lifecycle from availability confirmation through reservation, pick/pack/ship, and partial/backorder handling. Coordinate ATP commitment and release with Stock Position aggregate. Enforce pick verification before shipment. Capture customer acknowledgment for backorders. Emit shipment events that trigger stock deduction. Provide order fulfillment status visibility. |
| **Business Justification** | Order confirmation, reservation, picking, and shipping are one coherent business transaction chain with tightly coupled state — a reservation without pick tracking or a shipment without reservation release creates overselling or phantom stock. Keeping these entities in one aggregate guarantees order line quantities reconcile: requested = reserved = picked + backordered + cancelled at every stage. Cross-aggregate calls to Stock Position handle ATP mechanics while the order aggregate owns fulfillment intent. |

---

## Bounded Context 5: Network Transfer

---

### Aggregate 12: Stock Transfer

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Stock Transfer *(Transfer Request is the initial state; approved request promotes to transfer execution within same aggregate)* |
| **Included Entities** | In-Transit Stock |
| **Included Value Objects** | Transfer Line Detail (collection), Quantity, Lot Identity, User Action Attribution, Approval Threshold (evaluated) |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Transfer must not deplete source below its minimum threshold — quantity limited to spare stock above source policy minimum (BR-012). Network availability must have been evaluated before transfer was initiated as alternative to purchase (BR-011). Safety stock at source must not be breached without authorized exception (BR-010). Transfer requires approval before dispatch when policy mandates. Lot/batch must be captured on transfer lines for traceable products (BR-017). Dispatch deducts source Stock Position; receipt at destination increases destination Stock Position — in-transit quantity tracked between. In-transit stock excluded from both source and destination ATP until receipt confirmed. Source and destination locations must not be frozen during dispatch/receipt. |
| **Responsibilities** | Manage inter-location transfer lifecycle: request, approval, dispatch, in-transit tracking, and receipt confirmation. Enforce source location minimum protection. Track in-transit inventory state. Coordinate stock deductions and additions across two Stock Position aggregates via domain events. |
| **Business Justification** | A transfer is a single business operation spanning two locations with three states (requested → in-transit → received). In-Transit Stock belongs inside because it is meaningless without the transfer that created it — splitting would orphan pipeline inventory. Source minimum enforcement (BR-012) requires evaluating source Stock Policy within the transfer decision, making the transfer aggregate the natural enforcement point before dispatch events fire. |

---

## Bounded Context 6: Inventory Accuracy

---

### Aggregate 13: Cycle Count

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Cycle Count |
| **Included Entities** | None *(count result and variance reference are value objects; variance investigation spawns separate aggregate)* |
| **Included Value Objects** | Quantity (physical count result), Quantity Variance, User Action Attribution |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Count must be performed blind — counter must not see system expected quantity before recording result (BR-018). Class A products must receive highest count frequency (BR-032). Physical count quantity must be non-negative. Count assignment must reference valid product and location. Count completion with variance must spawn an Inventory Adjustment Case aggregate — Cycle Count does not directly mutate Stock Position. Counter identity recorded and must differ from eventual approver (BR-019). |
| **Responsibilities** | Schedule and assign cycle count work. Enforce blind counting protocol. Record physical count result. Calculate variance against system quantity (evaluated at submission, not shown to counter). Initiate variance investigation workflow when variance exists. |
| **Business Justification** | Cycle count is a bounded operational task — assign, count, record. It deliberately does not adjust stock directly because BR-022 requires investigation before adjustment and BR-019 requires independent approval. Separating count from adjustment into different aggregates enforces segregation of duties by design. |

---

### Aggregate 14: Physical Inventory Count

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Physical Inventory Count |
| **Included Entities** | None *(count teams and location scope managed on root)* |
| **Included Value Objects** | Effective Period (freeze window), Quantity Variance (per line, collected), User Action Attribution |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Physical inventory freeze must apply during wall-to-wall count — no receiving, shipping, transfers, or adjustments at the location until count completed and verified (BR-024). Freeze state must be communicated to Inventory Location aggregate. Count must cover full location scope. Count certification requires all variances identified and routed to Inventory Adjustment Case aggregates. Location must return to active operational status only after count event is certified complete and freeze released. |
| **Responsibilities** | Orchestrate full wall-to-wall count at a location. Impose and release location freeze. Collect all line-level count results and variances. Certify count completion. Coordinate with Inventory Location aggregate for freeze enforcement. |
| **Business Justification** | Physical count is a location-wide event affecting every concurrent operation — BR-024 freeze is the defining invariant. This aggregate owns the count event and freeze lifecycle because only the count process knows when the location snapshot is stable. Individual variances still flow to adjustment cases rather than mutating stock during the count. |

---

### Aggregate 15: Inventory Adjustment Case

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Count Variance *(when originating from count)* or Stock Adjustment *(when direct adjustment)* — unified as **Adjustment Case** with polymorphic origin |
| **Included Entities** | Stock Adjustment, Inventory Write-Off |
| **Included Value Objects** | Quantity Variance, Reason Code Attribution, Condition Grade, Disposition Decision, Approval Threshold, Audit Quantity Snapshot, User Action Attribution, Valuation Line Amount |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Variances must be investigated before adjustment is applied — root cause analysis or documented effort required (BR-022). Counter must not approve adjustments from their own count (BR-019). Every adjustment requires a mandatory reason code (BR-020). Adjustments above threshold require independent approval by someone who did not initiate the underlying transaction (BR-021). Write-off requires documented evidence and authorized approval (BR-023). Adjustment and write-off must emit domain events to Stock Position aggregate for quantity mutation. Write-off is terminal — quantity permanently removed. Adjustment quantity must not drive stock negative. |
| **Responsibilities** | Investigate count variances and document findings. Process stock adjustments with reason code and approval chain. Process inventory write-offs with evidence and authorization. Enforce segregation of duties between initiator and approver. Trigger Stock Position mutations only upon approved, finalized adjustment or write-off. |
| **Business Justification** | Investigation, approval, and execution of inventory corrections form a governance workflow that must not be bypassed. Combining Count Variance, Stock Adjustment, and Write-Off in one case aggregate ensures BR-022 (investigate before adjusting) and BR-019/BR-021 (independent approval) are enforced as a single state machine: variance → investigation → approval → stock mutation. Stock Position remains the quantity owner — this aggregate owns the decision to change it. |

---

## Bounded Context 7: Returns

---

### Aggregate 16: Customer Return Case

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Return Authorization |
| **Included Entities** | Customer Return, Return Disposition |
| **Included Value Objects** | Condition Grade, Disposition Decision, Receipt Line Detail, Reason Code Attribution, User Action Attribution |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Return authorization required before warehouse acceptance — no receipt without valid RMA linked to original order (BR-025). Returned goods must be verified on receipt — quantity and product matched to authorization (BR-004). Returned goods must be inspected before restocking — condition assessment mandatory (BR-026). Restock to sellable inventory permitted only when condition grade confirms resale quality. Damaged or defective returns must be dispositioned to quarantine or write-off — never directly to ATP. Disposition emits domain event to Stock Position (restock increase) or Inventory Adjustment Case (write-off). Original order referenced by identity for policy validation. |
| **Responsibilities** | Issue return authorization linked to original customer order. Receive and verify returned goods against authorization. Inspect condition and decide disposition (restock, quarantine, write-off). Coordinate stock position increase or write-off initiation based on disposition. Track return processing status end-to-end. |
| **Business Justification** | Return authorization, physical receipt, inspection, and disposition are one reverse-logistics workflow with strict sequencing (BR-025 → BR-004 → BR-026). Combining them prevents unauthorized returns entering stock and prevents uninspected goods reaching sellable inventory. The RMA is the natural root because it gates all subsequent steps — without authorization, receipt and disposition cannot proceed. |

---

## Bounded Context 8: Commercial

---

### Aggregate 17: Promotional Stock Allocation

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | Promotional Stock Allocation |
| **Included Entities** | None |
| **Included Value Objects** | Campaign Period, Channel Designation, Quantity, Stock Availability Breakdown (ring-fenced portion) |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | Promotional stock must be ring-fenced during campaign — allocated quantity must not be consumed by non-promotional orders without commercial leadership approval (BR-029). Allocation quantity must not exceed available stock at allocation time. Ring-fenced quantity reduces general ATP on Stock Position while allocation is active. Allocation must define effective campaign period — inactive outside period. Readiness status must be confirmable before campaign commitment. Release of un consumed allocation after campaign end restores quantity to general ATP. |
| **Responsibilities** | Ring-fence defined quantity for a promotional campaign or launch. Protect allocated stock from non-promotional reservation. Support readiness review before campaign start. Release un consumed allocation on campaign end. Coordinate with Stock Position aggregate to segregate ATP. |
| **Business Justification** | Promotional ring-fencing is a commercial policy overlay on stock availability with its own lifecycle (campaign start/end) independent of order fulfillment mechanics. A dedicated aggregate allows marketing and commercial teams to manage allocations without coupling to individual Customer Order Fulfillment aggregates. BR-029 enforcement requires a single authority on what quantity is promotional vs. general — this aggregate is that authority. |

---

## Bounded Context 9: Identity & Access

---

### Aggregate 18: User Account

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Aggregate Root** | User Account |
| **Included Entities** | Role Assignment |
| **Included Value Objects** | User Action Attribution (template), Effective Period (assignment dates) |
| **Invariants (Business Rules)** | User identifier must be unique. Account must have at least one role assignment to perform system actions. Segregation-of-duties conflicts must be blocked — e.g., user cannot hold both cycle count operator and count approval roles simultaneously (BR-019, BR-021). Location scope on role assignment must reference valid active locations. Deactivated accounts must not authenticate or perform actions. Role changes must be effective-dated; prior assignments retained as history. |
| **Responsibilities** | Provision and manage user identity for inventory operations. Assign roles with location scope and permission boundaries. Enforce segregation-of-duties constraints at assignment time. Support account lifecycle (active, suspended, deactivated). Provide user identity context consumed by all aggregates for attribution. |
| **Business Justification** | User identity and role assignments change independently of inventory transactions but govern who may initiate and approve them. Centralizing access control in one aggregate ensures SoD rules (BR-019, BR-021) are evaluated consistently at role assignment — not re-implemented in each operational aggregate. Role Assignments belong inside because they have no meaning without the user account they belong to. |

---

## Cross-Aggregate Interaction Model

Aggregates coordinate through **domain events** and **identity references** — never through shared mutable state.

```
┌─────────────────────┐     PutAwayCompleted      ┌─────────────────────┐
│   Goods Receipt     │ ─────────────────────────►│   Stock Position    │
│   (Aggregate 9)     │     (product, location,   │   (Aggregate 5)     │
└─────────────────────┘      qty, lot)            └─────────────────────┘
                                                           ▲
┌─────────────────────┐     ReservationCommitted          │
│ Customer Order      │ ──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Fulfillment (11)    │     ShipmentDispatched (deduct)   │
└─────────────────────┘ ──────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────┐     TransferDispatched            │
│   Stock Transfer    │ ──────────────────────────────────┤
│   (Aggregate 12)    │     TransferReceived              │
└─────────────────────┘ ──────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────┐     AdjustmentApproved            │
│ Inventory Adjustment│ ──────────────────────────────────┘
│ Case (15)           │
└─────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────┐     RestockApproved               │
│ Customer Return     │ ──────────────────────────────────► Stock Position
│ Case (16)           │
└─────────────────────┘
```

### Interaction Rules

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **No cross-aggregate transaction** | Goods Receipt put-away and Stock Position update are eventual consistency via domain event |
| **Reference by identity** | Customer Order Fulfillment holds `productSku + locationCode`, not Stock Position object reference |
| **Consult, don't couple** | Stock Transfer consults Stock Policy and Stock Position by identity for source minimum check before dispatch |
| **Governance consultation** | All adjustment aggregates consult Inventory Governance for reason code validity and approval thresholds |
| **Catalog validation** | Procurement and fulfillment aggregates consult Product Catalog by SKU for lifecycle status before accepting lines |

## Excluded from Aggregate Design

The following domain concepts are intentionally **not** modeled as aggregates:

| Concept | Treatment | Rationale |
|---------|-----------|-----------|
| **Inventory Movement Record** | Domain event / append-only log | Immutable history produced by aggregates; not a consistency boundary |
| **Audit Trail Record** | Domain event / compliance log | Cross-cutting observation of aggregate mutations |
| **Operational Alert** | Read model / notification projection | Derived from threshold breaches; no transactional invariant |
| **Inventory Valuation Snapshot** | Reporting read model | Point-in-time projection for finance; rebuilt from Stock Position events |
