# Domain Entity Relationships
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-DM-004 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Entity Relationships — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entity Model, v1.0), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates, v1.0), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules, v1.0) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business relationships only — no database foreign keys, ORM mappings, or persistence design |

### Purpose

This document identifies **business relationships** between all 40 domain entities in the Inventory Management System. Each relationship expresses how entities collaborate in real operational workflows — ownership, dependency, modification, authorization, and derivation — independent of how any system stores or joins data.

### Relationship Type Legend

| Type | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Composition** | Target is a constituent part of source; target lifecycle is bound to source |
| **Association** | Ongoing business link; both entities exist independently |
| **Reference** | Source identifies or consults target by business identity without ownership |
| **Modification** | Source operation changes quantity, status, or availability of target |
| **Derivation** | Target is computed, triggered, or produced from source state or event |
| **Authorization** | Source permits, gates, or validates an action on target |
| **Verification** | Source is validated against target before proceeding |

### Multiplicity Notation

| Notation | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| **1** | Exactly one |
| **0..1** | Zero or one (optional) |
| **1..*** | One or more (mandatory, many allowed) |
| **0..*** | Zero or more (optional, many allowed) |
| *** ** | Many (zero or more) |

| Domain | Relationship IDs | Count |
|--------|------------------|-------|
| Master Data & Reference | REL-001 – REL-018 | 18 |
| Inventory State & Balance | REL-019 – REL-032 | 14 |

| Financial Alignment | REL-129 – REL-134 | 6 |
| **Total** | **REL-001 – REL-134** | **134** |

## Domain 1: Master Data & Reference

---

### REL-001

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Product |
| **Target Entity** | Stock Position |
| **Relationship Type** | Association |
| **Business Meaning** | Every stock balance tracks exactly one product; a product may be held at zero or many locations simultaneously. Product defines *what* is counted; Stock Position defines *how much* and *where*. |
| **Multiplicity** | Product **1** → Stock Position **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-027 — discontinued products must not receive new stock through procurement; existing Stock Positions may remain until depleted. BR-017 — traceable products require lot attribution on all Stock Position movements. |

---

### REL-002

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Product |
| **Target Entity** | Stock Policy |
| **Relationship Type** | Association |
| **Business Meaning** | Replenishment thresholds are defined per product (and per location on the policy). Product classification (ABC, rotation, shelf-life) determines how policy is applied and monitored. |
| **Multiplicity** | Product **1** → Stock Policy **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-009 — reorder action triggers when Stock Position ATP reaches product-location reorder level defined in Stock Policy. BR-032 — Class A products require highest monitoring intensity. |

---

### REL-003

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Product |
| **Target Entity** | Lot/Batch |
| **Relationship Type** | Composition |
| **Business Meaning** | For traceable products, lot/batch records are subordinate groupings of stock identity within a product scope. Lots cannot exist without a parent product definition. |
| **Multiplicity** | Product **1** → Lot/Batch **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-017 — lot identity must be captured at receipt and through all movements for traceable products. BR-014 — FEFO applies when product has shelf-life; BR-015 — FIFO for standard goods. |

---

### REL-004

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Inventory Location |
| **Target Entity** | Storage Position |
| **Relationship Type** | Composition |
| **Business Meaning** | Storage positions are physical subdivisions within a location (zones, bins, shelves). They cannot exist outside their parent location and are decommissioned when the location closes. |
| **Multiplicity** | Inventory Location **1** → Storage Position **1..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-005 — put-away assigns received goods to a Storage Position before Stock Position ATP increases. BR-024 — location freeze suspends put-away activity during Physical Inventory Count. |

---

### REL-005

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Inventory Location |
| **Target Entity** | Stock Position |
| **Relationship Type** | Association |
| **Business Meaning** | Stock balances are anchored to a location. A location holds zero or many product balances; each balance exists at exactly one location. |
| **Multiplicity** | Inventory Location **1** → Stock Position **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-012 — inter-location transfers must not deplete source location Stock Position below its Stock Policy minimum. BR-024 — location must be frozen during wall-to-wall count. |

---

### REL-006

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Inventory Location |
| **Target Entity** | Inventory Location *(parent)* |
| **Relationship Type** | Association *(hierarchy)* |
| **Business Meaning** | Locations form a network hierarchy (region → site → zone) for reporting roll-up and organizational accountability. A location may optionally belong to one parent location. |
| **Multiplicity** | Inventory Location *(child)* **0..1** → Inventory Location *(parent)* **1** ; parent **1** → children **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | A location cannot be its own parent or ancestor. Deactivated parent does not automatically deactivate children — each location has independent operational status. |

---

### REL-007

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Inventory Location |
| **Target Entity** | Physical Inventory Count |
| **Relationship Type** | Association |
| **Business Meaning** | A wall-to-wall count event applies to exactly one location. The count event imposes operational freeze on that location for its duration. |
| **Multiplicity** | Inventory Location **1** → Physical Inventory Count **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-024 — receiving, shipping, transfers, and adjustments suspended at location while Physical Inventory Count is active and uncertified. |

---

### REL-008

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Stock Policy |
| **Target Entity** | Product |
| **Relationship Type** | Reference |
| **Business Meaning** | Stock Policy is scoped to a specific product. The policy defines replenishment behavior for that SKU at a given location. |
| **Multiplicity** | Stock Policy **1** → Product **1** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-009 — reorder level on policy triggers replenishment when ATP breaches threshold. BR-010 — safety stock on policy must not be bypassed without authorized exception. |

---

### REL-009

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Stock Policy |
| **Target Entity** | Inventory Location |
| **Relationship Type** | Reference |
| **Business Meaning** | Stock Policy is scoped to a specific location. The same product may have different thresholds at different locations reflecting local demand and lead time. |
| **Multiplicity** | Stock Policy **1** → Inventory Location **1** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-012 — minimum threshold on source location policy constrains maximum transfer quantity. Product + Location combination uniquely identifies a Stock Policy. |

---

### REL-010

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Stock Policy |
| **Target Entity** | Operational Alert |
| **Relationship Type** | Derivation |
| **Business Meaning** | When Stock Position ATP crosses policy thresholds (reorder level, minimum, zero), the system derives low-stock or out-of-stock alerts for replenishment review. |
| **Multiplicity** | Stock Policy **1** → Operational Alert **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-009 — replenishment action must be initiated same business day when reorder level is reached. BR-032 — Class A products generate higher-priority alerts. |

---

### REL-011

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Reason Code |
| **Target Entity** | Stock Adjustment |
| **Relationship Type** | Authorization |
| **Business Meaning** | Every stock adjustment must cite a reason code explaining why the correction occurred. Reason code categorizes the adjustment for shrinkage analysis and audit. |
| **Multiplicity** | Reason Code **1** → Stock Adjustment **0..*** ; Stock Adjustment **1** → Reason Code **1** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-020 — no adjustment may be applied without a categorized reason code. Retired reason codes must not be used on new adjustments. |

---

### REL-012

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Reason Code |
| **Target Entity** | Inventory Write-Off |
| **Relationship Type** | Authorization |
| **Business Meaning** | Write-offs require a reason code documenting why inventory value is permanently removed (damage, obsolescence, loss). |
| **Multiplicity** | Reason Code **1** → Inventory Write-Off **0..*** ; Inventory Write-Off **1** → Reason Code **1** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-020, BR-023 — mandatory reason code plus documented evidence and authorization for write-offs. |

---

### REL-013

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Reason Code |
| **Target Entity** | Receipt Discrepancy |
| **Relationship Type** | Association |
| **Business Meaning** | Receipt discrepancies are categorized by reason code type (short shipment, damage, wrong item) to drive resolution workflow and supplier accountability. |
| **Multiplicity** | Reason Code **1** → Receipt Discrepancy **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-006 — discrepancies must be documented with supporting evidence before acceptance. |

---

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Governance Policy |
| **Target Entity** | Stock Adjustment |
| **Relationship Type** | Verification |
| **Business Meaning** | Governance policy defines approval thresholds that Stock Adjustment must satisfy before taking effect. Adjustments above threshold require independent approver per policy. |
| **Multiplicity** | Governance Policy **1** → Stock Adjustment **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-021 — adjustments above financial or quantity threshold require independent approval by authorized person who did not initiate underlying transaction. |

---

### REL-015

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Governance Policy |
| **Target Entity** | Count Variance |
| **Relationship Type** | Verification |

| **Multiplicity** | Governance Policy **1** → Count Variance **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-019 — person who performed count must not approve adjustments arising from their own count. |

### REL-016

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|

| **Target Entity** | Goods Receipt |
| **Relationship Type** | Verification |

| **Multiplicity** | Governance Policy **1** → Goods Receipt **0..*** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-007 — PO required except where explicitly approved ad-hoc exception applies per governance policy. |

### REL-017

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Source Entity** | Storage Position |
| **Target Entity** | Put-Away |
| **Relationship Type** | Association |
| **Business Meaning** | Put-away confirms placement of received goods into a designated storage position, making stock physically findable for picking. |
| **Multiplicity** | Storage Position **1** → Put-Away **0..*** ; Put-Away **1** → Storage Position **1** |
| **Business Rules** | BR-005 — stock not available until put-away to storage position is confirmed. BR-014, BR-015 — rotation placement at put-away. |

| **Business Rules** | BR-003 — pick must be verified before shipment. BR-014, BR-015 — FEFO/FIFO guides which storage position/lot is picked first. |

## Domain 3: Procurement & Inbound Supply

---

### REL-033

| **Source Entity** | Supplier |

| **Business Rules** | BR-022 — each variance investigated before adjustment. BR-024 — no movements during count that would invalidate snapshot. |

# Domain Services
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-DM-005 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Services — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | DDD Architect |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entity Model), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates), SRS-DM-004 (Entity Relationships), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Domain-layer business services only — no application services, infrastructure, APIs, or persistence |

### Purpose

This document identifies **Domain Services** for the Inventory Management System. A domain service encapsulates business logic that is essential to the domain but does not naturally belong to a single entity or aggregate root — typically because it **coordinates**, **evaluates**, or **computes** across multiple aggregates, entities, or value objects.

Domain services are **stateless** with respect to business identity: they operate on domain objects passed to them and enforce cross-cutting business rules that no single aggregate can own without creating improper coupling.

### Domain Service vs. Entity Responsibility

| Criterion | Belongs on Entity/Aggregate | Belongs in Domain Service |
|-----------|------------------------------|---------------------------|
| **Scope** | Single consistency boundary | Spans two or more aggregates |
| **State** | Owns lifecycle and identity | Stateless operation on passed objects |
| **Example** | Stock Position maintains its own ATP formula | Network availability sums ATP across many Stock Positions |

### Service Catalog Overview

| Domain Area | Services | IDs |
|-------------|----------|-----|
| Availability & Commitment | Availability Confirmation, Inventory Reservation Coordination, Multi-Location Fulfillment Allocation | DS-001 – DS-003 |
| Network & Replenishment | Network Availability Evaluation, Replenishment Recommendation, Transfer Capacity Evaluation, Network Rebalancing Analysis | DS-004 – DS-007 |
| Inbound & Procurement | Receipt Verification, Put-Away Activation, Three-Way Match Evaluation | DS-008 – DS-010 |
| Fulfillment Execution | Stock Rotation Selection, Shipment Completion Coordination, Partial Fulfillment & Backorder Orchestration | DS-011 – DS-013 |
| Inventory Control | Physical Inventory Freeze Guard, Adjustment Governance Evaluation, Count Variance Adjudication | DS-014 – DS-016 |
| Monitoring & Classification | Stock Status Classification, Low-Stock Alert Evaluation, Promotional Readiness Evaluation | DS-017 – DS-019 |
| Returns & Ownership | Return Eligibility & Disposition Routing, Consignment Ownership Evaluation | DS-020 – DS-021 |
| Financial & Governance | Inventory Valuation Reconciliation, Segregation of Duties Validation, Product Transaction Eligibility | DS-022 – DS-024 |

**Total Domain Services:** 24

---

## Domain 1: Availability & Commitment

---

### DS-001 — Availability Confirmation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Evaluate whether requested order quantities can be committed by consulting available-to-promise (ATP) across one or more Stock Positions, Promotional Stock Allocations, and Quarantine Holds. Returns a confirmation result indicating full availability, partial availability, or unavailability with per-line ATP breakdown. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Availability confirmation spans Customer Order, Stock Position (potentially multiple locations), Promotional Stock Allocation, and Product catalog validity. Customer Order does not own stock; Stock Position does not know about order context. Neither aggregate should embed the other's rules — confirmation is a cross-aggregate query and decision. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-001 (ATP-only customer commitment), BR-013 (quarantine exclusion from sellable stock), BR-029 (promotional ring-fencing), BR-027 (inactive/discontinued product blocking) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-013 (Inquire Inventory Availability), UC-021 (Confirm Order Availability), UC-048 (Support Multi-Location Split Fulfillment) |

---

### DS-002 — Inventory Reservation Coordination Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Orchestrate reservation of stock for confirmed customer order lines by coordinating Customer Order Fulfillment aggregate with one or more Stock Position aggregates. Validates safety stock protection, promotional ring-fence rules, and product eligibility before instructing Stock Positions to increase reserved quantity and decrease ATP. Handles reservation release on cancellation. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Reservation requires atomic business intent across order and stock boundaries — Customer Order Fulfillment owns the commercial commitment while Stock Position owns quantity state. Placing reservation logic entirely in either aggregate creates coupling: the order aggregate would mutate foreign stock, or stock would need order context. Coordination is inherently a domain service operation. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-002 (reservation at order confirmation), BR-010 (safety stock protection), BR-029 (promotional stock ring-fencing), BR-001 (ATP-only commitment) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-022 (Reserve Inventory for Confirmed Orders), UC-023 (Release Inventory Reservations), UC-025 (Handle Partial Fulfillment and Backorders) |

---

### DS-003 — Multi-Location Fulfillment Allocation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | When a single location cannot satisfy order quantity, determine optimal split allocation across network Stock Positions based on ATP, fulfillment cost proximity, and location operational status. Produces a fulfillment plan assigning order line quantities to one or more ship-from locations. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Split fulfillment requires simultaneous evaluation of ATP at multiple locations, transfer feasibility, and order line decomposition — no single Stock Position or Customer Order aggregate has network-wide visibility. Location selection is a policy-driven optimization across the network, not a property of any one entity. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-001 (commit only against ATP at each location), BR-002 (reservation per allocated location), BR-012 (source minimum if transfer needed as fallback) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-048 (Support Multi-Location Split Fulfillment), UC-021 (Confirm Order Availability), UC-024 (Pick, Pack, and Ship Orders) |

---

## Domain 2: Network & Replenishment

---

### DS-004 — Network Availability Evaluation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Before initiating procurement or approving a transfer request, evaluate network-wide stock availability — summing ATP and in-transit quantities across all locations for a product — to determine whether local shortage can be resolved by redistribution rather than new purchase. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Network evaluation aggregates data from Stock Positions at many locations, In-Transit Stock records, and Expected Inbound Deliveries. No single location-scoped Stock Position or Purchase Requisition aggregate should own network-wide logic — that would violate aggregate boundaries and create a god entity. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-011 (network check before purchase), BR-012 (protect source location minimum when evaluating transfer alternative) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-029 (Plan Replenishment and Create Purchase Requisitions), UC-031 (Request Inter-Location Stock Transfer), UC-034 (Analyze and Recommend Network Rebalancing), UC-028 (Review Low-Stock and Out-of-Stock Alerts) |

---

### DS-005 — Replenishment Recommendation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Generate replenishment recommendations when Stock Position ATP breaches Stock Policy thresholds. Considers reorder level, safety stock, inbound expected supply, network excess at other locations, product lifecycle status, and ABC classification priority. Recommends purchase requisition, transfer request, or no action. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Replenishment decisions synthesize Stock Policy (product-location), Stock Position (current ATP), Expected Inbound Delivery (pipeline), Product (discontinued status, ABC class), and network availability. Stock Policy defines thresholds but should not scan all positions; Stock Position holds quantity but not replenishment authority. The recommendation is a derived cross-domain judgment. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-009 (reorder at reorder level), BR-010 (safety stock protection), BR-011 (network check before purchase), BR-027 (no reorder of discontinued products), BR-032 (Class A priority monitoring) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-028 (Review Low-Stock and Out-of-Stock Alerts), UC-029 (Plan Replenishment and Create Purchase Requisitions), UC-047 (Receive and Respond to Operational Notifications) |

---

### DS-006 — Transfer Capacity Evaluation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Calculate the maximum transferable quantity from a source location for a given product without breaching Stock Policy minimum threshold or safety stock buffer. Used during transfer request creation and approval to enforce source location protection. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Transfer capacity requires reading source Stock Position ATP/on-hand, source Stock Policy thresholds, and existing reservations — then computing spare quantity. Stock Transfer aggregate should not own source policy rules; Stock Policy aggregate should not know about transfer requests. The calculation is a stateless evaluation spanning source stock and policy. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-012 (protect source location minimum), BR-010 (safety stock protection) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-031 (Request Inter-Location Stock Transfer), UC-032 (Approve or Reject Transfer Requests), UC-033 (Execute and Record Inter-Location Transfer) |

---

### DS-007 — Network Rebalancing Analysis Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Analyze network-wide stock distribution for a product or category to identify imbalance patterns — locations with stockout risk alongside locations with excess — and recommend redistribution transfers. Supports proactive rebalancing before stockouts occur. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Rebalancing analysis compares Stock Positions and Stock Policies across the entire location network, identifying pairwise transfer opportunities. This network optimization view belongs to no single location, product, or transfer entity — it is an analytical domain operation over multiple aggregates. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-011 (network check before purchase), BR-012 (protect source location minimum), BR-009 (reorder level context for imbalance severity) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-034 (Analyze and Recommend Network Rebalancing), UC-031 (Request Inter-Location Stock Transfer), UC-012 (Monitor Inventory Status) |

---

## Domain 3: Inbound & Procurement

---

### DS-008 — Receipt Verification Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Verify inbound goods against Purchase Order lines, Product catalog (identity, traceability requirements), and Governance Policy (tolerance limits). Validates minimum remaining shelf life (MRSL) for shelf-life products, captures lot/batch requirements, and determines whether receipt discrepancies must be raised before acceptance. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Verification compares Goods Receipt data against Purchase Order (separate aggregate), Product (catalog aggregate), and Governance Policy (reference aggregate). Goods Receipt should record outcome but not own PO matching rules, MRSL policy from Product, or tolerance from Governance — those are cross-aggregate validations. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-004 (verify before inventory acceptance), BR-006 (document receipt discrepancies), BR-007 (PO required for supplier receipt), BR-016 (minimum remaining shelf life at receipt), BR-017 (lot/batch capture for traceable products) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-008 (Receive and Verify Supplier Goods), UC-009 (Document and Resolve Receipt Discrepancies), UC-011 (Receive Return and Non-PO Inbound Stock) |

---

### DS-009 — Put-Away Activation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Upon put-away confirmation, coordinate availability activation by validating bonded/customs clearance status (Quarantine Hold), assigning rotation-compliant storage position, and instructing the target Stock Position aggregate to increase on-hand quantity. Ensures stock does not become sellable until all preconditions are satisfied. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Put-away completion touches Goods Receipt (put-away entity), Storage Position (location aggregate), Quarantine Hold (stock aggregate), and Stock Position (quantity increase). Goods Receipt owns receipt workflow but should not directly mutate Stock Position; Stock Position should not embed put-away or customs rules. Activation is the cross-aggregate handoff point. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-005 (put-away before availability), BR-030 (bonded inventory customs clearance), BR-014 (FEFO rotation placement), BR-015 (FIFO rotation placement) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-010 (Perform Stock Put-Away), UC-008 (Receive and Verify Supplier Goods), UC-019 (Manage Quarantine and Hold Stock) |

---

### DS-010 — Three-Way Match Evaluation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Compare Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, and Supplier Invoice lines within Governance Policy tolerance limits. Determine match status (matched, quantity exception, price exception, unmatched) and whether payment authorization may proceed. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Three-way match is a financial control operation spanning three independent aggregates (Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Supplier Invoice) plus Governance Policy tolerances. None of the three document aggregates should own the comparison logic — each would create improper dependency on the other two. Match evaluation is a classic domain service. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-008 (three-way match before payment), BR-006 (receipt discrepancies affect match outcome) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-039 (Reconcile Inventory Valuation with Finance), UC-006 (Place and Manage Purchase Orders), UC-008 (Receive and Verify Supplier Goods) |

---

## Domain 4: Fulfillment Execution

---

### DS-011 — Stock Rotation Selection Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | For pick and put-away operations, select the correct lot/batch or oldest stock based on Product rotation policy (FIFO for standard goods, FEFO for shelf-life products). Returns recommended pick source (storage position and lot) from available Stock Position and Lot/Batch data at a location. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Rotation selection compares multiple Lot/Batch records under a Stock Position against Product rotation policy — a decision spanning Product (policy), Lot/Batch (expiration dates), Storage Position (physical location), and Fulfillment Execution (pick context). No single entity owns the selection algorithm without duplicating policy from Product into warehouse entities. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-014 (FEFO rotation for shelf-life products), BR-015 (FIFO rotation for standard goods), BR-017 (lot/batch capture on selected stock) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-024 (Pick, Pack, and Ship Orders), UC-010 (Perform Stock Put-Away), UC-026 (Handle Outbound Fulfillment Exceptions) |

---

### DS-012 — Shipment Completion Coordination Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Upon verified pick confirmation, coordinate shipment recording by instructing Stock Position to deduct on-hand quantity, Customer Order Fulfillment to consume Inventory Reservation, and movement history to be recorded. Validates that pick verification preceded dispatch. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Shipment completion is the cross-aggregate moment where Fulfillment Execution, Shipment, Stock Position, and Inventory Reservation must align. Shipment entity records dispatch but should not own stock deduction; Stock Position deducts but should not know order fulfillment state. Coordination ensures BR-003 is enforced across boundaries. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-003 (verified pick before shipment), BR-002 (reservation consumed on shipment), BR-017 (lot captured on outbound movement) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-024 (Pick, Pack, and Ship Orders), UC-027 (View Order Fulfillment Status), UC-026 (Handle Outbound Fulfillment Exceptions) |

---

### DS-013 — Partial Fulfillment and Backorder Orchestration Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | When full order quantity cannot be fulfilled, decompose order lines into fulfillable and backordered quantities, validate customer acknowledgment for backorder remainder, and coordinate partial reservation, partial shipment, and backorder recording within Customer Order Fulfillment aggregate while updating Stock Positions for fulfilled portion only. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Partial fulfillment spans availability confirmation (ATP check), reservation (partial quantity), backorder (customer acknowledgment), and shipment (partial dispatch) — each touching different aggregates with distinct lifecycle rules. Backorder acknowledgment (BR-028) is a commercial rule that neither Stock Position nor Shipment alone should own. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-028 (backorder customer acknowledgment), BR-001 (ATP-only for fulfillable portion), BR-002 (partial reservation) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-025 (Handle Partial Fulfillment and Backorders), UC-021 (Confirm Order Availability), UC-022 (Reserve Inventory for Confirmed Orders) |

---

## Domain 5: Inventory Control

---

### DS-014 — Physical Inventory Freeze Guard Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Before any stock mutation operation (receipt, shipment, transfer, adjustment), verify that the target Inventory Location is not under an active Physical Inventory Count freeze. Blocks unauthorized mutations and permits only authorized count-related adjustments during freeze period. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Freeze state belongs to Physical Inventory Count and Inventory Location aggregates, but enforcement must intercept operations initiated by Goods Receipt, Stock Transfer, Customer Order Fulfillment, and Inventory Adjustment Case — four separate aggregates. No mutating aggregate should own freeze enforcement without coupling to count lifecycle. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-024 (physical inventory freeze during wall-to-wall count) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-015 (Conduct Full Physical Inventory Count), UC-008 (Receive and Verify Supplier Goods), UC-024 (Pick, Pack, and Ship Orders), UC-033 (Execute and Record Inter-Location Transfer), UC-017 (Process Stock Adjustments) |

---

### DS-015 — Adjustment Governance Evaluation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Evaluate whether a proposed Stock Adjustment or Inventory Write-Off satisfies governance requirements: mandatory reason code validity, financial/quantity approval threshold from Governance Policy, and segregation of duties (initiator distinct from required approver). Returns approval requirement and authorization outcome. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Governance evaluation consults Inventory Governance (thresholds, reason codes), Inventory Adjustment Case (proposed change), and User Account (initiator/approver identities). Adjustment aggregate should not embed policy thresholds that change independently; Governance Policy should not know about specific adjustment instances. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-020 (mandatory adjustment reason codes), BR-021 (independent approval for material adjustments), BR-022 (investigate before adjusting), BR-023 (documented write-off authorization) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-017 (Process Stock Adjustments), UC-018 (Authorize and Process Inventory Write-Offs), UC-016 (Investigate and Approve Count Variances) |

---

### DS-016 — Count Variance Adjudication Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Adjudicate count variances by comparing Cycle Count or Physical Inventory Count results against Stock Position system quantity, enforcing blind count protocol (variance calculated at submission only), validating investigation completion, and confirming approver independence from counter before authorizing adjustment creation. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Adjudication connects Cycle Count (count result), Stock Position (system quantity), Count Variance (discrepancy), User Account (counter vs. approver), and Inventory Adjustment Case (correction). Cycle Count should not mutate Stock Position directly; Stock Position should not know count protocol. Adjudication is the governed bridge between count and correction domains. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-018 (blind cycle counting), BR-019 (independent count approval), BR-022 (investigate before adjusting) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-014 (Perform Cycle Count), UC-015 (Conduct Full Physical Inventory Count), UC-016 (Investigate and Approve Count Variances) |

---

## Domain 6: Monitoring & Classification

---

### DS-017 — Stock Status Classification Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Classify a Stock Position as in stock, low stock, out of stock, or overstock by comparing current ATP and on-hand quantities against Stock Policy thresholds (reorder level, minimum, maximum). Applies ABC classification weighting for alert priority where configured. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Classification derives status from two aggregates — Stock Position (quantities) and Stock Policy (thresholds) — plus Product (ABC class). Stock Position could compute a local indicator but should not own policy thresholds; Stock Policy defines limits but not current quantities. Classification is a derived cross-aggregate evaluation refreshed on quantity or policy changes. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-009 (reorder at reorder level), BR-032 (Class A priority monitoring) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-012 (Monitor Inventory Status), UC-013 (Inquire Inventory Availability), UC-028 (Review Low-Stock and Out-of-Stock Alerts) |

---

### DS-018 — Low-Stock Alert Evaluation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Scan Stock Positions against Stock Policies across the network to detect threshold breaches and generate or update Operational Alerts. Applies Class A priority escalation rules and suppresses duplicate alerts for acknowledged conditions. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Alert generation is a network-wide batch evaluation over many Stock Position and Stock Policy pairs — not a responsibility of any single position or policy. Operational Alert is a derived notification entity; the evaluation logic that creates it spans the monitoring domain without belonging to the alert itself. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-009 (reorder at reorder level — same business day action), BR-032 (Class A priority monitoring) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-028 (Review Low-Stock and Out-of-Stock Alerts), UC-047 (Receive and Respond to Operational Notifications), UC-012 (Monitor Inventory Status) |

---

### DS-019 — Promotional Readiness Evaluation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Evaluate whether Promotional Stock Allocation ring-fenced quantity is sufficient for upcoming campaign requirements by comparing allocated ATP against campaign demand forecast and effective campaign period. Identifies readiness gaps and triggers readiness alerts. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Readiness evaluation crosses Promotional Stock Allocation (ring-fenced quantity), Stock Position (actual availability), Product (campaign SKU), and campaign period parameters. Marketing readiness is a commercial judgment spanning inventory and campaign entities — neither aggregate owns the full readiness question. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-029 (promotional stock ring-fencing), BR-001 (general ATP separate from promotional pool) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-040 (Confirm Promotional and Launch Stock Readiness), UC-047 (Receive and Respond to Operational Notifications), UC-022 (Reserve Inventory for Confirmed Orders) |

---

## Domain 7: Returns & Ownership

---

### DS-020 — Return Eligibility and Disposition Routing Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Validate return eligibility by matching Return Authorization against original Customer Order lines and return policy. Upon inspection, route returned goods to the correct outcome — restock (Stock Position increase), quarantine (Quarantine Hold), or write-off (Inventory Write-Off) — based on condition assessment. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Return processing spans Return Authorization, Customer Order, Customer Return, Return Disposition, Stock Position, Quarantine Hold, and Inventory Write-Off. Customer Return records receipt but should not own disposition routing rules; Stock Position should not embed return policy. Routing is a cross-aggregate orchestration of reverse logistics. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-025 (return authorization required), BR-026 (inspect returns before restocking), BR-004 (verify before acceptance), BR-013 (quarantine exclusion), BR-023 (write-off authorization) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-035 (Authorize and Record Customer Returns), UC-036 (Receive, Inspect, and Disposition Returned Goods), UC-011 (Receive Return and Non-PO Inbound Stock) |

---

### DS-021 — Consignment Ownership Evaluation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Determine ownership classification (owned vs. consignment) for stock at receipt and at consumption/sale events based on Supplier consignment agreement. Governs whether Stock Position quantity counts toward owned valuation and when ownership transfer triggers financial recording. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Ownership determination consults Supplier (consignment agreement), Goods Receipt (inbound context), Stock Position (current classification), and Shipment (consumption event). Supplier owns commercial terms; Stock Position holds physical quantity — neither should fully own the ownership transfer decision that affects finance (Inventory Valuation Snapshot). |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-031 (consignment ownership at consumption) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-039 (Reconcile Inventory Valuation with Finance), UC-008 (Receive and Verify Supplier Goods), UC-024 (Pick, Pack, and Ship Orders) |

---

## Domain 8: Financial & Governance

---

### DS-022 — Inventory Valuation Reconciliation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Produce Inventory Valuation Snapshot by aggregating owned Stock Position quantities (excluding consignment, quarantined, and in-transit per policy), applying unit costs from matched Supplier Invoices, and comparing result against general ledger expectations to identify reconciliation variances. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Valuation reconciliation synthesizes Stock Positions (quantities, ownership), Supplier Invoices (costs), Inventory Write-Offs (period reductions), and Quarantine/In-Transit exclusions into a point-in-time financial view. No operational entity should own finance reconciliation — it is a derived cross-domain computation. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-008 (three-way match — cost authority), BR-031 (consignment exclusion from owned valuation) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-039 (Reconcile Inventory Valuation with Finance), UC-037 (Review Inventory Dashboards and Operational Reports), UC-038 (Review Inventory Performance KPIs) |

---

### DS-023 — Segregation of Duties Validation Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Validate that a proposed action does not violate segregation-of-duties rules by checking User Account role assignments — e.g., counter cannot approve own count variance, initiator cannot approve own material adjustment, conflicting roles not held simultaneously. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | SoD validation compares the acting user and proposed approver against User Account role assignments and Governance Policy rules across unrelated transactions (count, adjustment, write-off). Individual transaction entities should not embed user role logic — identity governance is a cross-cutting domain concern. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-019 (independent count approval), BR-021 (independent approval for material adjustments), BR-023 (write-off authorization by authorized person) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-016 (Investigate and Approve Count Variances), UC-017 (Process Stock Adjustments), UC-018 (Authorize and Process Inventory Write-Offs), UC-045 (Enforce Role-Based and Location-Scoped Access), UC-041 (Conduct Inventory Audit and Control Review) |

---

### DS-024 — Product Transaction Eligibility Service

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Business Responsibility** | Validate that a product is eligible for a proposed transaction type — purchase, reservation, fulfillment, or replenishment — based on Product lifecycle status (active, inactive, discontinued) and any authorized exceptions recorded in Governance Policy. |
| **Why It Should Not Belong to an Entity** | Eligibility checks Product catalog status against transaction context from Purchase Order, Customer Order, or Purchase Requisition. Product owns its status but should not know all transaction types that consume it; transaction aggregates should not duplicate lifecycle rules. Centralized eligibility prevents inconsistent enforcement of BR-027 across procurement and fulfillment. |
| **Related Business Rules** | BR-027 (no reorder of discontinued products) |
| **Related Use Cases** | UC-006 (Place and Manage Purchase Orders), UC-022 (Reserve Inventory for Confirmed Orders), UC-029 (Plan Replenishment and Create Purchase Requisitions), UC-001 (Manage Product Master Data) |

# Domain Events
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-DM-006 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Events — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entity Model), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates), SRS-DM-005 (Domain Services), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog) |
| **Date** | July 5, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business domain events only — no message brokers, event buses, or integration technology |

### Purpose

This document identifies **Domain Events** for the Inventory Management System. A domain event is an immutable record of something meaningful that happened in the business — expressed in past tense from the domain's ubiquitous language. Events announce state changes within aggregates and enable loose coupling between aggregates, read models, and downstream business reactions.

Domain events are **facts**, not commands. They describe what occurred; consumers decide how to respond.

### Event Naming Convention

Events are named in **PascalCase past tense**: `StockReserved`, `PutAwayCompleted`, `CountVarianceIdentified`. Each name should be understandable to business stakeholders without technical context.

### Consumer Types

| Consumer Type | Role |
|---------------|------|
| **Aggregate** | Another consistency boundary that reacts by updating its own state |
| **Domain Service** | Stateless evaluator triggered to apply cross-aggregate business rules |
| **Read Model / Projection** | Derived view rebuilt from events (movement history, alerts, dashboards) |
| **Business Process** | Human workflow or notification triggered for actor action |

---

## Event Catalog Overview

| Domain Area | Events | IDs |
|-------------|--------|-----|
| Catalog & Network | Product and location lifecycle | DE-001 – DE-010 |
| Inventory Balance | Stock quantity and hold state | DE-011 – DE-022 |
| Procurement & Inbound | Requisition through receipt | DE-023 – DE-035 |
| Order Fulfillment | Order commitment through shipment | DE-036 – DE-045 |
| Network Transfer | Inter-location movement | DE-046 – DE-051 |
| Inventory Control | Counting and correction | DE-052 – DE-060 |
| Returns | Reverse logistics | DE-061 – DE-067 |
| Commercial & Monitoring | Promotions and alerts | DE-068 – DE-073 |
| Financial & Governance | Finance alignment and audit | DE-074 – DE-081 |

**Total Domain Events:** 81

## Domain 1: Catalog & Network

---

### DE-001 — ProductRegistered

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller creates a new product record with unique SKU, name, and unit of measure in the Product Catalog aggregate. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Product Catalog |
| **Business Meaning** | The organization has introduced a new SKU into the trusted product catalog. The product is now eligible for stock policy assignment, procurement, and (when active) fulfillment referencing. |
| **Consumers** | Stock Policy aggregate *(policy may be assigned)*; Read Model — product catalog index; Business Process — master data notification to operational teams |

---

### DE-002 — ProductStatusChanged

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | Product lifecycle status transitions among active, inactive, or discontinued within the Product Catalog aggregate. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Product Catalog |
| **Business Meaning** | The commercial availability of a SKU has changed. Discontinued status prohibits new procurement and reservations; inactive status restricts new customer commitments. |
| **Consumers** | Product Transaction Eligibility domain service *(DS-024)*; Purchase Order aggregate *(blocks new lines)*; Customer Order Fulfillment aggregate *(blocks new reservations)*; Replenishment Recommendation domain service *(DS-005)*; Read Model — product status history |

---

### DE-003 — ProductABCClassificationAssigned

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | Inventory Controller assigns or updates ABC classification (A, B, or C) on a product during classification review. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Product Catalog |
| **Business Meaning** | Operational priority for the SKU has been set. Class A products receive highest count frequency, monitoring intensity, and alert priority per BR-032. |
| **Consumers** | Cycle Count aggregate *(scheduling priority)*; Low-Stock Alert Evaluation domain service *(DS-018)*; Read Model — ABC classification report |

---

### DE-004 — InventoryLocationActivated

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | Inventory Location transitions to active operational status after opening balance approval at go-live. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Inventory Location |
| **Business Meaning** | A location is authorized to receive, hold, fulfill, and transact inventory. Stock positions may be established and operational workflows enabled. |
| **Consumers** | Stock Position aggregate *(opening balances created)*; Read Model — location network index; Business Process — go-live notification to warehouse team |

---

### DE-005 — InventoryLocationDeactivated

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | Inventory Location is deactivated after stock disposition is complete or closure is authorized. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Inventory Location |
| **Business Meaning** | A location is no longer authorized for new inventory activity. Existing stock must have been cleared or dispositioned before deactivation. |
| **Consumers** | Physical Inventory Freeze Guard domain service *(DS-014)*; Purchase Order aggregate *(blocks new receiving)*; Customer Order Fulfillment aggregate *(blocks new fulfillment)*; Read Model — location status history |

---

### DE-006 — StoragePositionConfigured

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | New storage position (zone, aisle, bin) is added or updated within an Inventory Location aggregate. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Inventory Location |
| **Business Meaning** | A findable physical address within a location is available for put-away placement and pick path guidance. |
| **Consumers** | Put-Away Activation domain service *(DS-009)*; Stock Rotation Selection domain service *(DS-011)*; Read Model — warehouse layout reference |

---

### DE-007 — LocationFreezeImposed

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | Physical Inventory Count aggregate begins wall-to-wall count at a location, imposing operational freeze. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Physical Inventory Count |
| **Business Meaning** | All receiving, shipping, transfers, and adjustments at the location are suspended until the count is certified complete. Ensures stable snapshot for accurate counting per BR-024. |
| **Consumers** | Physical Inventory Freeze Guard domain service *(DS-014)*; Goods Receipt aggregate *(blocks receipt)*; Customer Order Fulfillment aggregate *(blocks shipment)*; Stock Transfer aggregate *(blocks dispatch/receipt)*; Inventory Adjustment Case aggregate *(blocks non-count adjustments)*; Business Process — freeze notification to warehouse staff |

---

### DE-008 — LocationFreezeReleased

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | Physical Inventory Count aggregate certifies count completion and releases location freeze. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Physical Inventory Count |
| **Business Meaning** | Normal inventory operations may resume at the location. Count variances have been identified and routed for investigation. |
| **Consumers** | Physical Inventory Freeze Guard domain service *(DS-014)*; Business Process — operations resume notification to warehouse staff |

---

### DE-009 — GovernancePolicyPublished

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | New or updated governance policy version becomes effective in the Inventory Governance aggregate (approval thresholds, tolerances, exception rules). |
| **Related Aggregate** | Inventory Governance |
| **Business Meaning** | Organization-wide inventory control parameters have changed. All subsequent transactions must evaluate against the new effective policy. |
| **Consumers** | Adjustment Governance Evaluation domain service *(DS-015)*; Receipt Verification domain service *(DS-008)*; Three-Way Match Evaluation domain service *(DS-010)*; Read Model — policy version history |

---

### DE-010 — ReasonCodeRetired

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Trigger** | A reason code is marked retired in the Inventory Governance aggregate and removed from active selection lists. |
| **Related Aggregate** | Inventory Governance |
| **Business Meaning** | A categorized exception reason is no longer valid for new transactions. Historical records retain prior reason code attributions unchanged. |
| **Consumers** | Adjustment Governance Evaluation domain service *(DS-015)*; Read Model — reason code catalog |

## Event Flow — Core Business Lifecycles

### Inbound Supply Lifecycle

```
PurchaseOrderPlaced → InboundDeliveryScheduled → GoodsReceiptVerified
    → [ReceiptDiscrepancyRecorded → ReceiptDiscrepancyResolved]
    → PutAwayCompleted → StockReceived → InventoryMovementRecorded
    → SupplierInvoiceReceived → ThreeWayMatchCompleted
```

### Order Fulfillment Lifecycle

```
OrderAvailabilityConfirmed → CustomerOrderConfirmed → StockReserved
    → PickVerified → ShipmentDispatched → StockShipped → InventoryMovementRecorded
    → [PartialFulfillmentCompleted → BackorderRecorded → BackorderFulfilled]
```

### Inventory Accuracy Lifecycle

```
CycleCountScheduled → CycleCountCompleted → CountVarianceIdentified
    → CountVarianceApproved → AdjustmentSubmitted → AdjustmentApproved
    → StockAdjusted → InventoryMovementRecorded → AuditTrailRecorded
```

### Network Transfer Lifecycle

```
TransferRequested → TransferApproved → TransferDispatched → TransferReceived
    → StockReceived (destination) → InventoryMovementRecorded
```

## Excluded from Domain Events

| Occurrence | Treatment | Rationale |
|------------|-----------|-----------|
| User clicks "Search" on inventory screen | UI interaction | No business state change |
| Report query executed | Read operation | Queries do not change domain state |
| Validation failure (business rule rejected) | Rejection response | Nothing happened — state unchanged |
| Scheduled job timer fired | Infrastructure | Timer is not a business event; the resulting state change emits the event |
| Email delivery confirmed | Infrastructure | Notification delivery is not inventory domain concern |

# Part V — Event Storming

# Actors and External Systems
## Inventory Management System — Event Storming

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-ES-004 |
| **Document Title** | Actors and External Systems — Event Storming Catalog |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-ES-001 (Domain Events), SRS-ES-002 (Domain Commands), SRS-ES-003 (Domain Policies), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog) |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business participants only — humans and external systems outside the inventory domain core; excludes internal aggregate handlers |

### Purpose

This document identifies all **Actors** (human business roles) and **External Systems** (organizations and systems outside the Inventory Management System boundary) involved in event storming. For each participant it defines responsibilities, commands they initiate, and domain events they consume or react to in the course of business workflows.

### Participant Types

| Type | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Human** | Business role with accountability for inventory decisions and operations |
| **External System** | Organization or system outside the IMS bounded context that exchanges business facts or triggers workflows |

### Participant Summary

| Category | IDs | Count |
|----------|-----|-------|
| Human Actors | ACT-001 – ACT-017 | 17 |
| External Systems | EXT-001 – EXT-006 | 6 |
| **Total** | | **23** |

### Legend — Events Consumed

"Events consumed" means the participant **acts upon**, **is notified of**, or **depends on** the business fact — via work queue, alert, dashboard, integration, or policy notification. Read-only inquiry events are included where the participant routinely monitors them for decisions.

# Domain Commands
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-ES-002 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Commands — Event Storming Catalog |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-ES-001 (Domain Events), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog), SRS-UC-002 (Main Flows) |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business commands that mutate domain state and initiate domain events — no queries, UI actions, or infrastructure signals |

### Purpose

This document identifies **all domain commands** that initiate domain events in the Inventory Management System. A command expresses a **business intention** — what the organization wants to happen. Commands are imperative, issued by a business actor (human or policy-driven evaluator), and target exactly one aggregate per transaction.

Commands that fail validation emit **no domain event** — the aggregate state remains unchanged. When segregation-of-duties rules block an action, `SegregationOfDutiesViolationDetected` (DE-078) is raised instead of the intended event.

### Command Naming Convention

Commands use **PascalCase imperative verbs**: `RegisterProduct`, `ReserveStock`, `ApproveTransferRequest`.

### Command Categories

| Category | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **Actor Command** | Issued directly by a business role through a use case |
| **Policy Command** | Issued by a domain service when business rules or thresholds are evaluated |
| **Reaction Command** | Issued by an aggregate handler consuming a domain event from another aggregate |

### Command Catalog Summary

| Domain Area | Command IDs | Count |
|-------------|-------------|-------|
| Catalog & Network | CMD-001 – CMD-010 | 10 |
| Inventory Balance | CMD-011 – CMD-020 | 10 |
| Procurement & Inbound | CMD-021 – CMD-033 | 13 |
| Order Fulfillment | CMD-034 – CMD-044 | 11 |
| Network Transfer | CMD-045 – CMD-050 | 6 |
| Inventory Control & Accuracy | CMD-051 – CMD-060 | 10 |
| Returns Management | CMD-061 – CMD-067 | 7 |
| Commercial & Monitoring | CMD-068 – CMD-072 | 5 |
| Financial & Governance | CMD-073 – CMD-078 | 6 |
| **Total** | | **78** |

## Excluded from Domain Commands

| Action | Treatment | Rationale |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| SearchProduct, ViewInventory, QueryAuditTrail | Query | Read-only — no state mutation |

| Failed validation (rule rejected) | Rejection response | Aggregate unchanged — no event |
| Login, Logout | Identity infrastructure | Outside inventory domain boundary |
| SendEmail, DeliverNotification | Infrastructure | Delivery channel is not a business command |

# Domain Events — Event Storming Catalog
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-ES-001 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Events — Event Storming Catalog |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-DM-001 (Domain Entities), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates), SRS-DM-006 (Domain Events), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog), SRS-UC-002 (Main Flows) |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business domain events only — no message brokers, integration technology, or UI interactions |

### Purpose

This document identifies **all domain events** for the Inventory Management System as derived from the domain model and use cases. Each event records a meaningful business fact expressed in **past tense**. Events are raised by aggregates after successful command execution and describe **what happened**, not what should happen next.

### Conventions

| Element | Convention |
|---------|------------|
| **Event ID** | `DE-xxx` — sequential identifier |
| **Event Name** | PascalCase past tense (e.g., `StockReserved`) |
| **Aggregate** | The consistency boundary that raises the event |
| **Triggering Command** | Imperative business command that caused the state change |
| **Resulting Business State** | Authoritative post-condition after the event is applied |

### Event Catalog Summary

| Domain Area | Event IDs | Count |
|-------------|-----------|-------|
| Catalog & Network | DE-001 – DE-010 | 10 |
| Inventory Balance | DE-011 – DE-022 | 12 |
| Procurement & Inbound | DE-023 – DE-035 | 13 |
| Order Fulfillment | DE-036 – DE-045 | 10 |
| Network Transfer | DE-046 – DE-051 | 6 |
| Inventory Control & Accuracy | DE-052 – DE-060 | 9 |
| Returns Management | DE-061 – DE-067 | 7 |
| Commercial & Monitoring | DE-068 – DE-073 | 6 |
| Financial & Governance | DE-074 – DE-081 | 8 |
| **Total** | | **81** |

---

## Domain 1: Catalog & Network

---

### DE-001 — ProductRegistered

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | ProductRegistered |
| **Business Meaning** | The organization has introduced a new SKU into the trusted product catalog. The product is eligible for stock policy assignment and, when active, for procurement and fulfillment referencing. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Product Catalog |
| **Triggering Command** | `RegisterProduct` *(UC-001, UC-046)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Product exists with unique SKU, mandatory attributes, and initial lifecycle status (typically active). Product is searchable across the network and eligible for downstream configuration. |

---

### DE-002 — ProductStatusChanged

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | ProductStatusChanged |
| **Business Meaning** | The commercial availability of a SKU has changed. Discontinued status prohibits new procurement and reservations; inactive status restricts new customer commitments. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Product Catalog |
| **Triggering Command** | `ChangeProductStatus` *(UC-001)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Product lifecycle status is updated with prior status, new status, and attribution recorded. Downstream eligibility rules (procurement, reservation, replenishment) reflect the new status. |

---

### DE-003 — ProductABCClassificationAssigned

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | ProductABCClassificationAssigned |
| **Business Meaning** | Operational priority for the SKU has been set. Class A products receive highest count frequency, monitoring intensity, and alert priority. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Product Catalog |
| **Triggering Command** | `AssignABCClassification` *(UC-004)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Product carries an ABC class (A, B, or C) with effective date. Cycle count scheduling and low-stock alert prioritization use the new classification. |

---

### DE-004 — InventoryLocationActivated

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | InventoryLocationActivated |
| **Business Meaning** | A location is authorized to receive, hold, fulfill, and transact inventory. Stock positions may be established and operational workflows enabled. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Inventory Location |
| **Triggering Command** | `ActivateInventoryLocation` *(UC-002, UC-046)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Location operational status is active. Opening balances (if required) are recorded. Location accepts receipts, reservations, fulfillments, and transfers. |

---

### DE-005 — InventoryLocationDeactivated

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | InventoryLocationDeactivated |
| **Business Meaning** | A location is no longer authorized for new inventory activity. Existing stock must have been cleared or dispositioned before deactivation. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Inventory Location |
| **Triggering Command** | `DeactivateInventoryLocation` *(UC-002)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Location operational status is deactivated or closing. New receipts, reservations, and fulfillments are blocked. Historical records remain intact. |

---

### DE-006 — StoragePositionConfigured

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | StoragePositionConfigured |
| **Business Meaning** | A findable physical address within a location is available for put-away placement and pick path guidance. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Inventory Location |
| **Triggering Command** | `ConfigureStoragePosition` *(UC-002)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Storage position (zone, aisle, bin) exists within the location hierarchy and is available for put-away and pick operations. |

---

### DE-007 — LocationFreezeImposed

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | LocationFreezeImposed |
| **Business Meaning** | All receiving, shipping, transfers, and adjustments at the location are suspended until the wall-to-wall count is certified complete. Ensures a stable snapshot for accurate counting. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Physical Inventory Count |
| **Triggering Command** | `StartPhysicalInventoryCount` *(UC-015)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Location is frozen. Receiving, shipping, transfers, and non-count adjustments are blocked. Count teams operate against a stable inventory snapshot. |

---

### DE-008 — LocationFreezeReleased

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | LocationFreezeReleased |
| **Business Meaning** | Normal inventory operations may resume at the location. Count variances have been identified and routed for investigation. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Physical Inventory Count |
| **Triggering Command** | `CertifyPhysicalInventoryCount` *(UC-015)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Location freeze is lifted. Normal receiving, shipping, transfers, and adjustments may resume. Count event is certified with variances routed to adjustment cases. |

---

### DE-009 — GovernancePolicyPublished

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | GovernancePolicyPublished |
| **Business Meaning** | Organization-wide inventory control parameters have changed. All subsequent transactions must evaluate against the new effective policy. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Inventory Governance |
| **Triggering Command** | `PublishGovernancePolicy` *(UC-005)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | New governance policy version is effective with approval thresholds, tolerances, and exception rules. Subsequent adjustments, receipts, and matches evaluate against this policy. |

---

### DE-010 — ReasonCodeRetired

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Event Name** | ReasonCodeRetired |
| **Business Meaning** | A categorized exception reason is no longer valid for new transactions. Historical records retain prior reason code attributions unchanged. |
| **Aggregate Responsible** | Inventory Governance |
| **Triggering Command** | `RetireReasonCode` *(UC-005)* |
| **Resulting Business State** | Reason code status is retired and removed from active selection lists. Historical transactions retain original reason code references. |

## Event Flow — Core Business Lifecycles

### Inbound Supply

```
PlacePurchaseOrder → PurchaseOrderPlaced
ScheduleInboundDelivery → InboundDeliveryScheduled
VerifyGoodsReceipt → GoodsReceiptVerified
[RecordReceiptDiscrepancy → ReceiptDiscrepancyRecorded → ResolveReceiptDiscrepancy → ReceiptDiscrepancyResolved]
CompletePutAway → PutAwayCompleted → StockReceived → InventoryMovementRecorded
RecordSupplierInvoice → SupplierInvoiceReceived → CompleteThreeWayMatch → ThreeWayMatchCompleted
```

### Order Fulfillment

```
ConfirmOrderAvailability → OrderAvailabilityConfirmed
ConfirmCustomerOrder → CustomerOrderConfirmed → ReserveStock → StockReserved
VerifyPick → PickVerified
DispatchShipment → ShipmentDispatched → StockShipped → InventoryMovementRecorded
[CompletePartialFulfillment → PartialFulfillmentCompleted → RecordBackorder → BackorderRecorded → FulfillBackorder → BackorderFulfilled]
```

### Inventory Accuracy

```
ScheduleCycleCount → CycleCountScheduled
SubmitCycleCountResult → CycleCountCompleted → IdentifyCountVariance → CountVarianceIdentified
ApproveCountVariance → CountVarianceApproved
SubmitAdjustment → AdjustmentSubmitted → ApproveAdjustment → AdjustmentApproved
→ StockAdjusted → InventoryMovementRecorded → AuditTrailRecorded
```

### Network Transfer

```
RequestStockTransfer → TransferRequested
ApproveTransferRequest → TransferApproved
DispatchTransfer → TransferDispatched
ConfirmTransferReceipt → TransferReceived → StockReceived → InventoryMovementRecorded
```

### Returns

```
IssueReturnAuthorization → ReturnAuthorizationIssued
ReceiveCustomerReturn → CustomerReturnReceived
InspectReturnedGoods → ReturnInspected
[RestockReturnedGoods → ReturnRestocked | QuarantineReturnedGoods → ReturnQuarantined | WriteOffReturnedGoods → ReturnWrittenOff]
```

## Excluded from Domain Events

| Occurrence | Treatment | Rationale |
|------------|-----------|-----------|
| User searches or views inventory | Read operation | No business state change |
| Report query executed | Read model projection | Queries do not mutate domain state |
| Validation failure / business rule rejection | Rejection response | Nothing happened — state unchanged |
| Scheduled timer fired | Infrastructure signal | Timer is not a business event; resulting evaluation emits the business event |
| Email or notification delivered | Infrastructure | Delivery channel is not an inventory domain concern |

# Domain Policies
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-ES-003 |
| **Document Title** | Domain Policies — Event Storming Catalog |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-ES-001 (Domain Events), SRS-ES-002 (Domain Commands), SRS-DM-005 (Domain Services), SRS-BR-001 (Business Rules) |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business reaction policies only — no message handlers, sagas, or infrastructure orchestration |

### Purpose

This document identifies **Domain Policies** for the Inventory Management System. A policy is a business reaction rule expressed as:

> **Whenever** [Domain Event] **then** [Business Action]

Policies connect domain events to subsequent business intentions. They represent organizational workflow discipline — what must happen next when a meaningful business fact is recorded. Policies may issue a command, block an action, route work to a human actor, or raise an alert.

### Policy Naming Convention

Policies use descriptive **PascalCase** names ending in `Policy` where helpful: `ReserveStockOnOrderConfirmationPolicy`, or concise workflow names: `Activate Stock on Put-Away`.

### Policy Catalog Summary

| Workflow Area | Policy IDs | Count |
|---------------|------------|-------|
| Order Fulfillment | POL-001 – POL-010 | 10 |
| Inbound & Procurement | POL-011 – POL-020 | 10 |
| Inventory Balance & Replenishment | POL-021 – POL-028 | 8 |
| Network Transfer | POL-029 – POL-033 | 5 |
| Inventory Accuracy & Control | POL-034 – POL-042 | 9 |
| Returns Management | POL-043 – POL-048 | 6 |
| Commercial & Promotional | POL-049 – POL-052 | 4 |
| Governance & Access Control | POL-053 – POL-058 | 6 |
| Financial Alignment | POL-059 – POL-062 | 4 |
| Master Data & Reference | POL-063 – POL-066 | 4 |
| **Total** | | **64** |

## Workflow 1: Order Fulfillment

---

### POL-001 — Reserve Stock on Order Confirmation

## Policy Flow — Core Business Lifecycles

### Order-to-Cash Reaction Chain

```
CustomerOrderConfirmed
  → [POL-001] ReserveStock
    → StockReserved
      → [POL-021] EvaluateStockStatus

PickVerified
  → [POL-004] authorize DispatchShipment
    → ShipmentDispatched
      → [POL-005] ShipStock
        → StockShipped
          → [POL-028] TransferConsignmentOwnership (if consignment)
          → [POL-042] InventoryMovementRecorded
```

### Procure-to-Pay Reaction Chain

```
PurchaseOrderPlaced
  → [POL-020] ScheduleInboundDelivery

GoodsReceiptVerified
  → [POL-011] stage for CompletePutAway
  → [POL-013] ApplyQuarantineHold (if bonded)

PutAwayCompleted
  → [POL-012] ReceiveStock
    → [POL-021] EvaluateStockStatus
      → [POL-022] RecommendReplenishmentAction (if low)

SupplierInvoiceReceived
  → [POL-015] EvaluateThreeWayMatch
    → ThreeWayMatchCompleted
      → [POL-017] authorize payment
      → [POL-059] PrepareValuationSnapshot
```

### Count-to-Adjust Reaction Chain

```
CycleCountCompleted
  → [POL-036] IdentifyCountVariance
    → CountVarianceIdentified
      → [POL-037] route for ApproveCountVariance
        → CountVarianceApproved
          → [POL-038] SubmitAdjustment
            → [POL-039] governance evaluation
              → AdjustmentApproved
                → [POL-025] ApplyApprovedAdjustment
```

---

## Excluded from Domain Policies

| Occurrence | Treatment | Rationale |
|------------|-----------|-----------|
| User views dashboard or report | Read model query | No reactive business workflow |
| User acknowledges alert without action | UI state only | Acknowledgment does not change inventory domain state |
| Command validation failure | Rejection response | No event raised — nothing to react to |
| Email/SMS delivery | Infrastructure | Delivery mechanism is not a business policy |
| Scheduled timer firing | Infrastructure signal | Policy reacts to the resulting domain event, not the timer |

# Read Models
## Inventory Management System — Event Storming

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-ES-005 |
| **Document Title** | Read Models — Event Storming Catalog |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-ES-001 (Domain Events), SRS-DM-003 (Domain Aggregates), SRS-DM-006 (Domain Events), SRS-UC-001 (Use Case Catalog), SRS-DM-004 (Bounded Contexts — Inventory Intelligence) |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Business information projections only — no database schemas, SQL, or UI wireframes |

### Purpose

This document identifies **Read Models** required by the Inventory Management System. A read model is a purpose-built projection that answers a specific business question by consuming domain events. Read models support inquiry, monitoring, decision-making, and compliance — they never mutate transactional aggregate state.

Read models belong to the **Inventory Intelligence** bounded context. They are eventually consistent with operational writes and may be rebuilt from the event stream.

### Read Model Catalog Summary

| Domain Area | Read Model IDs | Count |
|-------------|----------------|-------|
| Inventory Visibility & Availability | RM-001 – RM-004 | 4 |
| Alerts & Notifications | RM-005 – RM-006 | 2 |
| Procurement & Inbound Supply | RM-007 – RM-012 | 6 |
| Order Fulfillment | RM-013 – RM-016 | 4 |
| Network Transfer & Balance | RM-017 – RM-019 | 3 |
| Inventory Accuracy & Control | RM-020 – RM-025 | 6 |
| Commercial & Promotional | RM-026 – RM-027 | 2 |
| Financial & Valuation | RM-028 – RM-031 | 4 |
| Governance & Compliance | RM-032 – RM-034 | 3 |
| Master Data & Reference | RM-035 – RM-039 | 5 |
| **Total** | | **39** |

## Domain 1: Inventory Visibility & Availability

---

### RM-001 — Network Stock Status Board

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Name** | Network Stock Status Board |
| **Purpose** | Answer *"What do we have, where is it, and what is its health?"* across the location network for daily operational monitoring. |
| **Information Displayed** | On-hand, reserved, quarantined, and ATP quantities by product and location; stock status indicator (in stock, low stock, out of stock, overstock); ABC classification; last movement date; ownership classification (owned vs. consignment) |
| **Primary Users** | Inventory Controller, Operations Director, Warehouse Manager, Purchasing Manager |
| **Source Events** | StockReceived, StockShipped, StockReserved, StockReservationReleased, StockAdjusted, StockWrittenOff, QuarantineHoldApplied, QuarantineHoldReleased, PromotionalStockAllocated, PromotionalAllocationReleased, ConsignmentOwnershipTransferred, StockPolicyThresholdChanged, ProductABCClassificationAssigned, LowStockThresholdBreached, OutOfStockDetected, OverstockDetected |
| **Use Cases** | UC-012, UC-037 |

---

### RM-002 — Availability Inquiry View

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Name** | Availability Inquiry View |
| **Purpose** | Answer *"Can we promise this quantity to a customer at this location or across the network?"* before commercial commitment. |
| **Information Displayed** | ATP by product and location; network-wide ATP rollup; reserved and quarantined exclusions; promotional ring-fence impact; product lifecycle eligibility; partial availability breakdown per order line |
| **Primary Users** | Sales Representative, Customer Service Representative, Sales Manager |
| **Source Events** | OrderAvailabilityConfirmed, StockReserved, StockReservationReleased, StockReceived, StockShipped, QuarantineHoldApplied, QuarantineHoldReleased, PromotionalStockAllocated, ProductStatusChanged, LowStockThresholdBreached, OutOfStockDetected |
| **Use Cases** | UC-013, UC-021, UC-048 |

---

### RM-003 — Quarantine and Hold Register

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Name** | Quarantine and Hold Register |
| **Purpose** | Answer *"What stock is physically present but not sellable, and why?"* for quality, regulatory, and customs oversight. |
| **Information Displayed** | Held quantity by product, location, and lot/batch; hold reason (quality, recall, customs, bonded); hold applied date and attribution; expected disposition; ATP exclusion impact |
| **Primary Users** | Warehouse Manager, Inventory Controller, Operations Director |
| **Source Events** | QuarantineHoldApplied, QuarantineHoldReleased, ReturnQuarantined, GoodsReceiptVerified *(bonded)* |
| **Use Cases** | UC-019, UC-037 |

---

### RM-004 — Availability Inquiry Log

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Name** | Availability Inquiry Log |
| **Purpose** | Answer *"What availability checks were performed and what was promised?"* for sales accountability and dispute resolution. |
| **Information Displayed** | Inquiry timestamp, product, requested quantity, location scope, ATP result, confirming user, linked order reference (if confirmed) |
| **Primary Users** | Sales Representative, Customer Service Representative, Inventory Controller |
| **Source Events** | OrderAvailabilityConfirmed |
| **Use Cases** | UC-013, UC-021 |

## Excluded from Read Models

| Capability | Treatment | Rationale |
|------------|-----------|-----------|
| Aggregate current state query | Write model | ATP and on-hand authority lives in Stock Position aggregate — availability views project from events but operational commands read aggregate state for consistency |
| Ad-hoc SQL analytics | External BI | Exploratory analysis outside IMS bounded context |
| Real-time command validation | Domain service | Eligibility and freeze checks are synchronous evaluations, not read models |
| User session and permission cache | Infrastructure | Identity layer concern, not inventory intelligence |

## Inventory Management System — Complete Business Lifecycle
