## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-ES-008 |
| **Document Title** | Event Storming Board — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-ES-001 (Events), SRS-ES-002 (Commands), SRS-ES-003 (Policies), SRS-ES-004 (Actors), SRS-DM-003 (Aggregates) |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |

### Board Legend

```
┌─────────────┐
│   ACTOR     │  Human role or external system initiating action
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│  COMMAND    │  Business intention (imperative verb)
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│  AGGREGATE  │  Consistency boundary / transaction scope
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│DOMAIN EVENT │  Past-tense business fact (DE-xxx)
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   POLICY    │  Whenever [Event] then [Action] (POL-xxx)
└──────┬──────┘
       │
       ▼
   (next command in chain…)
```

| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `[Actor]` | Business participant |
| `→ CMD` | Command issued |
| `⇒ AGG` | Target aggregate |
| `⇒ EVT` | Domain event raised |
| `⇒ POL` | Policy reaction |
| `┄┄┄` | Optional / conditional branch |
| `════` | Cross-aggregate reaction (eventual consistency) |

### Lifecycle Index

| Board | Lifecycle | Primary Actors |
|-------|-----------|----------------|
| 1 | Foundation & Go-Live | Inventory Controller |
| 2 | Replenishment Detection | System / Purchasing Manager |
| 3 | Procurement & Inbound Supply | Buyer → Receiving Clerk → Warehouse Staff → Finance Manager |
| 4 | Order Fulfillment | Sales Rep → CS Rep → Picker |
| 5 | Partial Fulfillment & Backorder | Customer Service Representative |
| 6 | Network Transfer | Regional Manager → Operations Director → Warehouse Staff |
| 7 | Cycle Count & Adjustment | Warehouse Staff → Warehouse Manager → Operations Director |
| 8 | Physical Inventory Count | Inventory Controller |
| 9 | Customer Returns | CS Rep → Receiving Clerk → Warehouse Manager |
| 10 | Promotional Campaign | Marketing Manager |
| 11 | Quarantine & Hold | Warehouse Manager |
| 12 | Finance & Valuation Close | Finance Manager |

## Master Board — End-to-End Business Lifecycle

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 PHASE 1: FOUNDATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 Inventory Controller
   → RegisterProduct              ⇒ Product Catalog        ⇒ ProductRegistered
   → ActivateInventoryLocation    ⇒ Inventory Location     ⇒ InventoryLocationActivated
     ⇒ POL-064: Establish Opening Balances
   → EstablishOpeningBalances     ⇒ Stock Position         ⇒ StockReceived
   → UpdateStockPolicyThresholds  ⇒ Stock Policy           ⇒ StockPolicyThresholdChanged
   → PublishGovernancePolicy      ⇒ Inventory Governance   ⇒ GovernancePolicyPublished

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 PHASE 2: REPLENISHMENT & INBOUND SUPPLY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 [Low stock detected]
   ⇒ Stock Position               ⇒ LowStockThresholdBreached
     ⇒ POL-022: Trigger Replenishment
   → RecommendReplenishmentAction ⇒ (Domain Service)       ⇒ ReplenishmentRecommended

 Purchasing Manager / Buyer
   → SubmitPurchaseRequisition    ⇒ Purchase Requisition   ⇒ PurchaseRequisitionSubmitted
     ⇒ POL-029: Evaluate Network Before Procurement
   → ApprovePurchaseRequisition   ⇒ Purchase Requisition   ⇒ PurchaseRequisitionApproved
     ⇒ POL-019: Convert to PO
   → PlacePurchaseOrder           ⇒ Purchase Order         ⇒ PurchaseOrderPlaced
     ⇒ POL-020: Schedule Inbound
   → ScheduleInboundDelivery      ⇒ Purchase Order         ⇒ InboundDeliveryScheduled

 Supplier (external) delivers goods
 Receiving Clerk
   → VerifyGoodsReceipt           ⇒ Goods Receipt          ⇒ GoodsReceiptVerified
     ⇒ POL-011: Stage for Put-Away
 Warehouse Staff
   → CompletePutAway              ⇒ Goods Receipt          ⇒ PutAwayCompleted
     ⇒ POL-012: Activate Stock
   → ReceiveStock                 ⇒ Stock Position         ⇒ StockReceived
     ⇒ POL-021: Reclassify Stock Status

 Finance Manager
   → RecordSupplierInvoice        ⇒ Supplier Invoice       ⇒ SupplierInvoiceReceived
     ⇒ POL-015: Evaluate Match
   → EvaluateThreeWayMatch        ⇒ Supplier Invoice       ⇒ ThreeWayMatchCompleted
     ⇒ POL-017: Authorize Payment

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 PHASE 3: ORDER FULFILLMENT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 Sales Representative
   → ConfirmOrderAvailability     ⇒ Customer Order         ⇒ OrderAvailabilityConfirmed
 Customer Service Representative
   → ConfirmCustomerOrder           ⇒ Customer Order         ⇒ CustomerOrderConfirmed
     ⇒ POL-001: Reserve Stock
   → ReserveStock                   ⇒ Stock Position         ⇒ StockReserved
 Warehouse Picker
   → VerifyPick                     ⇒ Customer Order         ⇒ PickVerified
     ⇒ POL-004: Authorize Shipment
   → DispatchShipment               ⇒ Customer Order         ⇒ ShipmentDispatched
     ⇒ POL-005: Deduct Stock
   → ShipStock                      ⇒ Stock Position         ⇒ StockShipped
 Logistics / Carrier (external) picks up

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 PHASE 4: INVENTORY CONTROL & RETURNS (parallel ongoing operations)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 Cycle Count path ──► CountVarianceIdentified ──► AdjustmentApproved ──► StockAdjusted
 Transfer path    ──► TransferRequested ──► TransferApproved ──► TransferReceived ──► StockReceived
 Returns path     ──► ReturnAuthorizationIssued ──► ReturnInspected ──► ReturnRestocked ──► StockReceived

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 PHASE 5: FINANCIAL CLOSE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 Finance Manager
   → PrepareValuationSnapshot     ⇒ Valuation Snapshot     ⇒ InventoryValuationSnapshotPrepared
   → ReconcileInventoryValuation  ⇒ Valuation Snapshot     ⇒ ValuationVarianceIdentified (if mismatch)
```

## Complete Lifecycle Swimlane — Chronological Summary

```
TIME ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►

FOUNDATION     REPLENISH        INBOUND           FULFILLMENT        CONTROL
    │              │               │                  │                 │
    │         LowStock           PO placed          Order            Cycle Count
    │         detected           Receipt            confirmed        Variance
    │              │               │                  │                 │
    ▼              ▼               ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 Product      Requisition      PutAway           ReserveStock      Adjustment
 Location     → PO             completed         → Pick            approved
 activated    → Receipt        → StockReceived   → Ship            → StockAdjusted
 → Opening    → Match          → ATP updated     → StockShipped
   balances

     │                                                    │
     └────────────────── STOCK POSITION (central) ──────────┘
              on-hand │ reserved │ ATP │ quarantine │ status

RETURNS (parallel)          TRANSFER (parallel)         FINANCE (periodic)
    │                           │                          │
 RMA issued                Transfer approved            Valuation snapshot
 → Received               → Dispatched                 → GL reconcile
 → Inspected               → Received                   → Payment authorized
 → Restocked/Written-off  → StockReceived
```

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-ES-007 |
| **Document Title** | Event Storming Hotspots — Unresolved Business Issues |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Domain Expert |
| **Source Documents** | SRS-ES-001 through SRS-ES-006, SRS-DM-009 (Domain Model Review), SRS-BR-001, SRS-UC-001 |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Scope** | Unresolved business uncertainties discovered during event storming — not technical design decisions |

### Purpose

In Event Storming, a **hotspot** marks an area where the business model is uncertain, contested, or incomplete. Hotspots block confident aggregate design, policy definition, or rule enforcement until domain experts resolve them. This document captures hotspots surfaced by cross-checking commands, events, policies, aggregates, and business rules.

### Hotspot Severity

| Severity | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| **Critical** | Blocks architecture or MVP rule enforcement |
| **High** | Affects core workflows; workaround risky |
| **Medium** | Phase 2 scope or edge case; document assumption for MVP |
| **Low** | Clarification improves model; deferrable |

### Hotspot Summary

## HS-001 — Ad-Hoc Receipt Without Purchase Order

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | How supplier goods may be received when no purchase order exists, and how financial controls apply afterward |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-007 requires a PO for supplier receipt *except explicitly approved ad-hoc exceptions*, but the exception matrix is undefined (BRD ISS-020). Event storming has `VerifyGoodsReceipt` and POL-011 for PO-backed flow only. No command, event, authorization artifact, or policy exists for the exception path. Business Rule Dependencies flag **CF-007**: ad-hoc receipt conflicts with BR-008 three-way match assumptions. Validation rules VR-040 and VR-042 reference ad-hoc approval but no workflow owns it. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-07 (Goods Receipt & Verification), BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement), BP-30 (Inventory Valuation & Financial Reconciliation) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Who may authorize an ad-hoc receipt (role and approval level)? 2. Is retroactive PO creation required, and within what time limit? 3. What quantity/value caps apply per governance policy? 4. How does three-way match work when no PO existed at receipt — alternate match rules or retroactive PO? 5. Can ad-hoc receipt apply to consignment or bonded goods? 6. What reason codes and audit evidence are mandatory? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Workshop with Purchasing, Receiving, and Finance to define ad-hoc exception matrix. 2. Add **Ad-Hoc Receipt Authorization** concept with `AdHocReceiptAuthorized` event. 3. Formalize **BR-033** (or extend BR-007) and resolve CF-007 with Finance. 4. Update Goods Receipt aggregate and POL-011 with exception branch. 5. Document in ubiquitous language. |

---

## HS-002 — Opening Balance and Location Go-Live

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | How opening stock balances are established, verified, and approved before a location becomes transactionally active |
| **Why It Is Complex** | `ActivateInventoryLocation` emits DE-004 and `EstablishOpeningBalances` creates Stock Position quantities, but no aggregate governs the verification workflow. UC-046 covers bulk import; VR-025 requires approver sign-off — yet no commands or events model certification. Exception EX-004 (opening balance dispute) exists without resolution workflow. Constraint **CF-009** tensions go-live continuity (operations cannot shut down) vs. FR-010 (no transactions until balance approved). Event storming gap: first Stock Position creation lacks governing business process. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-02 (Location & Warehouse Setup), BP-01 (Product Master Data Management), BP-12 (Full Physical Inventory Count) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Is opening balance established by physical count, system import, or either? 2. Who approves opening balances (Inventory Controller, Finance, Operations Director)? 3. Can a location be *active* in read-only/staging mode before balance certification? 4. What happens when opening balance dispute arises at go-live (EX-004)? 5. Is a wall-to-wall count required for new locations or only data import with sample verification? 6. Relationship between FR-010 and FR-090 import — same workflow or alternatives? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Business decision: count-validated vs. import-only go-live. 2. Model **Opening Balance Establishment** aggregate or subprocess with `SubmitOpeningBalance`, `CertifyOpeningBalance`, `OpeningBalanceCertified` event. 3. Add **BR-043** Opening Balance Certification (per Business Rule Catalog Review). 4. Define precondition chain: certify → activate location → establish balances on Stock Position. 5. Resolve CF-009 with staging-mode business rule if needed. |

## HS-003 — Location Freeze Authority During Physical Count

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | Which business concept owns location operational freeze during wall-to-wall physical inventory count |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-024 requires freeze during physical count. Events DE-007 (`LocationFreezeImposed`) and DE-008 (`LocationFreezeReleased`) originate from **Physical Inventory Count**, but **Inventory Location** aggregate also lists freeze enforcement. DS-014 (Freeze Guard) consults both. Two aggregates could mutate freeze state — risk of race conditions at count certification vs. location status changes. POL-034 and POL-056 block mutations but do not resolve ownership. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-12 (Full Physical Inventory Count), BP-02 (Location & Warehouse Setup), BP-07–BP-09 (Inbound), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-25 (Transfer Execution) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Does freeze apply to the entire location hierarchy or only the counted site? 2. Can emergency receipts or shipments override freeze with director authorization? 3. Who can release freeze early if count is aborted? 4. Are count-related adjustments the *only* mutations permitted during freeze? 5. What is the business consequence if freeze is violated — reject transaction or flag exception? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Confirm pattern: Physical Count **initiates** freeze; Inventory Location **holds** authoritative frozen flag. 2. Document integration contract in bounded context map. 3. DS-014 reads Inventory Location state only. 4. Add **MR-09** formal rule: non-count adjustments blocked during freeze. 5. Workshop edge cases (emergency override, count abort). |

## HS-004 — Promotional Ring-Fence vs. General ATP

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | How promotional stock ring-fencing interacts with available-to-promise and who may consume ring-fenced quantity |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-029 requires ring-fencing during campaigns, but consumption rules for non-promotional orders are only partially stated (MR-10). Promotional Stock Allocation aggregate owns campaign intent; Stock Position owns ATP mechanics — dual context risks inconsistent state (P1-02). Event storming shows DE-020/DE-021 from Commercial aggregate and POL-026 affecting Stock Position, but invariant ownership is undocumented. Entity model still groups allocation under Inventory Balance domain. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-31 (Promotional & Launch Stock Readiness), BP-17 (Inventory Reservation), BP-16 (Order Availability Confirmation) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Can non-promotional orders ever consume ring-fenced stock, and who approves override (commercial leadership)? 2. Is ring-fence at product-location or network level? 3. What happens to un consumed allocation at campaign end — auto-release or manual review? 4. How is promotional ATP presented in availability inquiry (RM-002)? 5. If campaign stock is insufficient (DE-072), may general ATP backfill the campaign commitment? 6. Priority between existing reservations and new promotional allocation on same SKU? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Confirm: Commercial owns intent; Stock Position reacts to events only. 2. Formalize **MR-10** Promotional Consumption Approval. 3. Workshop Marketing, Sales, and Operations on override rules. 4. Update POL-026 with explicit ATP segregation mechanics. 5. Align SRS-DM-001 entity grouping with Commercial context. |

## HS-005 — Lot/Batch Quantity Model for Traceable Products

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | How traceable inventory quantities are scoped, reserved, picked, and counted when lot/batch identity is mandatory |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-017 requires lot/batch capture on receipt, transfer, and shipment. Stock Position identity is documented ambiguously as *product + location [+ lot]* vs. product-location with embedded Lot/Batch child entities (P1-05). This fork affects reservation (`ReserveStock`), cycle count variance scope, FEFO pick selection (DS-011), and transfer dispatch. Event storming commands do not specify lot-level vs. position-level reservation. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-09 (Put-Away), BP-11 (Cycle Counting), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-25 (Transfer Execution), BP-28 (Return Disposition) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. One Stock Position per product-location with lot sub-quantities, or one position per lot? 2. Can ATP be promised without specifying lot, with lot assigned at pick? 3. How are partial lot quantities handled on count variance? 4. Mandatory FEFO — can picker override lot selection with manager approval? 5. Recall scenario: how is affected lot isolated across locations? 6. Mixed-lot storage position — allowed or prohibited? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Business workshop with Quality and Warehouse on traceability operating model. 2. Adopt **single Stock Position per product-location** with Lot/Batch child entities (recommended in domain review). 3. Document invariant: lot quantities sum to on-hand; traceable products require lot on all movements. 4. Update reservation and pick commands with lot assignment rules. 5. Add recall workflow hotspot follow-up if in scope. |

## HS-006 — Consignment Ownership Transfer Trigger

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | When consignment stock becomes organization-owned for valuation, fulfillment, and payment purposes |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-031 states ownership transfers at *defined consumption or sale event per supplier agreement* — but the triggering events are not enumerated. DE-022 (`ConsignmentOwnershipTransferred`) is raised on `StockShipped` via POL-028, yet consignment agreements may trigger on issue, consumption, invoice, or other events. DEP-028 notes three-way match timing differs for consignment. VR/consignment ATP exclusion (CF-014) is unresolved — consignment may appear available for sale while not owned. Supplier aggregate has no lifecycle events to record agreement terms. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-30 (Valuation & Financial Reconciliation), BP-05 (Purchase Order Placement) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. What are the standard consumption triggers (shipment, internal issue, invoice, time-based)? 2. Is consignment stock included in ATP for customer commitment (BR-001 interaction)? 3. When does three-way match and payment occur for consignment — at ownership transfer? 4. How are consignment terms captured per supplier vs. per PO line? 5. Can consignment and owned stock coexist for same SKU at same location? 6. Financial valuation treatment before and after transfer? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Catalog consignment agreement types with Finance and Procurement. 2. Formalize **MR-08** with explicit trigger event list per agreement type. 3. Add Supplier terms commands/events. 4. Clarify ATP formula for consignment in BR-001 context. 5. Map consignment path in three-way match (resolve DEP-028). |

## HS-007 — Order Reservation and Stock Position Coordination

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | How customer order commitment stays consistent with stock position quantity when operations span two aggregates without a single transaction |
| **Why It Is Complex** | Customer Order Fulfillment holds `InventoryReservation` entity; Stock Position holds `reserved` quantity — coordinated by DS-002 and POL-001/002. Partial failure scenario: order confirmed and reservation fails on Stock Position leaves inconsistent state. High-concurrency hot SKUs create contention. `CompletePartialFulfillment` decomposes lines across fulfilled and backordered — quantity reconciliation invariant must hold. Multi-location fulfillment (UC-048, DE-045) multiplies coordination points. Aggregate review flags Customer Order as split candidate post-MVP. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-16 (Order Availability Confirmation), BP-17 (Inventory Reservation), BP-18 (Pick, Pack & Ship), BP-19 (Partial Fulfillment & Backorder) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. What is the business response when order is confirmed but reservation fails (retry, cancel, partial)? 2. Is reservation synchronous with confirmation or eventual within SLA? 3. How long may reservation remain open before mandatory release (see HS-016)? 4. Who wins when two orders compete for last ATP unit? 5. Multi-location split — single customer communication or per-shipment? 6. Compensation policy if shipment deduct fails after pick verified? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Define reservation SLA and failure compensation with Customer Service and Operations. 2. Document saga: ConfirmOrder → ReserveStock → on failure → CancelOrder or PartialConfirm. 3. Formalize order line invariant as published business rule. 4. Prototype contention scenario for Class A high-velocity SKUs. 5. Defer Shipment aggregate split decision until volume metrics available. |

## HS-008 — Return Write-Off Governance Path

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | Whether returned goods written off must follow the same adjustment governance workflow as operational write-offs |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-023 requires documented write-off authorization. Customer Return Case command `WriteOffReturnedGoods` currently triggers `ApplyApprovedWriteOff` on Stock Position directly (POL-047). Domain review REL-ISSUE-07 states return write-off should **create Adjustment Case** for governance. Two paths to write-off create SoD and audit inconsistency. Return inspection (BR-026) and write-off authorization (BR-023) may involve different approvers. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-27 (Customer Return Intake), BP-28 (Return-to-Stock or Disposal), BP-14 (Stock Adjustment & Write-Off), BP-15 (Shrinkage & Loss Management) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Can warehouse manager authorize return write-off at inspection, or must Operations Director approve via Adjustment Case? 2. Is return write-off threshold governed by same approval limits as operational shrinkage? 3. Should return write-off reason codes differ from general adjustment codes? 4. Finance notification timing — at inspection or at governance approval? 5. Partial return line disposition — mixed restock and write-off on same RMA? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Confirm with Finance and Operations: single governance path via Adjustment Case. 2. Update POL-047: `ReturnWrittenOff` → create Adjustment Case → `ApproveAdjustment` → `ApplyApprovedWriteOff`. 3. Define return-specific reason code subset. 4. Align event storming commands with BR-019/BR-021 SoD. |

## HS-009 — Bonded Inventory vs. General Quarantine

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | Whether customs-bonded inventory follows the same hold workflow as quality quarantine |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-030 requires bonded goods remain on hold until customs clearance — modeled today as `QuarantineHoldApplied` (POL-013). Business may require distinct **Customs Clearance Record** (ME-05) with different release authority (Regulatory Authority vs. Warehouse Manager). Bonded release triggers put-away activation; quality quarantine may route to write-off. External participant EXT-005 (Customs) triggers `ReleaseQuarantineHold` but clearance documentation differs from quality release. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-07 (Goods Receipt), BP-09 (Put-Away), BP-14 (Stock Adjustment & Write-Off) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Is bonded hold a quarantine subtype or separate business concept? 2. Who records customs clearance — receiving clerk or finance/compliance role? 3. Can bonded goods move within bonded zone without clearance? 4. Partial clearance — some quantity cleared, remainder held? 5. Audit evidence required for clearance (document reference)? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Clarify with Compliance whether bonded = quarantine subtype for MVP. 2. If distinct, add Customs Clearance Record and `CustomsClearanceGranted` event. 3. Update POL-013 and POL-012 bonded branch. 4. Defer to Phase 2 if bonded inventory not in MVP scope. |

## HS-010 — Transfer-Before-Buy vs. Purchase Decision

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | Who decides between network transfer and new procurement when local shortage is detected, and how mandatory the network check is |
| **Why It Is Complex** | BR-011 requires network availability evaluation before purchase. POL-029 may recommend `RequestStockTransfer` or `RejectPurchaseRequisition`, but replenishment recommendation (DE-071) is advisory — not a binding business decision. Regional manager, buyer, and operations director may disagree. Source location minimum (BR-012) may block transfer that purchasing prefers. No persistent **Replenishment Suggestion** entity for audit of overridden recommendations (ME-06). |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-21 (Low-Stock Alert Review), BP-22 (Replenishment Planning), BP-24 (Transfer Request), BP-26 (Network Rebalancing) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Is network check mandatory gate before PO approval, or advisory? 2. Who has final authority when transfer is recommended but buyer prefers purchase? 3. Must rejection of transfer recommendation be documented? 4. Cost comparison (transfer cost vs. purchase) — in scope for decision? 5. Auto-generated transfer request from rebalancing (UC-034) — approval required? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Define decision authority matrix: Purchasing vs. Operations vs. Regional Manager. 2. Clarify BR-011 enforcement level (hard block vs. warning). 3. Add acknowledgment workflow when recommendation overridden. 4. Workshop BP-21/BP-22/BP-24 integrated replenishment policy. |

POL-008 triggers `FulfillBackorder` on `StockReceived`, but priority rules are undefined — FIFO by acknowledgment date, order value, customer tier, or product class? MR-06 states backorder must convert to reservation before fulfillment — sequence not fully modeled. Competition between backorder fulfillment and new order reservation on inbound stock. `BackorderFulfilled` (DE-043) chain spans multiple commands without documented priority policy. |

Auto-fulfill on stock arrival or manual customer service trigger? 3. Customer notification required before backorder shipment? 4. Partial backorder fulfillment over multiple receipts — allowed? 5. Backorder expiry or cancellation policy? |

## HS-016 — Reservation Expiry and Stale Commitments

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Area of Uncertainty** | Whether inventory reservations expire and how stale commitments are released |
| **Why It Is Complex** | Reservations reduce ATP indefinitely until fulfillment or cancellation (BR-002). MR-05 proposes expiry/escalation policy — not formalized. Long-lived reservations on slow-moving orders block ATP for other customers. No command `ExpireReservation` or policy for auto-release. Customer Service may not cancel abandoned orders promptly. |
| **Related Business Processes** | BP-17 (Inventory Reservation), BP-16 (Order Availability Confirmation), BP-10 (Inventory Status Monitoring) |
| **Questions Requiring Clarification** | 1. Reservation time limit — days, weeks, configurable by product class? 2. Auto-release vs. escalation notification before release? 3. Customer notification before reservation release? 4. Does expiry apply to backorders differently than confirmed reservations? 5. Re-reservation priority if customer reorders after expiry? |
| **Recommended Next Steps** | 1. Define reservation TTL policy with Customer Service and Sales. 2. Formalize MR-05 as business rule if approved. 3. Add `ReservationExpired` event and POL if auto-release adopted. 4. MVP: manual release only with dashboard alert for aged reservations. |

# Part VI — System Architecture

<div class="page-break"></div>

# System Modules Design
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-SA-003 |
| **Document Title** | System Modules Design — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Solution Architect |
| **Prepared For** | Delivery leads, technical architects, and development squads |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Classification** | Internal — Architecture Confidential |
| **Scope** | Logical module decomposition within the modular monolith — no class design, database schema, or API specification |

### Related Documents

| Document | ID | Relationship |
|----------|-----|--------------|
| Architecture Vision | SRS-SA-001 | Strategic direction |
| Architecture Style Recommendation | SRS-SA-002 | Modular monolith + Clean/Hexagonal |
| Bounded Contexts | SRS-DM-007 | 1:1 module alignment source |
| Domain Aggregates | SRS-DM-003 | Owned aggregate definitions |
| System Context | SRS-SA-002 (System Context) | External actors and systems |

### Document Purpose

This document defines the **logical system modules** of the Inventory Management System. Each module maps to a bounded context, owns specific aggregates, exposes a minimal public interface, and declares explicit dependencies. Modules are designed for **loose coupling** — integration occurs through commands, queries, domain events, and shared identifiers only.

### Module Design Principles

| Principle | Rule |
|-----------|------|
| **One module per bounded context** | Strategic domain boundary = compile-time module boundary |
| **Aggregate ownership is exclusive** | Each aggregate belongs to exactly one module |
| **No cross-module aggregate access** | Other modules reference aggregates by identity (SKU, Location Code, Order ID) only |
| **No shared mutable state** | Inventory Balance is the sole ATP mutator; Intelligence is read-only |
| **Events over direct calls** | Cross-module state propagation prefers domain events; synchronous queries for read-only consultation |
| **ACL at external boundaries** | Sales/CRM and Finance/ERP integrate through dedicated adapter ports — not module internals |

### Published Language (Cross-Module Identifiers)

All modules share these **value-only identifiers** — not domain object references:

| Identifier | Owner Module | Consumers |
|------------|--------------|-----------|
| `ProductSku` | Product Catalog | All operational modules |
| `LocationCode` | Warehouse Network | All operational modules |
| `UserId` | Identity & Access | All modules |
| `SupplierCode` | Procurement & Supplier | Inbound Receiving, Intelligence |
| `PurchaseOrderId` | Procurement & Supplier | Inbound Receiving, Intelligence |
| `GoodsReceiptId` | Inbound Receiving | Procurement, Intelligence, Finance ACL |
| `CustomerOrderId` | Order Fulfillment | Returns, Intelligence, Sales ACL |
| `TransferId` | Network Transfer | Inventory Balance, Intelligence |
| `AdjustmentCaseId` | Inventory Accuracy | Inventory Balance, Intelligence |
| `ReturnAuthorizationId` | Returns Management | Order Fulfillment, Inbound Receiving |
| `CampaignId` | Commercial Campaign | Order Fulfillment, Inventory Balance |
| `ReasonCode` | Inventory Governance | All modules performing adjustments or exceptions |

## M-01 — Product Catalog

### 1. Module Name

**Product Catalog** (`ims.catalog`)

### 2. Business Responsibility

Maintain the authoritative product identity catalog — SKU definitions, lifecycle status, ABC classification, rotation policy, and traceability attributes — that all other modules reference when identifying *what* is being bought, held, counted, or sold.

| Process Coverage | BP-01, BP-04 |
|------------------|--------------|

### 3. Owned Aggregates

| Aggregate | Root Entity | Consistency Scope |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Product Catalog** | Product | Single SKU master record and embedded classification attributes |

### 4. Public Interfaces

#### Commands (Write)

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `CreateProduct` | Register new SKU with mandatory attributes |
| `UpdateProductAttributes` | Amend name, category, UoM, traceability settings |
| `ChangeProductLifecycleStatus` | Transition active → inactive → discontinued |
| `AssignAbcClassification` | Set or update ABC class for a SKU |
| `ResolveDuplicateProductConflict` | Merge or reject duplicate identity |

#### Queries (Read)

| Query | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `GetProductBySku` | Retrieve product master by SKU |
| `SearchProducts` | Filter by name, category, status, ABC class |
| `ValidateProductTransactionEligibility` | Check lifecycle allows procurement/reservation |
| `ListProductsByCategory` | Catalog browse for operational screens |

#### Published Events

| Event | Consumers |
|-------|-----------|
| `ProductCreated` | Intelligence |
| `ProductUpdated` | Intelligence |
| `ProductLifecycleStatusChanged` | Procurement, Order Fulfillment, Intelligence |
| `AbcClassificationAssigned` | Inventory Accuracy, Intelligence |

#### External Adapter Ports (Inbound)

| Port | Source |
|------|--------|
| `BulkProductImportPort` | UC-046 go-live data import |

### 5. Dependencies

| Dependency | Module | Coupling Type | Purpose |
|------------|--------|---------------|---------|
| Identity & Access | M-12 | Sync query | User attribution on mutations |
| Inventory Intelligence | M-13 | Event publish | Catalog change projections |

**No dependencies on operational or quantity modules.** Product Catalog is an upstream supplier context.

## M-02 — Warehouse Network

### 1. Module Name

**Warehouse Network** (`ims.network`)

### 2. Business Responsibility

Define and manage the inventory location network — warehouses, stores, distribution points, storage positions, hierarchy, operational status, and location lifecycle (go-live, closure, freeze state) — that anchors all stock to physical places.

| Process Coverage | BP-02, BP-12 (freeze state) |
|------------------|----------------------------|

### 3. Owned Aggregates

| Aggregate | Root Entity | Consistency Scope |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Inventory Location** | Inventory Location | Location master, hierarchy, status, **authoritative freeze flag**, storage positions |

### 4. Public Interfaces

#### Commands (Write)

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `CreateInventoryLocation` | Register new warehouse, store, or DC |
| `UpdateLocationHierarchy` | Assign parent, zones, layout structure |
| `ConfigureStoragePosition` | Add or amend bin/aisle positions within location |
| `ActivateInventoryLocation` | Enable location after opening balance certification |
| `DeactivateInventoryLocation` | Begin closure workflow |
| `ApplyLocationFreeze` | Set frozen flag (driven by Physical Count event) |
| `ReleaseLocationFreeze` | Clear frozen flag (driven by Physical Count event) |
| `CloseInventoryLocation` | Finalize closure with disposition confirmation |

#### Queries (Read)

| Query | Description |
|-------|-------------|

| `ListActiveLocations` | Network directory for dropdowns and filters |
| `GetStoragePositions` | Positions available for put-away assignment |
| `IsLocationFrozen` | Freeze guard check for operational modules |
| `IsLocationTransactionallyActive` | Go-live and status gate for mutations |

#### Published Events

| Event | Consumers |
|-------|-----------|
| `InventoryLocationCreated` | Intelligence |
| `InventoryLocationActivated` | Inventory Balance, Intelligence |
| `InventoryLocationDeactivated` | All operational modules, Intelligence |
| `LocationFreezeApplied` | Inventory Balance, Inbound, Fulfillment, Transfer, Intelligence |
| `LocationFreezeReleased` | All operational modules, Intelligence |
| `StoragePositionConfigured` | Inbound Receiving, Intelligence |

#### Subscribed Events

| Event | Source Module | Reaction |
|-------|---------------|----------|
| `LocationFreezeImposed` | Inventory Accuracy | `ApplyLocationFreeze` |
| `LocationFreezeReleased` | Inventory Accuracy | `ReleaseLocationFreeze` |

### 5. Dependencies

| Dependency | Module | Coupling Type | Purpose |
|------------|--------|---------------|---------|
| Identity & Access | M-12 | Sync query | User attribution; location-scoped role validation |
| Inventory Accuracy | M-09 | Event subscribe | Freeze initiation from physical count |
| Inventory Intelligence | M-13 | Event publish | Location network projections |

**Warehouse Network does not depend on Inventory Balance or any quantity module.**

| `RetireReasonCode` | Deactivate code for new transactions |

| `UpdateApprovalThreshold` | Amend financial/quantity approval limits |
| `UpdateReceiptTolerance` | Amend auto-accept vs. discrepancy thresholds |

| Event | Consumers |
|-------|-----------|

| `ReasonCodeCreated` | Intelligence |
| `ReasonCodeRetired` | All operational modules, Intelligence |

### 5. Dependencies

| Dependency | Module | Coupling Type | Purpose |
|------------|--------|---------------|---------|

**Governance is consulted by operational modules; it does not call them.**

## M-04 — Inventory Balance

### 1. Module Name

**Inventory Balance** (`ims.balance`)

### 2. Business Responsibility

Own the authoritative inventory quantity state — on-hand, reserved, available-to-promise (ATP), quarantine holds, lot/batch breakdown, and replenishment thresholds — answering *what do we have, where is it, and what is available?*

This is the **core domain module** and the **sole mutator of stock quantities**.

| Process Coverage | BP-03, BP-10, BP-21 |
|------------------|----------------------|

### 3. Owned Aggregates

| Aggregate | Root Entity | Consistency Scope |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| **Stock Position** | Stock Position | On-hand, reserved, ATP, lots, quarantine holds — per product per location |
| **Stock Policy** | Stock Policy | Reorder level, minimum, safety stock, maximum — per product per location |

### 4. Public Interfaces

#### Commands (Write)

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `EstablishOpeningBalance` | Create initial Stock Position at location go-live |
| `ReceiveStock` | Increase on-hand after put-away (event-driven) |
| `ReserveStock` | Commit ATP for order line |
| `ReleaseReservation` | Restore ATP on cancellation |
| `DeductStockForShipment` | Reduce on-hand and reserved after verified pick |
| `DeductStockForTransfer` | Reduce source on dispatch |
| `ReceiveStockFromTransfer` | Increase destination on transfer receipt |
| `ApplyApprovedAdjustment` | Apply governed quantity correction |
| `ApplyApprovedWriteOff` | Permanently remove quantity |
| `ApplyQuarantineHold` | Reduce ATP for held quantity |
| `ReleaseQuarantineHold` | Restore ATP after clearance |
| `SegregatePromotionalStock` | Ring-fence ATP per campaign event |
| `ReleasePromotionalAllocation` | Restore general ATP after campaign |
| `TransferConsignmentOwnership` | Reclassify ownership on consumption trigger |
| `DefineStockPolicy` | Set replenishment thresholds |
| `UpdateStockPolicy` | Amend thresholds with effective dating |

#### Queries (Read)

| Query | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `GetStockPosition` | On-hand, reserved, ATP for product at location |
| `GetAvailabilityBySku` | ATP for single SKU (hot path — NFR-PERF-002) |
| `GetNetworkAvailability` | ATP across locations for a SKU |
| `GetStockStatusIndicator` | In-stock / low-stock / out-of-stock derived state |
| `GetStockPolicy` | Thresholds for product at location |
| `GetLotBreakdown` | Lot-level quantities for traceable products |
| `EvaluateSourceTransferCapacity` | Spare quantity above minimum for transfer |

#### Published Events

| Event | Consumers |
|-------|-----------|
| `OpeningBalanceEstablished` | Intelligence |
| `StockReceived` | Order Fulfillment (backorder), Intelligence |
| `StockReserved` | Order Fulfillment, Intelligence |
| `ReservationReleased` | Intelligence |
| `StockShipped` | Intelligence, Finance ACL |
| `StockAdjusted` | Intelligence, Finance ACL |
| `StockWrittenOff` | Intelligence, Finance ACL |
| `QuarantineHoldApplied` | Intelligence |
| `QuarantineHoldReleased` | Intelligence |
| `LowStockThresholdBreached` | Procurement, Intelligence |
| `OutOfStockDetected` | Procurement, Intelligence |
| `PromotionalStockSegregated` | Commercial Campaign, Intelligence |
| `PromotionalAllocationReleased` | Commercial Campaign, Intelligence |
| `ConsignmentOwnershipTransferred` | Intelligence, Finance ACL |

#### Subscribed Events

| Event | Source Module | Reaction |
|-------|---------------|----------|
| `PutAwayCompleted` | Inbound Receiving | `ReceiveStock` |
| `TransferDispatched` | Network Transfer | `DeductStockForTransfer` |
| `TransferReceived` | Network Transfer | `ReceiveStockFromTransfer` |
| `AdjustmentApproved` | Inventory Accuracy | `ApplyApprovedAdjustment` / `ApplyApprovedWriteOff` |
| `ReturnRestocked` | Returns Management | `ReceiveStock` |
| `ReturnQuarantined` | Returns Management | `ApplyQuarantineHold` |
| `PromotionalStockAllocated` | Commercial Campaign | `SegregatePromotionalStock` |
| `PromotionalAllocationReleased` | Commercial Campaign | `ReleasePromotionalAllocation` |

### 5. Dependencies

| Dependency | Module | Coupling Type | Purpose |

## Module Boundary Enforcement Rules

| Rule ID | Rule |
|---------|------|
| MB-01 | No module imports another module's domain entities or aggregate internals |
| MB-02 | Cross-module communication uses only published commands, queries, events, and shared identifiers |
| MB-03 | Only M-04 (Inventory Balance) mutates on-hand, reserved, or quarantined quantities |
| MB-04 | Only M-02 (Warehouse Network) mutates the location freeze flag — initiated by M-09 events |
| MB-05 | M-13 (Intelligence) subscribes to events only — no write-back to source modules |
| MB-06 | External systems integrate through ACL adapter ports — never directly into domain cores |
| MB-07 | Each module owns its persistence — no shared tables across module boundaries |
| MB-08 | Governance and Identity are consulted synchronously; state changes propagate asynchronously via events |

# Layered Architecture Design
## Inventory Management System

---

## Document Information

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Document ID** | SRS-SA-004 |
| **Document Title** | Layered Architecture Design — Inventory Management System |
| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Solution Architect |
| **Prepared For** | Development squads, technical architects, and QA leads |
| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |
| **Classification** | Internal — Architecture Confidential |
| **Scope** | Layer structure and dependency rules within each bounded-context module — no framework selection, class diagrams, or code |

### Related Documents

| Document | ID | Relationship |
|----------|-----|--------------|
| Architecture Vision | SRS-SA-001 | Strategic direction |
| Architecture Style Recommendation | SRS-SA-002 | Clean/Hexagonal + modular monolith |
| System Modules Design | SRS-SA-003 | 13 module boundaries |
| Domain Aggregates | SRS-DM-003 | Domain layer content |
| Domain Services | SRS-DM-005 | Domain and application coordination |

### Document Purpose

This document defines the **four-layer internal architecture** applied within each bounded-context module of the Inventory Management System modular monolith. It follows **Clean Architecture** (dependency rule: source code dependencies point inward) combined with **Hexagonal ports and adapters** at module boundaries.

---

## 1. Clean Architecture Overview

### 1.1 Layer Model

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        PRESENTATION LAYER                                    │
│   HTTP Controllers │ Web UI │ Mobile API │ Integration Webhooks │ DTOs      │
└──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ calls
                                   ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        APPLICATION LAYER                                     │
│   Command Handlers │ Query Handlers │ Sagas │ Event Handlers │ AuthZ Gates  │
└──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ orchestrates
                                   ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          DOMAIN LAYER                                        │
│   Aggregates │ Entities │ Value Objects │ Domain Services │ Domain Events   │
│   Repository Interfaces (ports) │ Domain Policies │ Invariants              │
└──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ implemented by
                                   ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER                                   │
│   Persistence │ Event Bus │ ACL Adapters │ Auth │ Logging │ Notifications   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

        ◄────────────── DEPENDENCY DIRECTION (inward only) ──────────────
```

### 1.2 The Dependency Rule

| Rule | Statement |
|------|-----------|
| **DR-01** | Source code dependencies must point **inward** only — from outer layers toward the domain |
| **DR-02** | Inner layers **never** reference outer layers — no domain import of controllers, ORM, or HTTP clients |
| **DR-03** | Cross-layer collaboration uses **interfaces (ports)** defined in the domain or application layer, implemented in infrastructure |
| **DR-04** | Data crosses boundaries as **plain data structures** — DTOs, commands, queries, events — never as framework types |
| **DR-05** | Frameworks and drivers are **details** relegated to the infrastructure layer |

### 1.3 Layer-to-Module Relationship

Each of the **13 bounded-context modules** (SRS-SA-003) contains its own complete four-layer stack. Layers are **replicated per module**, not shared as a single horizontal slice across the entire application.

```
ims/
├── catalog/          (M-01)  → presentation / application / domain / infrastructure
├── network/          (M-02)
├── governance/       (M-03)
├── balance/          (M-04)  → core domain — richest layer
├── procurement/      (M-05)
├── inbound/          (M-06)
├── fulfillment/      (M-07)
├── transfer/         (M-08)
├── accuracy/         (M-09)
├── returns/          (M-10)
├── campaign/         (M-11)
├── identity/         (M-12)
├── intelligence/     (M-13)  → query-heavy; thin domain, rich application + infra read models
└── shared-kernel/    → published identifiers only (ProductSku, LocationCode) — no layers
```

### 1.4 CQRS Layer Split

Command and query paths share the domain layer but diverge in application and infrastructure:

| Path | Application Layer | Infrastructure Layer |
|------|-------------------|----------------------|
| **Commands** (writes) | Command handlers, sagas, domain event dispatch | Write repositories, transactional outbox, unit of work |
| **Queries** (reads) | Query handlers | Read repositories, projections, materialized views |

Inventory Intelligence (M-13) is predominantly **query path** — minimal domain, no write command handlers.

---

## 2. Presentation Layer

### 2.1 Responsibilities

The Presentation Layer is the **outermost adapter** that translates external actor input into application-layer commands and queries, and translates application results into responses consumable by users and external systems.

| Responsibility | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| **Request reception** | Accept HTTP requests, UI actions, mobile scanner input, and integration webhook payloads |
| **Input validation (syntactic)** | Validate request shape, required fields, data types, and format — not business rules |
| **Authentication presentation** | Extract identity tokens or session credentials and pass to application layer |
| **DTO mapping** | Map HTTP/JSON/UI models to application commands and queries; map results to response DTOs |
| **Authorization presentation** | Invoke application-layer authorization gates before dispatching commands |
| **Error translation** | Map application/domain exceptions to HTTP status codes and user-safe error messages |
| **API versioning and routing** | Route requests to correct module endpoints |
| **Content negotiation** | JSON for APIs; HTML/view models for web UI; optimized payloads for mobile warehouse clients |
| **Correlation ID attachment** | Attach trace/correlation identifiers to requests for observability |

**The Presentation Layer does not:**
- Enforce business rules (BR-001 – BR-032)
- Access databases or repositories directly
- Mutate domain entities
- Publish domain events
- Contain transaction boundaries

### 2.2 Allowed Dependencies

| May Depend On | Must Not Depend On |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Application Layer (command/query dispatch) | Domain Layer (direct aggregate access) |
| Shared presentation utilities (validation attributes, base controller) | Infrastructure Layer (repositories, ORM, message bus) |
| Cross-cutting presentation middleware (auth middleware invokes application) | Other modules' domain internals |
| Published DTO / request/response contracts | Framework-specific types leaking into application |

```
Presentation ──► Application     ✅
Presentation ──► Domain          ❌
Presentation ──► Infrastructure  ❌
```

### 2.3 Typical Components

| Component | Purpose | IMS Examples |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| **REST API Controllers** | HTTP endpoint per use case group | `StockController`, `ReceiptController`, `OrderController` |
| **Web UI Controllers / Views** | Server-rendered or SPA shell pages | Dashboard views, master data forms |
| **Mobile Warehouse API Controllers** | Optimized endpoints for scanner workflows | `PickController`, `PutAwayController`, `CycleCountController` |
| **Integration Webhook Controllers** | Inbound endpoints for external systems | `SalesOrderWebhookController` (CRM ACL entry) |
| **Request DTOs** | Inbound data contracts | `ReserveStockRequest`, `VerifyReceiptRequest` |
| **Response DTOs** | Outbound data contracts | `AvailabilityResponse`, `OrderStatusResponse` |
| **Input Validators** | Syntactic validation | Required SKU, positive quantity, valid date format |
| **Exception Filters / Handlers** | Uniform error responses | `BusinessRuleViolationException` → 422; `NotFoundException` → 404 |
| **Authentication Middleware** | Token/session extraction | JWT bearer, SSO redirect |
| **API Documentation** | OpenAPI/Swagger metadata | Endpoint catalog per module |
| **Model Binders / Mappers** | DTO ↔ Command/Query translation | `ReserveStockRequest` → `ReserveStockCommand` |

### 2.4 Presentation Layer by Actor

| Actor | Presentation Entry Points |
|-------|--------------------------|
| Warehouse Staff | Mobile API — put-away, cycle count, transfer |
| Receiving Clerk | Mobile/Web API — goods receipt, discrepancy |
| Picker/Packer | Mobile API — pick verification, shipment |
| Customer Service | Web API — availability inquiry, order confirm, RMA |
| Purchasing | Web API — PO, requisition, inbound pipeline |
| Management | Web UI — dashboards (delegates to Intelligence queries) |
| Finance | Web API — invoice match, valuation export |
| System Administrator | Web UI — user and role management |
| Sales/CRM (external) | Integration webhook — order import |

---

## 3. Application Layer

### 3.1 Responsibilities

The Application Layer **orchestrates use cases** — it coordinates domain objects, enforces application-level workflow, manages transactions, and dispatches cross-module integration. It contains **no business invariants**; those belong in the domain layer.

| Responsibility | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| **Use case execution** | Receive commands/queries from presentation and execute the corresponding workflow |
| **Transaction management** | Define unit-of-work boundaries — one aggregate mutation per transaction (DR-DDD) |
| **Domain orchestration** | Load aggregates via repository ports, invoke domain methods, persist changes |
| **Authorization gates** | Verify user permission and location scope before command execution (delegates to Identity module) |
| **Saga coordination** | Manage multi-step cross-module workflows with compensation (order confirm → reserve) |
| **Domain event dispatch** | Collect domain events from aggregates and publish via event bus port |
| **Cross-module consultation** | Invoke other modules' query ports synchronously (e.g., ATP lookup, freeze check) |
| **Application services** | Coordinate operations spanning domain services or multiple ports within one use case |
| **Idempotency** | Ensure duplicate command submission does not double-apply (receipt, reservation) |
| **Audit context enrichment** | Attach user identity and correlation ID to commands before domain execution |
| **Query orchestration** | Route read requests to appropriate read repositories or cross-module query ports |
| **DTO assembly (reads)** | Compose query results from read models into response shapes |

**The Application Layer does not:**
- Implement business invariants (ATP formula, SoD, freeze rules)
- Contain SQL or ORM code
- Reference HTTP, JSON, or UI frameworks
- Own long-lived state beyond saga/process manager instances

### 3.2 Allowed Dependencies

| May Depend On | Must Not Depend On |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Domain Layer (aggregates, domain services, repository interfaces) | Infrastructure Layer (concrete implementations) |
| Application contracts (commands, queries, handler interfaces) | Presentation Layer |
| Cross-module **query ports** (interfaces only) | Other modules' aggregate internals |
| Shared kernel identifiers (`ProductSku`, `LocationCode`) | ORM entities, HTTP clients, framework types |

```
Application ──► Domain              ✅
Application ──► Infrastructure      ❌  (depends on ports defined in domain/application)
Application ──► Presentation        ❌
```

**Dependency inversion:** Application layer defines or uses **interfaces (ports)** that infrastructure implements:

| Port Type | Defined In | Implemented In |
|-----------|------------|----------------|
| `IStockPositionRepository` | Domain | Infrastructure |
| `IEventBus` | Application | Infrastructure |
| `IUnitOfWork` | Application | Infrastructure |
| `IAvailabilityQueryPort` | Application (fulfillment module) | Infrastructure or Balance module adapter |
| `IIdentityService` | Application | Infrastructure (Identity module adapter) |

### 3.3 Typical Components

| Component | Purpose | IMS Examples |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| **Commands** | Immutable write intent records | `ReserveStockCommand`, `ConfirmPutAwayCommand`, `ApproveAdjustmentCommand` |
| **Queries** | Immutable read intent records | `GetAvailabilityQuery`, `GetStockPositionQuery`, `SearchAuditTrailQuery` |
| **Command Handlers** | One handler per command — executes use case | `ReserveStockCommandHandler`, `VerifyGoodsReceiptCommandHandler` |
| **Query Handlers** | One handler per query — returns read data | `GetAvailabilityQueryHandler`, `GetDashboardQueryHandler` |
| **Saga / Process Managers** | Multi-step cross-module workflows | `OrderConfirmationSaga`, `OpeningBalanceGoLiveSaga` |
| **Saga Steps** | Individual saga activities with compensation | `ReserveStockStep`, `CompensateOrderConfirmationStep` |
| **Domain Event Handlers** | React to events from other modules | `OnPutAwayCompletedHandler` (Balance module) |
| **Application Services** | Coordinate when logic is not natural on one aggregate | `AvailabilityConfirmationService`, `TransferCapacityEvaluationService` |
| **Authorization Behaviors** | Pre-handler permission checks | `RequirePermissionBehavior`, `LocationScopeBehavior` |
| **Validation Behaviors** | Application-level validation (not domain) | Command field presence, saga preconditions |
| **Unit of Work** | Transaction boundary abstraction | `IUnitOfWork.Begin()`, `Commit()`, `Rollback()` |
| **Command Bus / Dispatcher** | Route commands to handlers | Mediator-style dispatch |
| **Query Bus / Dispatcher** | Route queries to handlers | CQRS query dispatch |
| **Integration Command Adapters** | Translate external commands to internal | `ImportSalesOrderCommandHandler` |
| **Read Model Assemblers** | Compose complex query responses | `DashboardAssembler`, `KpiReportAssembler` |

### 3.4 Application Layer Patterns by Module

| Module | Notable Application Components |
|--------|-------------------------------|
| M-04 Inventory Balance | `ReserveStockCommandHandler`, `ReceiveStockCommandHandler`; contention-sensitive handlers |
| M-07 Order Fulfillment | `OrderConfirmationSaga`, `FulfillBackorderCommandHandler` |
| M-06 Inbound Receiving | `ConfirmPutAwayCommandHandler` → publishes `PutAwayCompleted` |
| M-09 Inventory Accuracy | `ApproveAdjustmentCommandHandler` → publishes `AdjustmentApproved` |
| M-13 Intelligence | Query handlers only — `GetDashboardQueryHandler`, `ExportAuditEvidenceQueryHandler` |

### 3.5 Command Handler Flow (Reference)

```
Controller
    │
    ▼
CommandBus.Dispatch(ReserveStockCommand)
    │
    ▼
AuthorizationBehavior          ──► IIdentityService.AuthorizeAction()
    │
    ▼
ReserveStockCommandHandler
    │
    ├──► IStockPositionRepository.GetBySkuAndLocation()
    ├──► StockPosition.Reserve(quantity)     [Domain Layer]
    ├──► IStockPositionRepository.Save()
    ├──► IUnitOfWork.Commit()
    └──► IEventBus.Publish(StockReserved)    [Infrastructure port]
```

---

## 4. Domain Layer

### 4.1 Responsibilities

The Domain Layer is the **center of the architecture** — it contains the business logic, rules, and models that represent the inventory management problem space. It is **framework-agnostic** and **persistence-ignorant**.

| Responsibility | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| **Aggregate roots** | Enforce consistency boundaries and transactional invariants |
| **Entities** | Objects with identity and lifecycle within aggregates |
| **Value objects** | Immutable, identity-less concepts (Quantity, Money, ReasonCode) |
| **Domain invariants** | Enforce business rules at aggregate boundaries (BR-001 – BR-032) |
| **Domain events** | Record meaningful business facts in past tense (`StockReserved`, `PutAwayCompleted`) |
| **Domain services** | Stateless operations spanning concepts not natural on one entity |
| **Domain policies** | Encapsulate decision rules (FEFO lot selection, freeze guard evaluation) |
| **Repository interfaces** | Define persistence contracts — no implementation |
| **Factory methods** | Controlled aggregate creation with invariant validation |
| **Ubiquitous language** | Naming aligned to SRS-DM-008 terms |

**The Domain Layer does not:**
- Know about databases, HTTP, UI, or message brokers
- Depend on application or infrastructure layers
- Perform I/O of any kind
- Reference other modules' aggregates directly — only shared identifiers

### 4.2 Allowed Dependencies

| May Depend On | Must Not Depend On |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Other domain types within the **same module** | Application Layer |
| Shared kernel value types (`ProductSku`, `LocationCode`, `UserId`) | Infrastructure Layer |
| Domain interfaces (repository ports) defined in same module | Presentation Layer |
| Standard language primitives and approved domain libraries (none required) | ORM attributes, HTTP attributes, logging frameworks |
| | Other modules' domain aggregates or entities |

```
Domain ──► Shared Kernel identifiers    ✅
Domain ──► Application                  ❌
Domain ──► Infrastructure               ❌
Domain ──► Presentation                 ❌
Domain ──► Other module domain          ❌
```

**Cross-module domain interaction** uses only:
- **Identity references** (`ProductSku`, not `Product` entity)
- **Domain events** consumed by application-layer handlers in other modules
- **Query ports** (interfaces) for read-only consultation — interface may be defined in calling module's domain or a shared contracts package; implementation in infrastructure

### 4.3 Typical Components

| Component | Purpose | IMS Examples |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| **Aggregate Roots** | Consistency and mutation entry points | `StockPosition`, `GoodsReceipt`, `CustomerOrder`, `GovernancePolicy` |
| **Entities** | Identified objects within aggregates | `LotBatch`, `QuarantineHold`, `InventoryReservation`, `PutAway` |
| **Value Objects** | Immutable domain concepts | `Quantity`, `ProductSku`, `LocationCode`, `AtpBreakdown`, `ReasonCode`, `ApprovalThreshold` |
| **Domain Events** | Past-tense business facts | `StockReserved`, `PutAwayCompleted`, `AdjustmentApproved`, `LocationFreezeApplied` |
| **Domain Services** | Cross-aggregate logic within module | `FefoLotSelectionService`, `AtpCalculationService` |
| **Domain Policies** | Reusable rule evaluators | `SafetyStockPolicy`, `ProductEligibilityPolicy`, `SegregationOfDutiesPolicy` |
| **Repository Interfaces** | Persistence ports | `IStockPositionRepository`, `IGoodsReceiptRepository`, `IProductRepository` |
| **Specification Objects** | Composable query predicates (domain language) | `ActiveProductSpecification`, `FrozenLocationSpecification` |
| **Domain Exceptions** | Business rule violations | `InsufficientAtpException`, `LocationFrozenException`, `SegregationOfDutiesViolationException` |
| **Enumerations / Status Types** | Lifecycle states as domain concepts | `ProductLifecycleStatus`, `TransferStatus`, `AdjustmentCaseStatus` |
| **Aggregate Factories** | Controlled creation | `StockPosition.CreateOpeningBalance()`, `GoodsReceipt.CreateFromPurchaseOrder()` |

### 4.4 Domain Layer Richness by Module

| Module | Domain Complexity | Key Aggregates / Concepts |
|--------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| M-04 Inventory Balance | **Highest (core domain)** | `StockPosition` invariants: ATP = on-hand − reserved − quarantined |
| M-07 Order Fulfillment | High | `CustomerOrder` lifecycle: confirm → reserve → pick → ship |
| M-06 Inbound Receiving | High | `GoodsReceipt` — verify → discrepancy → put-away chain |
| M-09 Inventory Accuracy | High | `AdjustmentCase` state machine: variance → investigate → approve |
| M-03 Inventory Governance | Medium | `GovernancePolicy` versioning, reason code lifecycle |
| M-01 Product Catalog | Medium | `Product` lifecycle and eligibility |
| M-13 Intelligence | **Minimal** | No write aggregates; optional read value types only |

### 4.5 Aggregate Design Rules in Domain Layer

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| DL-01 | All state changes go through aggregate root public methods |
| DL-02 | One transaction modifies one aggregate |
| DL-03 | External references hold identity only — `ProductSku`, not `Product` |
| DL-04 | Domain events raised inside aggregate before persistence |
| DL-05 | Repository interfaces return aggregate roots — not ORM entities |
| DL-06 | Value objects are immutable — replacement, not mutation |
| DL-07 | Domain layer never queries other modules — consultation via ports at application layer |

---

## 5. Infrastructure Layer

### 5.1 Responsibilities

The Infrastructure Layer provides **technical capabilities** — the concrete implementations of ports defined by inner layers. It is the **outermost implementation detail**, swappable without changing business logic.

| Responsibility | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| **Persistence** | Implement repository interfaces — ORM mappings, SQL, aggregate hydration and persistence |
| **Event bus** | Publish and subscribe to domain events — in-process bus (MVP) or message broker (future) |
| **Transactional outbox** | Ensure reliable event delivery with database commits |
| **Unit of work** | Manage database transactions and connection lifecycle |
| **ACL adapters** | Translate external system models to/from application commands (Sales/CRM, Finance ERP) |
| **Authentication adapter** | Integrate enterprise IdP (SSO), validate tokens, resolve `UserId` |
| **Authorization adapter** | Implement Identity module query ports for other modules |
| **Cross-module adapters** | Implement query/command ports between modules within the monolith |
| **Read model projections** | Maintain CQRS read stores for Intelligence module |
| **Caching** | ATP hot-path cache with invalidation on balance events |
| **Logging and audit** | Structured logging, audit record persistence |
| **Monitoring** | Metrics, health checks, distributed tracing hooks |
| **Notification delivery** | Email/SMS gateway for operational alerts |
| **Background jobs** | Scheduled tasks — reservation expiry, KPI rollups, backup verification |
| **File import/export** | Bulk product/stock import (FR-090), audit evidence export |
| **Clock / ID generation** | Injectable time source and unique ID generation for testability |

**The Infrastructure Layer does not:**
- Contain business rules or invariants
- Be referenced directly by presentation layer
- Leak ORM entities into domain or application layers

### 5.2 Allowed Dependencies

| May Depend On | Must Not Depend On |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Domain Layer (implement repository interfaces) | Presentation Layer |
| Application Layer (implement ports, event handlers wiring) | — |
| Infrastructure frameworks (ORM, HTTP clients, message brokers) | Domain aggregate internals (only through repository interfaces) |
| Other modules' **public query ports** (adapter implementations) | Other modules' private infrastructure |
| Shared kernel types | — |

```
Infrastructure ──► Domain         ✅  (implements interfaces)
Infrastructure ──► Application     ✅  (implements ports, wires handlers)
Infrastructure ──► Presentation    ❌
```

### 5.3 Typical Components

| Component | Purpose | IMS Examples |
|-----------|---------|--------------|
| **Repository Implementations** | Aggregate persistence | `StockPositionRepository`, `GoodsReceiptRepository`, `ProductRepository` |
| **ORM Entity Mappings** | Database row ↔ aggregate mapping | `StockPositionConfiguration`, `GoodsReceiptConfiguration` |
| **Unit of Work Implementation** | Transaction scope | `EfUnitOfWork`, `DbContext` wrapper |
| **In-Process Event Bus** | MVP domain event dispatch | `InProcessEventBus`, `DomainEventDispatcher` |
| **Transactional Outbox** | Reliable event publish | `OutboxMessage`, `OutboxProcessor` |
| **Event Handlers (wiring)** | Register handlers with bus | `EventHandlerRegistry`, module startup configuration |
| **Cross-Module Adapters** | Inter-module port implementations | `BalanceAvailabilityQueryAdapter` (fulfillment → balance) |
| **ACL Adapters (external)** | External system translation | `SalesCrmOrderAdapter`, `FinanceErpValuationAdapter` |
| **Identity Provider Adapter** | SSO integration | `EntraIdAuthenticationAdapter`, `JwtTokenValidator` |
| **Read Model Repositories** | CQRS query stores | `MovementHistoryReadRepository`, `DashboardReadRepository` |
| **Projection Handlers** | Update read models on events | `OnStockReservedProjectionHandler` |
| **Cache Providers** | Performance optimization | `AtpCacheService` with event-driven invalidation |
| **Logging Adapter** | Structured audit logging | `SerilogAuditLogger`, `AuditTrailWriter` |
| **Notification Adapter** | Alert delivery | `EmailNotificationGateway` (SVC-02) |
| **Import/Export Adapters** | Bulk data operations | `ProductStockBulkImporter`, `AuditEvidenceExporter` |
| **Background Job Scheduler** | Async processing | `ReservationExpiryJob`, `KpiRollupJob` |
| **Health Check Implementations** | Ops monitoring | `DatabaseHealthCheck`, `EventBusHealthCheck` |
| **Migration Scripts** | Schema versioning | Per-module database migrations |

### 5.4 Infrastructure by Concern

| Concern | Components | NFR Alignment |
|---------|------------|---------------|
| **Write persistence** | Repositories, UoW, outbox | NFR-REL-006 (integrity), NFR-BDR-001 (RPO) |
| **Read persistence** | Read repositories, projections | NFR-PERF-002 (ATP), NFR-PERF-004 (dashboards) |
| **Security** | Auth adapter, encryption | NFR-SEC-001 – NFR-SEC-032 |
| **Observability** | Logging, metrics, tracing | NFR-LOG, NFR-MON |
| **Integration** | ACL adapters | TEC-04, TEC-05, HS-014 |
| **Resilience** | Outbox, retry, idempotency store | NFR-REL-011 – NFR-REL-014 |

### 5.5 Cross-Module Infrastructure Pattern

Cross-module integration within the monolith uses **infrastructure adapters** implementing application-layer ports:

```
┌─────────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ Fulfillment Module  │         │ Balance Module               │
│  Application Layer  │         │  Application Layer           │
│  IAtpQueryPort ◄────┼─────────┼── BalanceAtpQueryAdapter     │
│                     │         │       (Infrastructure)       │
└─────────────────────┘         └──────────────────────────────┘
```

The port interface (`IAtpQueryPort`) is defined in the **calling module's application layer**. The adapter is implemented in **infrastructure** and may live in either module's infrastructure package, registered at application composition root.

---

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns Placement

| Concern | Primary Layer | Notes |
|---------|---------------|-------|
| Business rules (BR-xxx) | **Domain** | Never in presentation or infrastructure |
| Use case orchestration | **Application** | Handlers and sagas |
| Syntactic input validation | **Presentation** | Format, required fields |
| Permission checks | **Application** | Via `IIdentityService` port before handler |
| Authentication | **Infrastructure** (adapter) + **Presentation** (middleware) | Token validation in infra; extraction in presentation |
| Transaction boundaries | **Application** | `IUnitOfWork` port |
| Audit trail recording | **Infrastructure** (persistence) | Triggered by domain events → Intelligence projections |
| API rate limiting | **Presentation** or **Infrastructure** | Edge concern |
| Correlation / tracing | **Presentation** (attach) + **Infrastructure** (propagate) | |
| Idempotency | **Application** (logic) + **Infrastructure** (store) | |
| Caching | **Infrastructure** | ATP cache with domain-event invalidation |
| Exception mapping | **Presentation** | HTTP status from domain exception types |

---

## 7. Dependency Matrix (Complete)

| Layer | Presentation | Application | Domain | Infrastructure |
|-------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Presentation** | — | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Application** | ❌ | internal | ✅ | ❌ (ports only) |
| **Domain** | ❌ | ❌ | internal | ❌ (interfaces only) |
| **Infrastructure** | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | internal |

---

## 8. Request Lifecycle (End-to-End)

### 8.1 Write Path — Confirm Customer Order

```
1. [Presentation]  OrderController.ConfirmOrder(ConfirmOrderRequest dto)
                      → maps to ConfirmCustomerOrderCommand
2. [Application]     AuthorizationBehavior checks permission
3. [Application]     ConfirmCustomerOrderCommandHandler
                      → starts OrderConfirmationSaga
4. [Application]     Saga step: CustomerOrder.Confirm()          [Domain]
5. [Infrastructure]  CustomerOrderRepository.Save()
6. [Application]     Saga step: ReserveStockCommand → Balance module port
7. [Application]     ReserveStockCommandHandler (Balance module)
                      → StockPosition.Reserve()                   [Domain]
8. [Infrastructure]  StockPositionRepository.Save()
                      → UnitOfWork.Commit()
                      → Outbox.Publish(StockReserved)
9. [Infrastructure]  EventBus dispatches StockReserved
10.[Application]     Fulfillment saga resumes on StockReserved event
11.[Presentation]    OrderController returns ConfirmOrderResponse
```

### 8.2 Read Path — ATP Lookup

```
1. [Presentation]  StockController.GetAvailability(sku, location)
                      → maps to GetAvailabilityQuery
2. [Application]     GetAvailabilityQueryHandler
3. [Infrastructure]  AtpReadRepository (or cache) returns projection
4. [Presentation]    Maps to AvailabilityResponse DTO
```

*Read path bypasses domain aggregate load for performance (CQRS) — NFR-PERF-002.*

---

## 9. Layer Implementation Standards

| Standard ID | Rule |
|-------------|------|
| LS-01 | Every module packages layers as `ModuleName.Presentation`, `.Application`, `.Domain`, `.Infrastructure` |
| LS-02 | Domain project has **zero** references to outer layer projects |
| LS-03 | Application project references Domain only — infrastructure wired at composition root |
| LS-04 | Repository interfaces live in Domain; implementations live in Infrastructure |
| LS-05 | Commands and queries are immutable records in Application layer |
| LS-06 | One command handler per command; handlers are stateless |
| LS-07 | Domain events are raised inside aggregates, collected by application layer after save |
| LS-08 | Cross-module calls use ports — never `using OtherModule.Domain` |
| LS-09 | Intelligence module has no command handlers for transactional writes |
| LS-10 | Integration tests target Application + Infrastructure with in-memory or test database adapters |

# Integration Architecture Design
## Inventory Management System

| **Version** | 1.0 |
| **Status** | Draft |
| **Document Owner** | Solution Architect |

| **Date** | July 6, 2026 |

### Related Documents

| Document | ID | Relationship |
|----------|-----|--------------|
| Architecture Vision | SRS-SA-001 | Event-driven direction, ACL principles |

### Document Purpose

This document defines **how the Inventory Management System integrates internally across its 13 modules and externally with enterprise systems and partners**. It establishes communication styles, synchronous versus asynchronous rules, and hard integration boundaries — so that quantity integrity, auditability, and phased delivery are preserved as integrations grow in complexity.

---

## 1. Integration Architecture Overview

### 1.1 Design Principles

| Principle | Statement |
|-----------|-----------|
| **IB-01 — Inventory Balance is the quantity authority** | No module other than Inventory Balance (M-04) mutates on-hand, reserved, or quarantined quantities |
| **IB-02 — Events for state propagation** | Cross-module state changes propagate through domain events, not shared mutable data |
| **IB-03 — Queries for read-only consultation** | Synchronous cross-module calls are permitted only for read-only lookups and pre-condition checks |
| **IB-04 — ACL at system boundary** | External models are translated at the boundary; foreign concepts never enter the domain layer |
| **IB-05 — Published language for identifiers** | Cross-boundary references use shared value identifiers (`ProductSku`, `LocationCode`) — not entity references |
| **IB-06 — Fail closed on integration uncertainty** | When ATP, freeze, or authorization cannot be confirmed, the operation is rejected — not guessed |
| **IB-07 — Idempotent integration handlers** | Duplicate event or command delivery must not double-apply stock mutations |
| **IB-08 — Observable integration flows** | Every cross-module and external exchange is traceable via correlation ID in audit and movement history |

### 1.2 Integration Topology

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           EXTERNAL INTEGRATION ZONE                              │
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │
│  │ Sales /  │ │ Finance  │ │  Sales   │ │Marketing │ │    HR    │ │ Customs  │ │
│  │   CRM    │ │   ERP    │ │ Channel  │ │ Campaign │ │ Directory│ │ Regulatory│ │
│  └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ └────┬─────┘ │
│       │  ACL       │  ACL       │  ACL       │  ACL       │  ACL       │  ACL    │
└───────┼────────────┼────────────┼────────────┼────────────┼────────────┼────────┘
        │            │            │            │            │            │
┌───────▼────────────▼────────────▼────────────▼────────────▼────────────▼────────┐
│                        IMS MODULAR MONOLITH BOUNDARY                             │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │                     PRESENTATION / API GATEWAY LAYER                         │ │
│  └──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                     │                                            │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐ │ ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  │
│  │  Fulfillment │  │  Inbound     │ │ │  Procurement │  │    Campaign      │  │
│  │    M-07      │  │    M-06      │ │ │     M-05     │  │      M-11        │  │
│  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘ │ └──────┬───────┘  └────────┬─────────┘  │
│         │    sync query   │         │         │                   │             │
│         │    + saga       │ events  │         │                   │ events      │
│         ▼                 ▼         ▼         ▼                   ▼             │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │              INVENTORY BALANCE (M-04) — Core Integration Hub             │  │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│         ▲                 ▲                   ▲                   ▲             │
│  ┌──────┴───────┐  ┌──────┴───────┐  ┌──────┴───────┐  ┌──────┴─────────┐   │
│  │   Transfer   │  │   Accuracy   │  │   Returns    │  │    Network     │   │
│  │     M-08     │  │     M-09     │  │     M-10     │  │      M-02      │   │
```
